CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

addedLines: - caveman:cavecrew-builder: Surgical 1-2 file edit. Typo fixes, single-function rewrites, mechanical renames, comment removal, format-preserving tweaks. Hard refuses 3+ file scope. Returns caveman diff receipt. Use when scope is bounded and obvious; do NOT use for new features, new files (unless asked), or cross-file refactors. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob)

- caveman:cavecrew-investigator: Read-only code locator. Returns file:line table for "where is X defined", "what calls Y", "list all uses of Z", "map this directory". Output is caveman-compressed so the main thread eats ~60% fewer tokens than vanilla Explore. Refuses to suggest fixes. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- caveman:cavecrew-reviewer: Diff/branch/file reviewer. One line per finding, severity-tagged, no praise, no scope creep. Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning. (Tools: Read, Grep, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Railway MCP server. Manage your Railway projects, services, deployments, and more.

- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. I have a full picture. Here's the map.

## 1. Layout types

| Type | File:line | Kind | Conformances | Stored properties |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SplitOrientation` | `WorkroomApp/Models/PaneLayout.swift:25` | enum | `Equatable` | `.horizontal` / `.vertical` |
| `PaneEdge` | `Models/PaneLayout.swift:32` | enum | — | `.top/.right/.bottom/.left`; derives `orientation`, `placesDroppedFirst` |
| `PaneDirection` | `Models/PaneLayout.swift:41` | enum | — | `.left/.right/.up/.down` (focus movement) |
| `PaneRatio` | `Models/PaneLayout.swift:45` | enum (namespace) | — | `sanitize(_:)` clamps to (0.001, 0.999) |
| **`PaneLayout<Leaf: Hashable>`** | `Models/PaneLayout.swift:51` | `indirect enum`, value type | `Equatable`. **NOT Codable, NOT Identifiable, NOT Observable** | `.leaf(Leaf)` \| `.split(id: UUID, orientation: SplitOrientation, ratio: CGFloat, first:, second:)` |
| `TerminalPaneLayout` | `Models/PaneLayout.swift:203` | typealias | — | `= PaneLayout<TerminalTab.ID>` (i.e. `PaneLayout<UUID>`) |
| **`TerminalTab`** | `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:14` | **struct** (value type, deliberately) | `Identifiable` only. **NOT Codable, NOT Hashable, NOT Equatable** | `let id = UUID()` (freshly minted, no custom init), `var content: TabContent`, `var diffViewModeOverride: DiffViewMode?`, `var markdownPreviewOverride: Bool?` |
| **`TerminalSessions`** | `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:249` | `@MainActor final class` | `ObservableObject` (Combine `@Published`, not `@Observable`) | see below |
| `TerminalState` | `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:215` | struct | none | `let view: GhosttySurfaceView`, `let defaultTitle: String`, `var liveTitle/cwd: String?`, `var progressActive: Bool?` — **holds a live AppKit view, non-serializable** |
| `TerminalTarget` | `Core/Models.swift:89` | struct | `Identifiable, Hashable` | `let id: String` (`"wr\|<project>\|<name>"` / `"root\|<project>"`), `title`, `path`, `isMissing`; id builders at `:98-99` |
| `SidebarID` | `Core/AppStore.swift:10` | enum | `Hashable`. **NOT Codable** | `.project(String)` \| `.root(project:)` \| `.workroom(project:, name:)` |
| `AppStore` | `Core/AppStore.swift:86` | `@MainActor final class` | `ObservableObject` | one per **window**; owns `terminals` (`:609`), `workroomSplits` (`:265`) |
| `ProjectStore` | `Core/ProjectStore.swift:15` | `@MainActor final class` | `ObservableObject` | app-wide singleton `.shared`; project list only, no pane state |
| `WindowRegistry` | `Core/WindowRegistry.swift:22` | `@MainActor final class` | `ObservableObject` | `.shared`; holds only **weak** window↔store `Entry` pairs, `keyStore` (`:117`), `lastActiveStore` (`:41`) |
| `WindowSeed` | `WorkroomApp.swift:86` | struct | **`Codable, Hashable`** | `let id: UUID`, `let restore: Bool` — the SwiftUI `WindowGroup(for:)` scene value |
| `WindowToken` | `Core/SwitcherRecency.swift:13` | struct | `Hashable` | per-window identity for switcher recency (never reused) |

`TerminalSessions` stored state (all `@Published private`, `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:251-263`) — **this is the whole in-memory pane model per window**:

```swift
tabsByTarget:      [TerminalTarget.ID: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTab]]   // :251
orderByTarget:     [TerminalTarget.ID: [TerminalTab.ID]]               // :254  loose strip order
splitByTarget:     [TerminalTarget.ID: TerminalPaneLayout]             // :256  ≤1 split per target
focusedTabByTarget:[TerminalTarget.ID: TerminalTab.ID]                 // :258
activityPulses:    [TerminalTab.ID: Int]                               // :262  transient
counts:            [TerminalTarget.ID: Int]                            // :264  "Terminal N" numbering
```

Two levels of splitting exist, both instantiations of the same generic tree:
- **Terminal split** — `PaneLayout<TerminalTab.ID>`, at most **one per target**, in `splitByTarget`. Solo tabs live alongside; the split renders only when the focused tab is a member (`isSplitVisible`, `:439`).
- **Workroom split** — `PaneLayout<SidebarID>`, **many disjoint groups per window**, in `AppStore.workroomSplits: [PaneLayout<SidebarID>]` (`Core/AppStore.swift:265`). At most one visible: the group holding `selectedTargetID`.

## 2. Pane content kinds

`TabContent` — `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:101`, a plain enum (no Codable/Equatable), 4 closed cases:

| Case | Payload type | File:line | Payload fields | Serializable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.terminal` | `TerminalState` | `TerminalSessions.swift:215` | live `GhosttySurfaceView` + `defaultTitle`, `liveTitle`, `cwd`, `progressActive` | **No** — owns an AppKit/Metal surface. Respawn inputs would be `lastKnownCwd` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:97`) + optional `command` (`init` at `:156`) |
| `.diff` | `DiffDescriptor` | `Core/DiffDescriptor.swift:25` | `var path: String`, `var change: ChangedFile.Change`, `var source: DiffSource`, `var isPreview: Bool` | `Equatable, Hashable, Sendable` — pure value, trivially Codable-able |
| `.file` | `FileDescriptor` | `Core/FileTree.swift:15` | `var path: String`, `var isPreview: Bool` | same |
| `.changeset` | `ChangesetDescriptor` | `Core/ChangesetDescriptor.swift:7` | `var commitID: String`, `var title: String`, `var isPreview: Bool`, `var selectedPath: String?` | same |

Discriminating protocol: **`ContentDescriptor`** — `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:202` (`isPreview` get/set, `makeTabContent()`, `matches(_:)`). The three non-terminal descriptors conform (`DiffDescriptor.swift:42`, `FileTree.swift:28`, `ChangesetDescriptor.swift:27`). One generic opener pair drives all three.

Supporting enums: `DiffSource` (`DiffDescriptor.swift:14`) — `.gitWorktree / .jjWorkingCopy / .jjParent / .commit(String)`, `Hashable, Sendable`. `ChangedFile.Change` (`Core/WorkroomStatus.swift:97`) — `String`-raw enum. `DiffViewMode` (`Core/DiffViewMode.swift:12`) — already `Defaults.Serializable`.

Two identity reductions of `TabContent` already exist and are the natural persistence seams:
- `FocusedTabSelection` — `Core/FocusedTabSelection.swift:18`, `Equatable`, cases `.changeset(commitID:)`, `.diff(path:source:)`, `.file(path:)`; built by `init?(content:)` at `TerminalSessions.swift:188`.
- `NavPayload` — `Core/NavigationHistory.swift:53`, `Sendable`, wraps the three descriptors whole; bridge `init?(_ content: TabContent)` at `TerminalSessions.swift:138`, `makeTabContent(isPreview:)` at `:157`. **This is already "the replay data for a content pane"** — an existing three-case, terminal-excluded projection.

**Terminal split / tabs — `Core/TerminalSessions.swift`:**

| Op | Function | Line |

| create first tab on pane mount | `ensureTab(for:)` | 458 |
| new terminal tab (⌘T) | `addTab(for:)` | 464 |
| open content preview (generic) | `openContentPreview<D: ContentDescriptor>` | 498 |
| open content persisted | `openContentPersistent` | 533 |
| pin preview → persisted | `persist(_:for:)` | 576 |
| per-tab diff mode / md preview | `setDiffViewMode` 614, `setMarkdownPreview` 667 | |
| changeset file selection | `setChangesetSelectedPath` | 626 |
| replay content into a specific tab | `setContent(_:forTab:in:)` | 687 |
| run tab | `addRunTab` 733, `respawnRunTab` 757, `makeRunTab` 798 | |
| **split** (⌘D/⇧⌘D) | `splitFocusedPane(for:orientation:)` 810 → `splitFocusedPane(for:edge:)` **819** | |
| what the new pane is | `newPaneTab(splitting:for:)` | 852 |
| split a named tab (toolbar/menu) | `splitTab(_:on:for:)` | 877 |
| **drag-to-split / rearrange** | `moveTabIntoSplit(_:ontoEdge:of:for:)` | 892 |
| pop pane out of split | `extractFromSplit(_:for:)` | 936 |
| **focus** (single chokepoint) | `focus(_:for:)` 949, `select(_:for:)` 964, `private setFocused` **974** | |
| keyboard pane focus (⌃⌘arrows) | `focusAdjacentPane(_:for:)` | 985 |
| **reorder** strip | `moveTab(_:toIndex:for:)` | 996 |
| divider drag | `setRatio(_:forSplit:for:)` | 1006 |
| equalize (#83) | `equalizeSplit(for:)` | 1013 |
| **close** | `closeTab(_:for:)` | 1020 |
| tear down a whole target | `reap(_:)` 1047, `reapAll()` 1062 | |
| display order normalisation | `displayedTabIDs(for:)` | 368 |
| GPU occlusion reconcile | `reconcileOcclusion(for:)` | 1089 |
| private helpers | `insert` 1259, `insertID` 1264, `makeTerminalTab` **1277**, `closeSuccessor` 1249, `teardown` 1336 | |

Pure tree transforms (all in `Models/PaneLayout.swift`): `inserting` 91, `removingLeaf` 120, `replacingLeaf` 140, `settingRatio` 154, `equalized` 188; queries `tabIDs` 59, `firstTabID` 69, `contains` 71, `containsSplit` 76, `leafCount` 172.

**Workroom split — `Core/AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift`:** `workroomSplit(containing:)` 18, `visibleWorkroomSplit` 32, `resolvedSplitLeaves` 39/48, `visibleWorkroomLayout(for:)` 74, `displayedWorkroomTargets()` 91, `workroomSplitGroupIndices()` 127, `focusWorkroomMember` 139, `insertWorkroomSplit(_:beside:edge:)` **149**, `detachFromSplitGroup` 178, `removeWorkroomSplitMember` 192, `autoCloseEmptiedSplitMember` 210, `selectFallbackWorkroom` 242, `setWorkroomSplitRatio` 260, `equalizeWorkroomSplit` 273, **`pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves(formerSelection:)` 297** (self-healing against dead workrooms — the model tolerates stale leaves).

**Store-level entry points — `Core/AppStore.swift`:** `openDiffPreview/Persistent` 3505/3514, `openFilePreview/Persistent` 3523/3530, `openChangesetPreview/Persistent` 3538/3546, `selectChangesetFile` 3563, `splitFocusedRight/Down/Left/Up` 3663-3681, `equalizeFocusedSplit` 3685, `focusPane` 3693, `ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` **2280**, `armAutoRun` 2262.

**View call sites:** `Views/PaneTreeView.swift:71` (ratio), `:142` (drop-into-split), `:145` (extract); `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:199, 310, 316, 417, 928-957`; `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:99` (`ensureInitialTerminal`), `:138 contentLayout`; renderer math `PaneTreeLayout` at `Views/PaneTreeView.swift:172` (`plan` 232, `dropTarget` 277, `adjacentPane` 296).

## 4. Window ↔ project/workroom selection

- **One `AppStore` per window.** `WindowGroup(for: WindowSeed.self)` at `WorkroomApp.swift:58`; `RootWindow` (`:97`) constructs the `@StateObject AppStore` in its `init` (`:101-111`) and calls `store.bootstrap(restore: seed.restore)` (`:127`). Deliberate — sidesteps the `@StateObject`-in-`WindowGroup` sharing bug.
- **Selection state lives on `AppStore`:** `selectedProjectID: Project.ID?` (`AppStore.swift:156`) and **`selectedTargetID: SidebarID?`** (`:161`) with a large `didSet` (persists to `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]`, records switcher recency, records nav history, refreshes status). Derived: `selectedTarget` `:1045`, `selectedWorkroom` `:1126`, `target(for:)` `:1110`.
- The **focused workroom-split member IS `selectedTargetID`** (no separate field).
- **Restore today is selection-only, one window:** `ProjectStore.consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`) returns `true` exactly once; `AppStore.bootstrap(restore:)` (`:2306`) drops `pendingRestoreSelection` for every other window. Resolution: `validatedSelection` `:2571`, `sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)` `:4171`, `targetIDString(for:)` `:4253`.

**Structural obstacles to expect:** `TerminalTab.ID` is `let id = UUID()` (`TerminalSessions.swift:15`) — split trees, focus, run state, navigation history and notification routing all key on it, so ids must either be persisted alongside the trees or remapped consistently on restore; `DiffSource`/the descriptors are `Hashable, Sendable` but **not** `Codable`; `PaneLayout` is an `indirect enum` with a `UUID` per split node, also not `Codable`; and `window.isRestorable = false` plus the one-shot `consumeInitialRestore()` mean multi-window restore needs a deliberate design decision, not just a serializer.
Explored. Now design.

---

# Issue #46 — Persist open panels (terminals, diffs) and layouts across restarts

## Design premise

One new `Defaults` key holding one `Codable` snapshot, written by the last-active window and read by the one launch window that already wins `ProjectStore.consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`). Restored terminals are **fresh shells in the remembered cwd** — no scrollback, no process resume. Zero changes to the pane model's semantics; `PaneLayout` gains only a `Codable` conformance and one pure transform.

---

## 1. What gets persisted, and what is deliberately dropped

### Persisted (per target, keyed by `TerminalTarget.ID` string)
| Thing | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tab list **in strip order** | `TerminalSessions.displayedTabIDs(for:)` (`TerminalSessions.swift:368`) | The snapshot array **is** the order — no separate order field to desync. Feeding the displayed order back as the loose `orderByTarget` reproduces the same display, because normalisation is idempotent when the split's members are already a contiguous run in tree order. |
| Terminal tab payload | `cwd` = `surface.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path`; `title` = `TerminalState.defaultTitle` | `defaultTitle` is the stable "Terminal N"; `liveTitle` is not persisted. |
| Diff tab payload | `DiffDescriptor` (`DiffDescriptor.swift:25`) — `path`, `change.rawValue`, `source`, `isPreview` | |
| File tab payload | `FileDescriptor` (`FileTree.swift:15`) — `path`, `isPreview` | |
| Changeset tab payload | `ChangesetDescriptor` (`ChangesetDescriptor.swift:7`) — `commitID`, `title`, `isPreview`, `selectedPath` | |
| Per-tab overrides | `diffViewModeOverride`, `markdownPreviewOverride` (`TerminalSessions.swift:22`, `:28`) | Cheap, and their loss is a visible "it forgot". |
| Split tree | `splitByTarget` (`TerminalSessions.swift:256`) | |
| Focused tab | `focusedTabByTarget` (`TerminalSessions.swift:258`) | |
| `counts` (the "Terminal N" counter) | `TerminalSessions.swift:264` | Without it, the next ⌘T after restoring "Terminal 1–3" is another "Terminal 1". |

### Persisted (per window, in the same snapshot)
- `AppStore.workroomSplits` (`AppStore.swift:265`) as `[PaneLayout<String>]` of target-id strings.
- `AppStore.expandedTerminalTargets` (`AppStore.swift:271`) as `[String]`. Its "deliberately NOT persisted" rationale (`AppStore.swift:268-270`) is *specifically* "the terminals themselves don't survive a relaunch" — that premise is exactly what this issue reverses, so leaving the comment standing while it is false is worse than the two lines.

### Reused, **not** duplicated into the snapshot
- Selection → `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:109`), applied at `AppStore.swift:2495`.
- Workroom tab-bar order → `Defaults[.workroomTabOrder]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:133`).
- Window frame → `Defaults[.mainWindowFrame]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:119`), applied in `attachWindow` (`AppStore.swift:975-985`).
- Inspector shape/width, diff mode, theme — all existing keys.

### Deliberately dropped (each needs the rationale in a code comment)
1. **Scrollback / PTY / running processes.** libghostty has no session dump, and `canSpawnSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:195`) refuses to respawn a torn-down view. A restored terminal is a new login shell. Anything else would be a lie in the UI.
2. **Run tabs and run state.** A run tab is a terminal whose surface carries a command (`makeRunTab` → `makeTerminalTab(…command:)`, `TerminalSessions.swift:798`/`:1277`); restoring it would silently start the user's dev server on every launch, which `RunConfig.autoRun` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:9`) exists to make an explicit opt-in. The snapshot builder lives on `AppStore` precisely because only it knows `runStates[targetID]?.tab` (`AppStore.swift:1275`), and it excludes that id. **Belt and braces:** the restore path never passes a `command`, so even a leaked run tab returns as a plain shell, never a relaunched server.
3. **`liveTitle` / `cwd` / `progressActive` / `activityPulses`** — surface-reported state about a process that no longer exists. Excluding them is also what makes the save debounce cheap (§5).
4. **Navigation history** (`AppStore.history`) — its entries key on tab UUIDs that are remapped on restore (§4); cross-launch back/forward is its own feature.
5. **Notifications** — already ephemeral by design.
6. **Extra windows.** `window.isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`) is a deliberate "launch with a single window" decision. Do not touch it.

---

## 2. The Codable model

**New file `WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift`.** Three new types, all `Codable, Equatable`; only `SessionSnapshot` is `Defaults.Serializable` (copying `InspectorPaneState`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:225`).

```swift
struct SessionSnapshot: Codable, Defaults.Serializable, Equatable {
  static let currentVersion = 1
  var version = Self.currentVersion
  var targets: [TargetSnapshot]
  var workroomSplits: [PaneLayout<String>]   // leaves are TerminalTarget.ID strings
  var expandedTargets: [String]

  static let maxTargets = 50
  static let maxTabsPerTarget = 40           // cf. NavigationHistory.maxEntries:75
}

struct TargetSnapshot: Codable, Equatable {
  var targetID: String                       // "wr|<project>|<name>" / "root|<project>"
  var tabs: [TabSnapshot]                    // the array IS the strip order
  var split: PaneLayout<UUID>?               // over TabSnapshot.id; ≥2 leaves when present
  var focused: UUID?
  var terminalCounter: Int
}

/// ONE flat, lenient struct for all four content kinds. Flat + optional on purpose: an unknown
/// `kind`, or a kind missing its required field, drops THAT TAB and keeps its siblings — where a
/// synthesised enum-with-payload decoder would throw and take the whole snapshot with it.
struct TabSnapshot: Codable, Equatable {
  var id: UUID                               // join key WITHIN this snapshot only — see §4
  var kind: String                           // terminal | diff | file | changeset
  var cwd: String?          // terminal
  var title: String?        // terminal defaultTitle / changeset title
  var path: String?         // diff / file
  var change: String?       // diff — ChangedFile.Change.rawValue (WorkroomStatus.swift:97)
  var sourceKind: String?   // diff — gitWorktree | jjWorkingCopy | jjParent | commit
  var sourceCommit: String? // diff — .commit(sha) payload
  var commitID: String?     // changeset
  var selectedPath: String? // changeset
  var isPreview = false
  var diffViewMode: String? // DiffViewMode.rawValue (DiffViewMode.swift:12)
  var markdownPreview: Bool?
}
```

**The `Defaults` key** goes in `Core/DefaultsKeys.swift` beside its siblings, since that file is declared "the single source of truth for every persisted preference" (`:19-26`):

```swift
/// Last session's open panels + layouts (issue #46) …
static let session = Key<SessionSnapshot?>("session.snapshot.v1", default: nil)
```

Versioning follows the established two-mechanism story: **version the key string** (`inspector.layout.v2`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:175`) *plus* an in-shape check — here `guard snapshot.version == SessionSnapshot.currentVersion else { return }`, which discards rather than migrates, exactly as `reconcileInspectorState` (`AppStore.swift:4209`) discards a mismatched shape.

### `PaneLayout` gets Codable (not a DTO mirror)

**New file `WorkroomApp/Models/PaneLayout+Codable.swift`** — a hand-written conditional conformance, `extension PaneLayout: Codable where Leaf: Codable`, with explicit `CodingKeys` (`leaf, id, orientation, ratio, first, second`), discriminating on "is `leaf` present". Two reasons to hand-write rather than synthesise: the synthesised enum format is an implementation detail, and this file's key strings are a **stored-data contract** in the sense `RunConfig` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:6-8`) spells out. Decode runs the ratio through `PaneRatio.sanitize` (`PaneLayout.swift:48`), so a hand-edited `0`/`1` can never produce a collapsed pane.

Two supporting edits in **`Models/PaneLayout.swift`**:
- `enum SplitOrientation: String, Equatable` at `:25` — stable `"horizontal"`/`"vertical"` strings. No exhaustive switch breaks; nothing else changes.
- One new pure transform, beside the others (`:91-198`), because the file's contract says structural walks live here:

```swift
/// Rewrite every leaf through `transform`, dropping leaves it maps to nil and collapsing their
/// parent to the surviving sibling — the same collapse rule as `removingLeaf`. Returns nil when
/// nothing survives. One transform serves four jobs: SidebarID ⇄ target-id string on both sides
/// of persistence, and the persisted-tab-id → live-tab-id remap on restore.
func compactMapLeaves<B: Hashable>(_ transform: (Leaf) -> B?) -> PaneLayout<B>?
```

A DTO mirror was the alternative; it was rejected because it would duplicate the tree shape *and* still need a mapping function, i.e. strictly more code for strictly less reuse.

**Why one conformance covers both instantiations:** the terminal split is `PaneLayout<TerminalTab.ID>` = `PaneLayout<UUID>` (Codable); the workroom split is persisted as `PaneLayout<String>` via `compactMapLeaves { AppStore.targetIDString(for: $0) }` (`AppStore.swift:4253`) and read back with `AppStore.sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)` (`AppStore.swift:4171`) — both existing, both `nonisolated static` and already unit-tested.

---

## 3. Tab identity across launches — **remap, do not revive**

`TerminalTab.id` is `let id = UUID()` with no id-taking init (`TerminalSessions.swift:15`). **Do not change it.** Restore mints fresh tabs and builds a `[persistedUUID: TerminalTab.ID]` map; the split tree and the focused id are rewritten through it with `compactMapLeaves`. The persisted UUID is a **join key valid only inside one snapshot**, never an identity.

Why this over persisting the UUID plus an id-taking init:
1. Zero change to `TerminalTab`, so nothing that keys on tab identity can be affected — `WindowRegistry.ownerOf(tabID:)` (`WindowRegistry.swift:127`), `TerminalSessions.containsTab` (`:393`), `SwitcherRecency.recordPane`, `NotificationCenterStore`.
2. Tab ids escape the process: an OS notification carries `tabID` in `userInfo` and is routed by it (`WorkroomApp.swift:520-533`). A delivered-but-unclicked notification from before the relaunch would, with revived UUIDs, route into a "restored" tab that is not the tab it was posted about. Remapping makes that impossible by construction.
3. It costs nothing extra — `compactMapLeaves` is needed for the `SidebarID`↔`String` mapping regardless.

---

## 4. Terminal restore semantics — **lazy spawn. Firm recommendation.**

Restore the tab **models** eagerly (so the strip, chips, split geometry and focus are all correct the instant the window appears), and let each surface spawn its shell exactly as it does today: on window mount.

This requires **no new spawn machinery at all**, because it is already the behaviour:
- `createSurface` is only reachable from `viewDidMoveToWindow` / `ensureSurfaceCreated` / deferred layout, all gated on `canSpawnSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:195-198`). Constructing a `GhosttySurfaceView` allocates no PTY and no Metal surface — `TerminalSessionsTests.swift:6-7` states and depends on exactly this ("constructing one here is inert").
- `reconcileOcclusion` (`TerminalSessions.swift:1089`) already means only the on-screen panes render, and it is already called before any mount (from `addTab`, `:468`).
- The fixture path already relies on this at scale: `loadFixture`'s workroom-overflow branch comments "this costs N tab models and one terminal, not N terminals" (`AppStore.swift`, `UITestFixture.workroomCount` branch).

Eager spawn would cost, at launch, one real login shell **per restored tab** — a modest 4-workrooms × 3-tabs session is 12 `$SHELL -l` processes sourcing the user's dotfiles plus 12 Metal surfaces, i.e. the whole `ShellEnvironment` hazard class ("a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux`", `macapp/CLAUDE.md`) multiplied twelvefold, on the launch path — and buys the user nothing they can see, because a hidden tab's shell has produced no output anyone will read.

The one deliberate eager-spawn exception in the codebase is `addRunTab(focus: false)` → `ensureSurfaceCreated(initialSize:)` (`TerminalSessions.swift:743`), and it exists *because a run command must actually run*. Restored tabs carry no such obligation — and run tabs are dropped from the snapshot anyway (§1).

---

## 5. Write path

### Trigger: coalesced observation, not per-mutation hooks

`TerminalSessions` has ~20 structural mutators; threading a save call through each is a large diff and easy to leave a hole in. Instead, **one** subscription in `AppStore.init` (beside the existing `terminals.activityHandler` / `onFocusChange` / `onTabsRemoved` wiring at `AppStore.swift:840-915`):

```swift
sessionObservation = terminals.objectWillChange.sink { [weak self] _ in self?.scheduleSessionSave() }
```

plus `didSet { scheduleSessionSave() }` on `workroomSplits` (`AppStore.swift:265`) and `expandedTerminalTargets` (`:271`) — mirroring how `collapsedProjects` (`:210`) and `workroomTabOrder` (`:218`) already persist.

The obvious objection — `objectWillChange` also fires on every OSC title frame (`updateTitle`, `TerminalSessions.swift:1108`, ~1–10×/s while a TUI works), every cwd report, every progress flip, every `pulsePaneActivity` — is answered by two things and needs no filtering:
1. **Debounce**, cancel-and-replace, ~1.5 s, copying the `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh` idiom (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:127-145`).
2. **An equality gate**: build the snapshot, compare to the last one written, and return if equal. Because the snapshot excludes titles/cwd/progress/pulses **by design** (§1), every one of those high-frequency publishes produces a byte-identical snapshot and is dropped for free. `SessionSnapshot: Equatable` makes this one line.

Building the snapshot walks a few dozen tiny structs at most once per 1.5 s. Negligible.

### Gates on the write

```swift
guard persistsSidebarPrefs,                 // AppStore.swift:145 — the last-key window only
      !isolatesSessionForTesting,           // cf. isolatesInspectorLayoutForTesting :468
      !UITestFixture.isActive || UITestFixture.persistSession
else { return }
```

`persistsSidebarPrefs` must widen from `private` to internal (`AppStore.swift:145`) so the new extension file can read it. **Reusing that exact gate is load-bearing, not cosmetic:** the session and `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` must be written by the same window or restore is incoherent — you would rehydrate window A's panels under window B's selection.

### Quit and signal paths

`UserDefaults` writes are synchronous, so a flush is a one-liner; no async machinery.

- `applicationShouldTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:548`): `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore?.flushSessionSave()` as the **first** statement — *above* the `UITestFixture.isActive` early return at `:549`, so `app.terminate()` in an XCUITest is deterministic rather than racing the debounce. `WindowRegistry.swift:11-13` already documents `lastActiveStore` as existing "so quit-time persistence reads the right window".
- `installSigtermHandler` (`WorkroomApp.swift:465-477`): same line inside the existing `MainActor.assumeIsolated` block, before `gracefullyStopAllWindows` — this is the path `make app-run` and `pkill` take.
- **Window close needs no new code**, and this should be said in a comment so a reviewer doesn't think it was overlooked: a background window closing is not `lastActiveStore` and therefore never wrote; the last window closing *is*, and its debounced save has already run.
- **Crash**: at most ~1.5 s of layout changes lost. Acceptable; state it.

---

## 6. Read path — the exact interposition ahead of `ensureInitialTerminal`

The race to beat: `WorkroomTerminalsView`'s `.task(id: target.id)` (`Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:96-101`) calls `store.ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:2280`), which adds a tab when `tabCount == 0`.

**Interpose inside `AppStore.apply(_:)` (`AppStore.swift:2468`), immediately before the existing `pendingRestoreSelection` block at `:2495`:**

```swift
// Rehydrate last session's panels BEFORE the selection is restored below. The terminals view
// cannot have mounted yet — it only exists once `selectedTargetID` is non-nil, which happens a
// few lines down in this same synchronous main-actor body — so this always lands ahead of
// `ensureInitialTerminal`'s `tabCount == 0` check and no stray "Terminal 1" is created.
if let saved = pendingRestoreSession { restoreSession(saved, in: fresh) }
pendingRestoreSession = nil
```

This is race-free by construction, not by timing: SwiftUI cannot render between two statements of one main-actor function.

Plumbing, mirroring `pendingRestoreSelection` exactly:
- `AppStore.init`, beside `:839`: `pendingRestoreSession = Defaults[.session]`.
- `bootstrap(restore:)` (`:2306`), beside the existing `if !shouldRestore { pendingRestoreSelection = nil }`: also nil `pendingRestoreSession`. This makes the one-shot `consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`) gate the session too, for free.
- One-shot: consumed in `apply`, so `reload` / `reloadIfStale` (which also reach `apply`, `:2337`/`:2344`) can never re-fire it.
- `loadFixture` (`:2369`) never calls `apply`, so it nils `pendingRestoreSession` alongside its existing `pendingRestoreSelection = nil` — except under the new UI-test flag (§9).

`restoreSession` resolves each `targetID` string → `SidebarID` (`sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)`, `:4171`) → `TerminalTarget` (`target(for:)`, `:1110`), skipping anything that no longer resolves, then calls one new primitive on `TerminalSessions`:

```swift
/// Rehydrate a target's panels from a saved session (issue #46). The ONLY write path that sets the
/// four per-target dictionaries wholesale. Deliberately silent on `onFocusChange` (`notify: false`,
/// the same escape `reap` uses at :1056) — a restore is not navigation, and navigation history is
/// not restored. No-op when the target already has tabs, so a restore can never race a live session.
func restore(_ target: TerminalTarget, from snapshot: TargetSnapshot)
```

It lives in `TerminalSessions` (not `AppStore`) because it must reach `makeTerminalTab` (`:1277`, private) — which already takes a `title:`, so restoring "Terminal 3" adds **zero** new tab-construction code — and the `TerminalTab.diff/.file/.changeset` statics (`:83-95`). It writes `counts[target.id]` after building (since `makeTerminalTab` bumps it), and ends with `reconcileOcclusion`, like every other mutator.

The `TabContent` ⇄ `TabSnapshot` bridge goes in the **existing MARK section at `TerminalSessions.swift:124-182`**, right beside the `NavPayload` bridge, for the reason that section already states: "so a fifth content kind is a compile error in ONE place instead of failing silently in several." The **encode** direction is an exhaustive switch over `TabContent` (that is where the compile-error guarantee bites); the **decode** direction is lenient by design (§2).

---

## 7. Multi-window

Unchanged in shape from the existing design — this is the whole point:
- **One** snapshot, written only by the last-key window (`persistsSidebarPrefs`, `AppStore.swift:145`).
- Restored by exactly the one window that wins `consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`); every ⌘N window and every non-restore window still starts blank.
- Extra windows open at quit are still **not** reopened (`window.isRestorable = false`, `AppStore.swift:971`). Add a sentence to that comment so a future reader doesn't "fix" it: the one restored window now rehydrates its *panels* from `Defaults[.session]`, but the *window set* is still deliberately one.
- Known and accepted consequence, worth naming in the plan and the code: a blank ⌘N window that becomes key and then something publishes on it will write an empty session — because that window is `lastActiveStore`. This is **already** the product's behaviour for `sidebarSelection` (a blank window that becomes key writes `nil`), and matching it exactly is what keeps selection and session mutually consistent. Do not add a "don't overwrite with empty" heuristic: it would break "the user closed everything on purpose".

---

## 8. Robustness

| Hazard | Handling |
|---|---|
| Decode failure / corrupt value | `Defaults` returns the key default (`nil`) → app starts blank, i.e. today's behaviour. No try/catch needed. |
| `version` mismatch | Discard whole snapshot (no migration), mirroring `reconcileInspectorState`'s discard-to-default stance (`AppStore.swift:4209`). |
| Deleted workroom / project | Target-id string fails to resolve against the *live* `fresh` projects → whole entry dropped. Same self-heal as `validatedSelection` (`:2571`), `orderedActiveTargets` (`:4270`), `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` (`AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift:297`). |
| Stale workroom-split leaf | `compactMapLeaves` drops it and collapses; `<2` surviving leaves ⇒ the group is dropped, matching the ≥2-leaf invariant. `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` then runs later in the same `apply` as a second net. |
| Split leaf naming a tab that was dropped (run tab, unknown kind) | Same `compactMapLeaves` collapse, both on encode and decode. |
| Target with zero surviving tabs | Dropped entirely — never write an empty `orderByTarget` key, which would make `ensureTab`'s `orderByTarget[target.id] == nil` check (`TerminalSessions.swift:459`) lie. |
| **Deleted file / rebased-away commit** | **Restore anyway; do not stat.** The viewers already own their empty states (`PlainFileViewer`'s "File unavailable", referenced in `UITestFixture.swift`; `DiffViewer`'s load guard, cf. `DiffViewerLoadGuardTests`). Pre-flighting would put N filesystem/VCS hits on the launch path for an answer that can change a second later. This is the single most important "don't over-engineer" call in the plan. |
| Missing workroom directory | `target(for:)` yields `isMissing: true`; restoring the tab models is inert because the pane never mounts, so no shell spawns. Leave alone. |
| Two preview tabs for one target (hand-edited/corrupt) | Decode normalisation keeps the first, persists the rest — enforcing Inv A (`TerminalSessions.swift:474-476`). Pure, unit-testable. |
| Runaway size | Cap at `maxTargets` / `maxTabsPerTarget` (§2), the `NavigationHistory.maxEntries` idiom (`NavigationHistory.swift:75`). |

---

## 9. Ordered build sequence

Every step ends with `make app-format` and `make app-lint`; steps that add a file need `make app-generate` first (the `macapp/CLAUDE.md` "adding a `.swift` file" gotcha).

**Step 1 — pane-model plumbing (pure, no behaviour).**
`Models/PaneLayout.swift`: `SplitOrientation: String` (`:25`); add `compactMapLeaves` beside the other transforms.
New `Models/PaneLayout+Codable.swift`: conditional `Codable`.
Tests: `PaneLayoutCodableTests`.

**Step 2 — the snapshot type.**
New `Core/SessionSnapshot.swift` (3 types + the decode normalisers: version check, preview de-dup, caps). No wiring yet.
`Core/DefaultsKeys.swift`: add `session` key with its doc comment.
Tests: `SessionSnapshotTests` (pure).

**Step 3 — the `TabContent` ⇄ `TabSnapshot` bridge + the restore primitive.**
`Core/TerminalSessions.swift`: bridge in the `:124-182` MARK section; `restore(_:from:)`; `sessionSnapshot(for:excluding:)`; a two-line `func tabCounter(for:)` accessor for `counts` (`:264`).
Tests: `SessionRestoreTests` restore-half — order, split shape, focus, remap, un-spawned surfaces.

**Step 4 — the store-side read.**
New `Core/AppStore+Session.swift`: `buildSessionSnapshot()`, `restoreSession(_:in:)`, `scheduleSessionSave()`, `flushSessionSave()`, `writeSessionSnapshotIfChanged()`.
`Core/AppStore.swift`: `pendingRestoreSession` field; set in `init` (`:839`); nil in `bootstrap` (`:2306`) and `loadFixture` (`:2369`); consume in `apply` (`:2495`); widen `persistsSidebarPrefs` (`:145`) to internal; add `isolatesSessionForTesting`.
Tests: the "restore then `ensureInitialTerminal` adds nothing" assertion.

**Step 5 — the write path.**
`AppStore.init` subscription; `didSet` on `workroomSplits` / `expandedTerminalTargets`.
`WorkroomApp.swift`: flush in `applicationShouldTerminate` (`:548`, above the fixture early return) and `installSigtermHandler` (`:465`).
Tests: `SessionSaveTests`, including the run-tab exclusion and the equality-gate coalescing.

**Step 6 — UI-test seam.**
`Core/UITestFixture.swift`: `persistSession` flag (`-WorkroomUITestPersistSession 1`); in `applyFixtureDefaults` (`:494`) add `if !persistSession { Defaults[.session] = nil }`, with the same rationale the `Defaults[.vcsLastFetch] = [:]` line already carries. Under the flag only, `loadFixture` calls `restoreSession(saved, in: fixtures)` immediately before its `fixtureAutoSelect` block. The enabling fact that makes this testable at all: fixture project paths are **stable across launches** (`NSTemporaryDirectory()/workroom-uitest/…`, `UITestFixture.projects()`), so a snapshot written in launch 1 resolves in launch 2.

**Step 7 — the load-bearing comments that are now false.** Not optional in this codebase:
- `TerminalSessions.swift:241-242` — "Cross-relaunch disk persistence is intentionally out of scope."
- `DefaultsKeys.swift:131-133` — `workroomTabOrder`: "Terminals don't survive relaunch, so this is just an ordering hint."
- `AppStore.swift:262-263` — `workroomSplits`: "Session-only (not persisted, like the terminal split)."
- `AppStore.swift:268-270` — `expandedTerminalTargets`: "the terminals themselves don't survive a relaunch."

**Step 8 — XCUITests** (`make app-uitest`; not part of the `make app-test` gate).

---

## 10. Test plan

### Unit (`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/`)

**`PaneLayoutCodableTests`** — round-trip `PaneLayout<UUID>` and `PaneLayout<String>` for a lone leaf, a 2-pane split, a 3-deep asymmetric tree; **decode a hand-written JSON literal** so a future refactor that renames a key fails loudly (the stored-data-contract convention). `compactMapLeaves`: total map; one leaf dropped → parent collapses to sibling; both children of a subtree dropped → that subtree collapses; everything dropped → nil.

**`SessionSnapshotTests`** (pure) — version mismatch discarded; unknown `kind` drops that tab and keeps siblings; a `.diff` missing `path` dropped; split leaf naming a dropped tab collapses; target with zero survivors dropped; two previews normalised to one; caps enforced.

**`SessionRestoreTests`** (`@MainActor`, real `TerminalSessions` with the `makeView` seam, `TerminalSessionsTests.swift:12-16` idiom) —
- restore N tabs → `tabs(for:)` order, `split(for:)` shape, `focusedTab(for:)`, `tabCounter(for:)`;
- **displayed-order round-trip idempotence**: snapshot a split session, restore it, re-snapshot ⇒ identical;
- **no eager spawn**: every restored terminal's surface still reports `canSpawnSurface == true` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:195`, already exercised by `GhosttySurfaceViewTests`);
- **the `ensureInitialTerminal` assertion**: after restoring, calling `AppStore.ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` adds nothing;
- stale target-id string → entry dropped, siblings restored;
- workroom-split groups round-trip; a group with a since-deleted leaf collapses/dissolves.

**`SessionSaveTests`** — run tab excluded (and its split leaf collapsed); a target whose only tab was the run tab is dropped; **the coalescing gate**: `sessions.pulsePaneActivity(tabID)` (`TerminalSessions.swift:1100`, public and genuinely high-frequency) produces an *equal* snapshot ⇒ no write.

**Defaults hygiene** — per the `SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift:11-19` doctrine (parallel workers share one on-disk domain, so exactly one class owns a shared key): **one** new class owns the raw `session.snapshot.v1` key with save/restore in `setUp`/`tearDown`. Every other test above drives the pure encode/decode functions or an `AppStore` with `isolatesSessionForTesting = true` and an injected snapshot — never `Defaults`.

### XCUITest (`macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests.swift`) — warranted

This is new user-visible behaviour on the launch path, and one of its two failure modes (the `ensureInitialTerminal` view-`.task` ordering fault) is exactly the kind a unit test cannot fully prove. Model the file on `SplitPaneUITests.swift` (`panes(_:)` counts `terminal.pane`, `tabs(_:)` counts `terminal.tab.*` chips, `assertCount(_:reaches:)`).

1. **`testSplitLayoutSurvivesRelaunch`** — launch with `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1 -WorkroomUITestPersistSession 1 -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`; wait for 1 pane; ⌘D → assert 2 panes; `app.terminate()` (deterministic thanks to the Step-5 flush ordering); `app.launch()` with the same arguments; **assert 2 panes render with no ⌘D** — the split came back.
2. **`testRestoreDoesNotAddAStrayTerminal`** — the highest-value assertion in the feature: after the relaunch, the chip count equals exactly what was saved. This is the regression that a stray "Terminal 1" from `ensureInitialTerminal` would produce.
3. *(optional, if cheap)* **`testRelaunchWithoutTheFlagStartsFresh`** — proves the fixture seam isolates the other 34 UI tests; every other test's `applyFixtureDefaults` clears the key, so this is self-cleaning teardown as well.

---

## 11. Risks

1. **`objectWillChange` firing more often than expected.** Mitigated by debounce + the `Equatable` gate; if profiling shows the build cost matters, the *narrowing* step is to fire from `setFocused` (`:974`), `insert`/`insertID` (`:1259`/`:1264`) and the `splitByTarget` writers instead — but do not start there.
2. **`persistsSidebarPrefs` widened to internal.** One-word access change; note in the doc comment that the session and the sidebar prefs must share the gate.
3. **Fixture-mode leakage.** Fully closed by clearing `Defaults[.session]` in `applyFixtureDefaults` unless the new flag is set — the `vcsLastFetch` precedent (`UITestFixture.swift:~507`) exists because this exact class of leak already bit once.
4. **Scope creep into cross-launch navigation history.** Explicitly out (§1.4); the UUID remap makes it a non-starter anyway, which is a feature.

# Issue #46 — Persist open panels (terminals, diffs) and layouts across restarts

## Design premise

One new `Defaults` key holding one `Codable` snapshot, written by the last-active window and read by the one launch window that already wins `ProjectStore.consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`). Restored terminals are **fresh shells in the remembered cwd** — no scrollback, no process resume. Zero changes to the pane model's semantics; `PaneLayout` gains only a `Codable` conformance and one pure transform.

---

## 1. What gets persisted, and what is deliberately dropped

### Persisted (per target, keyed by `TerminalTarget.ID` string)
| Thing | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tab list **in strip order** | `TerminalSessions.displayedTabIDs(for:)` (`TerminalSessions.swift:368`) | The snapshot array **is** the order — no separate order field to desync. Feeding the displayed order back as the loose `orderByTarget` reproduces the same display, because normalisation is idempotent when the split's members are already a contiguous run in tree order. |
| Terminal tab payload | `cwd` = `surface.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path`; `title` = `TerminalState.defaultTitle` | `defaultTitle` is the stable "Terminal N"; `liveTitle` is not persisted. |
| Diff tab payload | `DiffDescriptor` (`DiffDescriptor.swift:25`) — `path`, `change.rawValue`, `source`, `isPreview` | |
| File tab payload | `FileDescriptor` (`FileTree.swift:15`) — `path`, `isPreview` | |
| Changeset tab payload | `ChangesetDescriptor` (`ChangesetDescriptor.swift:7`) — `commitID`, `title`, `isPreview`, `selectedPath` | |
| Per-tab overrides | `diffViewModeOverride`, `markdownPreviewOverride` (`TerminalSessions.swift:22`, `:28`) | Cheap, and their loss is a visible "it forgot". |
| Split tree | `splitByTarget` (`TerminalSessions.swift:256`) | |
| Focused tab | `focusedTabByTarget` (`TerminalSessions.swift:258`) | |
| `counts` (the "Terminal N" counter) | `TerminalSessions.swift:264` | Without it, the next ⌘T after restoring "Terminal 1–3" is another "Terminal 1". |

### Persisted (per window, in the same snapshot)
- `AppStore.workroomSplits` (`AppStore.swift:265`) as `[PaneLayout<String>]` of target-id strings.
- `AppStore.expandedTerminalTargets` (`AppStore.swift:271`) as `[String]`. Its "deliberately NOT persisted" rationale (`AppStore.swift:268-270`) is *specifically* "the terminals themselves don't survive a relaunch" — that premise is exactly what this issue reverses, so leaving the comment standing while it is false is worse than the two lines.

### Reused, **not** duplicated into the snapshot
- Selection → `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:109`), applied at `AppStore.swift:2495`.
- Workroom tab-bar order → `Defaults[.workroomTabOrder]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:133`).
- Window frame → `Defaults[.mainWindowFrame]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:119`), applied in `attachWindow` (`AppStore.swift:975-985`).
- Inspector shape/width, diff mode, theme — all existing keys.

### Deliberately dropped (each needs the rationale in a code comment)
1. **Scrollback / PTY / running processes.** libghostty has no session dump, and `canSpawnSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:195`) refuses to respawn a torn-down view. A restored terminal is a new login shell. Anything else would be a lie in the UI.
2. **Run tabs and run state.** A run tab is a terminal whose surface carries a command (`makeRunTab` → `makeTerminalTab(…command:)`, `TerminalSessions.swift:798`/`:1277`); restoring it would silently start the user's dev server on every launch, which `RunConfig.autoRun` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:9`) exists to make an explicit opt-in. The snapshot builder lives on `AppStore` precisely because only it knows `runStates[targetID]?.tab` (`AppStore.swift:1275`), and it excludes that id. **Belt and braces:** the restore path never passes a `command`, so even a leaked run tab returns as a plain shell, never a relaunched server.
3. **`liveTitle` / `cwd` / `progressActive` / `activityPulses`** — surface-reported state about a process that no longer exists. Excluding them is also what makes the save debounce cheap (§5).
4. **Navigation history** (`AppStore.history`) — its entries key on tab UUIDs that are remapped on restore (§4); cross-launch back/forward is its own feature.
5. **Notifications** — already ephemeral by design.
6. **Extra windows.** `window.isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`) is a deliberate "launch with a single window" decision. Do not touch it.

## 2. The Codable model

**New file `WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift`.** Three new types, all `Codable, Equatable`; only `SessionSnapshot` is `Defaults.Serializable` (copying `InspectorPaneState`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:225`).

```swift
struct SessionSnapshot: Codable, Defaults.Serializable, Equatable {
  static let currentVersion = 1
  var version = Self.currentVersion
  var targets: [TargetSnapshot]
  var workroomSplits: [PaneLayout<String>]   // leaves are TerminalTarget.ID strings
  var expandedTargets: [String]

  static let maxTargets = 50
  static let maxTabsPerTarget = 40           // cf. NavigationHistory.maxEntries:75
}

struct TargetSnapshot: Codable, Equatable {
  var targetID: String                       // "wr|<project>|<name>" / "root|<project>"
  var tabs: [TabSnapshot]                    // the array IS the strip order
  var split: PaneLayout<UUID>?               // over TabSnapshot.id; ≥2 leaves when present
  var focused: UUID?
  var terminalCounter: Int
}

/// ONE flat, lenient struct for all four content kinds. Flat + optional on purpose: an unknown
/// `kind`, or a kind missing its required field, drops THAT TAB and keeps its siblings — where a
/// synthesised enum-with-payload decoder would throw and take the whole snapshot with it.
struct TabSnapshot: Codable, Equatable {
  var id: UUID                               // join key WITHIN this snapshot only — see §4
  var kind: String                           // terminal | diff | file | changeset
  var cwd: String?          // terminal
  var title: String?        // terminal defaultTitle / changeset title
  var path: String?         // diff / file
  var change: String?       // diff — ChangedFile.Change.rawValue (WorkroomStatus.swift:97)
  var sourceKind: String?   // diff — gitWorktree | jjWorkingCopy | jjParent | commit
  var sourceCommit: String? // diff — .commit(sha) payload
  var commitID: String?     // changeset
  var selectedPath: String? // changeset
  var isPreview = false
  var diffViewMode: String? // DiffViewMode.rawValue (DiffViewMode.swift:12)
  var markdownPreview: Bool?
}
```

**The `Defaults` key** goes in `Core/DefaultsKeys.swift` beside its siblings, since that file is declared "the single source of truth for every persisted preference" (`:19-26`):

```swift
/// Last session's open panels + layouts (issue #46) …
static let session = Key<SessionSnapshot?>("session.snapshot.v1", default: nil)
```

Versioning follows the established two-mechanism story: **version the key string** (`inspector.layout.v2`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:175`) *plus* an in-shape check — here `guard snapshot.version == SessionSnapshot.currentVersion else { return }`, which discards rather than migrates, exactly as `reconcileInspectorState` (`AppStore.swift:4209`) discards a mismatched shape.

### `PaneLayout` gets Codable (not a DTO mirror)

**New file `WorkroomApp/Models/PaneLayout+Codable.swift`** — a hand-written conditional conformance, `extension PaneLayout: Codable where Leaf: Codable`, with explicit `CodingKeys` (`leaf, id, orientation, ratio, first, second`), discriminating on "is `leaf` present". Two reasons to hand-write rather than synthesise: the synthesised enum format is an implementation detail, and this file's key strings are a **stored-data contract** in the sense `RunConfig` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:6-8`) spells out. Decode runs the ratio through `PaneRatio.sanitize` (`PaneLayout.swift:48`), so a hand-edited `0`/`1` can never produce a collapsed pane.

Two supporting edits in **`Models/PaneLayout.swift`**:
- `enum SplitOrientation: String, Equatable` at `:25` — stable `"horizontal"`/`"vertical"` strings. No exhaustive switch breaks; nothing else changes.
- One new pure transform, beside the others (`:91-198`), because the file's contract says structural walks live here:

```swift
/// Rewrite every leaf through `transform`, dropping leaves it maps to nil and collapsing their
/// parent to the surviving sibling — the same collapse rule as `removingLeaf`. Returns nil when
/// nothing survives. One transform serves four jobs: SidebarID ⇄ target-id string on both sides
/// of persistence, and the persisted-tab-id → live-tab-id remap on restore.
func compactMapLeaves<B: Hashable>(_ transform: (Leaf) -> B?) -> PaneLayout<B>?
```

A DTO mirror was the alternative; it was rejected because it would duplicate the tree shape *and* still need a mapping function, i.e. strictly more code for strictly less reuse.

**Why one conformance covers both instantiations:** the terminal split is `PaneLayout<TerminalTab.ID>` = `PaneLayout<UUID>` (Codable); the workroom split is persisted as `PaneLayout<String>` via `compactMapLeaves { AppStore.targetIDString(for: $0) }` (`AppStore.swift:4253`) and read back with `AppStore.sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)` (`AppStore.swift:4171`) — both existing, both `nonisolated static` and already unit-tested.

## 3. Tab identity across launches — **remap, do not revive**

`TerminalTab.id` is `let id = UUID()` with no id-taking init (`TerminalSessions.swift:15`). **Do not change it.** Restore mints fresh tabs and builds a `[persistedUUID: TerminalTab.ID]` map; the split tree and the focused id are rewritten through it with `compactMapLeaves`. The persisted UUID is a **join key valid only inside one snapshot**, never an identity.

Why this over persisting the UUID plus an id-taking init:
1. Zero change to `TerminalTab`, so nothing that keys on tab identity can be affected — `WindowRegistry.ownerOf(tabID:)` (`WindowRegistry.swift:127`), `TerminalSessions.containsTab` (`:393`), `SwitcherRecency.recordPane`, `NotificationCenterStore`.
2. Tab ids escape the process: an OS notification carries `tabID` in `userInfo` and is routed by it (`WorkroomApp.swift:520-533`). A delivered-but-unclicked notification from before the relaunch would, with revived UUIDs, route into a "restored" tab that is not the tab it was posted about. Remapping makes that impossible by construction.
3. It costs nothing extra — `compactMapLeaves` is needed for the `SidebarID`↔`String` mapping regardless.

---

## 4. Terminal restore semantics — **lazy spawn. Firm recommendation.**

Restore the tab **models** eagerly (so the strip, chips, split geometry and focus are all correct the instant the window appears), and let each surface spawn its shell exactly as it does today: on window mount.

This requires **no new spawn machinery at all**, because it is already the behaviour:
- `createSurface` is only reachable from `viewDidMoveToWindow` / `ensureSurfaceCreated` / deferred layout, all gated on `canSpawnSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:195-198`). Constructing a `GhosttySurfaceView` allocates no PTY and no Metal surface — `TerminalSessionsTests.swift:6-7` states and depends on exactly this ("constructing one here is inert").
- `reconcileOcclusion` (`TerminalSessions.swift:1089`) already means only the on-screen panes render, and it is already called before any mount (from `addTab`, `:468`).
- The fixture path already relies on this at scale: `loadFixture`'s workroom-overflow branch comments "this costs N tab models and one terminal, not N terminals" (`AppStore.swift`, `UITestFixture.workroomCount` branch).

Eager spawn would cost, at launch, one real login shell **per restored tab** — a modest 4-workrooms × 3-tabs session is 12 `$SHELL -l` processes sourcing the user's dotfiles plus 12 Metal surfaces, i.e. the whole `ShellEnvironment` hazard class ("a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux`", `macapp/CLAUDE.md`) multiplied twelvefold, on the launch path — and buys the user nothing they can see, because a hidden tab's shell has produced no output anyone will read.

The one deliberate eager-spawn exception in the codebase is `addRunTab(focus: false)` → `ensureSurfaceCreated(initialSize:)` (`TerminalSessions.swift:743`), and it exists *because a run command must actually run*. Restored tabs carry no such obligation — and run tabs are dropped from the snapshot anyway (§1).

---

## 5. Write path

### Trigger: coalesced observation, not per-mutation hooks

`TerminalSessions` has ~20 structural mutators; threading a save call through each is a large diff and easy to leave a hole in. Instead, **one** subscription in `AppStore.init` (beside the existing `terminals.activityHandler` / `onFocusChange` / `onTabsRemoved` wiring at `AppStore.swift:840-915`):

```swift
sessionObservation = terminals.objectWillChange.sink { [weak self] _ in self?.scheduleSessionSave() }
```

plus `didSet { scheduleSessionSave() }` on `workroomSplits` (`AppStore.swift:265`) and `expandedTerminalTargets` (`:271`) — mirroring how `collapsedProjects` (`:210`) and `workroomTabOrder` (`:218`) already persist.

The obvious objection — `objectWillChange` also fires on every OSC title frame (`updateTitle`, `TerminalSessions.swift:1108`, ~1–10×/s while a TUI works), every cwd report, every progress flip, every `pulsePaneActivity` — is answered by two things and needs no filtering:
1. **Debounce**, cancel-and-replace, ~1.5 s, copying the `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh` idiom (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:127-145`).
2. **An equality gate**: build the snapshot, compare to the last one written, and return if equal. Because the snapshot excludes titles/cwd/progress/pulses **by design** (§1), every one of those high-frequency publishes produces a byte-identical snapshot and is dropped for free. `SessionSnapshot: Equatable` makes this one line.

Building the snapshot walks a few dozen tiny structs at most once per 1.5 s. Negligible.

### Gates on the write

```swift
guard persistsSidebarPrefs,                 // AppStore.swift:145 — the last-key window only
      !isolatesSessionForTesting,           // cf. isolatesInspectorLayoutForTesting :468
      !UITestFixture.isActive || UITestFixture.persistSession
else { return }
```

`persistsSidebarPrefs` must widen from `private` to internal (`AppStore.swift:145`) so the new extension file can read it. **Reusing that exact gate is load-bearing, not cosmetic:** the session and `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` must be written by the same window or restore is incoherent — you would rehydrate window A's panels under window B's selection.

### Quit and signal paths

`UserDefaults` writes are synchronous, so a flush is a one-liner; no async machinery.

- `applicationShouldTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:548`): `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore?.flushSessionSave()` as the **first** statement — *above* the `UITestFixture.isActive` early return at `:549`, so `app.terminate()` in an XCUITest is deterministic rather than racing the debounce. `WindowRegistry.swift:11-13` already documents `lastActiveStore` as existing "so quit-time persistence reads the right window".
- `installSigtermHandler` (`WorkroomApp.swift:465-477`): same line inside the existing `MainActor.assumeIsolated` block, before `gracefullyStopAllWindows` — this is the path `make app-run` and `pkill` take.
- **Window close needs no new code**, and this should be said in a comment so a reviewer doesn't think it was overlooked: a background window closing is not `lastActiveStore` and therefore never wrote; the last window closing *is*, and its debounced save has already run.
- **Crash**: at most ~1.5 s of layout changes lost. Acceptable; state it.

## 6. Read path — the exact interposition ahead of `ensureInitialTerminal`

The race to beat: `WorkroomTerminalsView`'s `.task(id: target.id)` (`Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:96-101`) calls `store.ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:2280`), which adds a tab when `tabCount == 0`.

**Interpose inside `AppStore.apply(_:)` (`AppStore.swift:2468`), immediately before the existing `pendingRestoreSelection` block at `:2495`:**

```swift
// Rehydrate last session's panels BEFORE the selection is restored below. The terminals view
// cannot have mounted yet — it only exists once `selectedTargetID` is non-nil, which happens a
// few lines down in this same synchronous main-actor body — so this always lands ahead of
// `ensureInitialTerminal`'s `tabCount == 0` check and no stray "Terminal 1" is created.
if let saved = pendingRestoreSession { restoreSession(saved, in: fresh) }
pendingRestoreSession = nil
```

This is race-free by construction, not by timing: SwiftUI cannot render between two statements of one main-actor function.

Plumbing, mirroring `pendingRestoreSelection` exactly:
- `AppStore.init`, beside `:839`: `pendingRestoreSession = Defaults[.session]`.
- `bootstrap(restore:)` (`:2306`), beside the existing `if !shouldRestore { pendingRestoreSelection = nil }`: also nil `pendingRestoreSession`. This makes the one-shot `consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`) gate the session too, for free.
- One-shot: consumed in `apply`, so `reload` / `reloadIfStale` (which also reach `apply`, `:2337`/`:2344`) can never re-fire it.
- `loadFixture` (`:2369`) never calls `apply`, so it nils `pendingRestoreSession` alongside its existing `pendingRestoreSelection = nil` — except under the new UI-test flag (§9).

`restoreSession` resolves each `targetID` string → `SidebarID` (`sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)`, `:4171`) → `TerminalTarget` (`target(for:)`, `:1110`), skipping anything that no longer resolves, then calls one new primitive on `TerminalSessions`:

```swift
/// Rehydrate a target's panels from a saved session (issue #46). The ONLY write path that sets the
/// four per-target dictionaries wholesale. Deliberately silent on `onFocusChange` (`notify: false`,
/// the same escape `reap` uses at :1056) — a restore is not navigation, and navigation history is
/// not restored. No-op when the target already has tabs, so a restore can never race a live session.
func restore(_ target: TerminalTarget, from snapshot: TargetSnapshot)
```

It lives in `TerminalSessions` (not `AppStore`) because it must reach `makeTerminalTab` (`:1277`, private) — which already takes a `title:`, so restoring "Terminal 3" adds **zero** new tab-construction code — and the `TerminalTab.diff/.file/.changeset` statics (`:83-95`). It writes `counts[target.id]` after building (since `makeTerminalTab` bumps it), and ends with `reconcileOcclusion`, like every other mutator.

The `TabContent` ⇄ `TabSnapshot` bridge goes in the **existing MARK section at `TerminalSessions.swift:124-182`**, right beside the `NavPayload` bridge, for the reason that section already states: "so a fifth content kind is a compile error in ONE place instead of failing silently in several." The **encode** direction is an exhaustive switch over `TabContent` (that is where the compile-error guarantee bites); the **decode** direction is lenient by design (§2).

## 7. Multi-window

Unchanged in shape from the existing design — this is the whole point:
- **One** snapshot, written only by the last-key window (`persistsSidebarPrefs`, `AppStore.swift:145`).
- Restored by exactly the one window that wins `consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`); every ⌘N window and every non-restore window still starts blank.
- Extra windows open at quit are still **not** reopened (`window.isRestorable = false`, `AppStore.swift:971`). Add a sentence to that comment so a future reader doesn't "fix" it: the one restored window now rehydrates its *panels* from `Defaults[.session]`, but the *window set* is still deliberately one.
- Known and accepted consequence, worth naming in the plan and the code: a blank ⌘N window that becomes key and then something publishes on it will write an empty session — because that window is `lastActiveStore`. This is **already** the product's behaviour for `sidebarSelection` (a blank window that becomes key writes `nil`), and matching it exactly is what keeps selection and session mutually consistent. Do not add a "don't overwrite with empty" heuristic: it would break "the user closed everything on purpose".

## 8. Robustness

| Hazard | Handling |
|---|---|
| Decode failure / corrupt value | `Defaults` returns the key default (`nil`) → app starts blank, i.e. today's behaviour. No try/catch needed. |
| `version` mismatch | Discard whole snapshot (no migration), mirroring `reconcileInspectorState`'s discard-to-default stance (`AppStore.swift:4209`). |
| Deleted workroom / project | Target-id string fails to resolve against the *live* `fresh` projects → whole entry dropped. Same self-heal as `validatedSelection` (`:2571`), `orderedActiveTargets` (`:4270`), `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` (`AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift:297`). |
| Stale workroom-split leaf | `compactMapLeaves` drops it and collapses; `<2` surviving leaves ⇒ the group is dropped, matching the ≥2-leaf invariant. `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` then runs later in the same `apply` as a second net. |
| Split leaf naming a tab that was dropped (run tab, unknown kind) | Same `compactMapLeaves` collapse, both on encode and decode. |
| Target with zero surviving tabs | Dropped entirely — never write an empty `orderByTarget` key, which would make `ensureTab`'s `orderByTarget[target.id] == nil` check (`TerminalSessions.swift:459`) lie. |
| **Deleted file / rebased-away commit** | **Restore anyway; do not stat.** The viewers already own their empty states (`PlainFileViewer`'s "File unavailable", referenced in `UITestFixture.swift`; `DiffViewer`'s load guard, cf. `DiffViewerLoadGuardTests`). Pre-flighting would put N filesystem/VCS hits on the launch path for an answer that can change a second later. This is the single most important "don't over-engineer" call in the plan. |
| Missing workroom directory | `target(for:)` yields `isMissing: true`; restoring the tab models is inert because the pane never mounts, so no shell spawns. Leave alone. |
| Two preview tabs for one target (hand-edited/corrupt) | Decode normalisation keeps the first, persists the rest — enforcing Inv A (`TerminalSessions.swift:474-476`). Pure, unit-testable. |
| Runaway size | Cap at `maxTargets` / `maxTabsPerTarget` (§2), the `NavigationHistory.maxEntries` idiom (`NavigationHistory.swift:75`). |

## 1. Storage: a versioned JSON file in Application Support. Firm.

Not `Defaults`. The arguments, weighted:

**Decisive — blast radius.** This app's known crash mode is libghostty surface teardown; `WorkroomApp.swift:606-617` is an entire comment about not freeing surfaces on quit because it crashes. A session blob in UserDefaults shares one plist with `themeFamily`, `runCommands`, `workroomLabels`, `releaseChannel`, `switcher*Modifier`, `lastSeenVersion`. A corrupted or partially-flushed domain takes **all of them**. A separate file loses only the session. That asymmetry alone settles it.

**Decisive — schema evolution.** The house pattern for versioning a `Defaults` key is to version the *key string* (`inspector.layout.v2`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:175`) plus discard-on-shape-mismatch (`reconcileInspectorState`, `AppStore.swift:4209`). That's correct for a 4-bool preference. For a user's 40-tab layout, "silently throw it away on every schema bump" is the wrong default and a bad habit to build in. A file gets a real `schemaVersion` int, real migrations, and **element-granular** degradation.

**Debuggability.** "Delete `~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<bundle id>/session.json` and relaunch" is a support instruction a user can follow, and a file a bug report can attach. `defaults read com.developwithstyle.workroom` dumps every preference the app has.

**Size/shape.** 8 workrooms × 6 tabs with paths ≈ 20–40 KB. Not fatal in UserDefaults, but it's the wrong shape for a store designed for scalar preferences, and it rides `cfprefsd`'s whole-domain sync.

**Atomicity.** `Data.write(to:options:.atomic)` is a rename(2): the file on disk is always a complete old or complete new document. UserDefaults gives no per-key equivalent and `synchronize()` is deprecated.

**Test hygiene (underrated).** `SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift:10-19` documents that parallel test workers share one UserDefaults domain, so a whole class exists purely to serialise writes to three keys. An injectable file URL sidesteps that entirely — the new unit tests touch **zero** shared Defaults keys.

**The one real cost, and its price.** A file does *not* get the per-bundle-id domain separation that makes `Workroom`, `Workroom Dev`, and `Workroom Nightly` coexist (macapp/CLAUDE.md "Gotchas"). `GhosttyApp.themeConfigURL` (`Core/GhosttyApp.swift:217-223`) already writes `Application Support/Workroom/ghostty.conf` from all three identities. Without buying that back, a Debug run's fixture temp-dir workrooms would be restored into the release build. **So the path is scoped by bundle id:**

```
~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier>/session.json
```

Second cost: a new IO surface (permissions, disk full). Mitigation is a hard rule — **every read and write is best-effort; the app must behave identically with the file absent, empty, or unreadable.** Failures log via `Logger(subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "session")` (the `GhosttyApp.swift:39` / `LibGit2.swift:28` pattern) and are never surfaced.
