## 2. The schema

New file `WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift`. **Every type here is a hand-written mirror.** No runtime type gains `Codable`.

```swift
struct SessionFile: Codable, Sendable {
  static let currentSchemaVersion = 1
  var schemaVersion: Int
  var savedAt: Date
  var appVersion: String?              // diagnostics only, never branched on
  @Lossy var windows: [WindowSession]  // exactly one today — the growth seam (§6)
}

struct WindowSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// Reserved for per-window restore. Always nil today: no window has a cross-launch identity
  /// (`WindowSeed.launch` mints a fresh UUID per access, `isRestorable = false`). See §6.
  var windowKey: String?
  @Lossy var targets: [TargetSession]
  /// `AppStore.workroomSplits` — leaves are `TerminalTarget.ID` strings.
  @Lossy var workroomSplits: [LayoutNode<String>]
  /// `AppStore.expandedTerminalTargets`.
  var expandedTargets: [String]?
}

struct TargetSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// `TerminalTarget.ID`: "wr|<project>|<name>" or "root|<project>".
  var targetID: String
  @Lossy var tabs: [TabSession]      // strip order; `key` is the address space
  var split: LayoutNode<String>?     // leaves are TabSession.key
  var focusedKey: String?
  var terminalCounter: Int?          // TerminalSessions.counts — keeps "Terminal 7" going
}

struct TabSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// Unique *within this TargetSession*. Sourced from the runtime `TerminalTab.ID.uuidString`
  /// at capture time purely because it's already unique — it is NOT a cross-launch identity
  /// (restore mints fresh runtime ids; see §3).
  var key: String
  var kind: String                   // "terminal" | "diff" | "file" | "changeset"
  var terminal: TerminalPayload?
  var diff: DiffPayload?
  var file: FilePayload?
  var changeset: ChangesetPayload?
}

struct TerminalPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var defaultTitle: String   // "Terminal 3" — NOT the live OSC title (see below)
  var cwd: String?           // last reported cwd; validated at restore
}
struct DiffPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var path: String
  var change: String                 // ChangedFile.Change.rawValue — already a String raw enum
  var source: DiffSourcePayload
  var isPreview: Bool
  var viewMode: String?              // TerminalTab.diffViewModeOverride
}
struct DiffSourcePayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var kind: String                   // "gitWorktree"|"jjWorkingCopy"|"jjParent"|"commit"
  var commit: String?
}
struct FilePayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var path: String; var isPreview: Bool; var markdownPreview: Bool?
}
struct ChangesetPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var commitID: String; var title: String; var isPreview: Bool; var selectedPath: String?
}

/// The Codable mirror of `PaneLayout`, generic over its leaf address. Hand-written with an explicit
/// `kind` discriminator so the on-disk format is a contract THIS file owns — not whatever Swift's
/// synthesized Codable emits for an indirect enum with associated values.
indirect enum LayoutNode<Leaf: Codable & Hashable & Sendable>: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  case leaf(Leaf)
  case split(orientation: String, ratio: Double, first: LayoutNode, second: LayoutNode)
}
```

**Deliberate omissions, each with a reason:**

- **`liveTitle` / `progressActive`.** A restored shell is a fresh process; a persisted live title is a lie the strip would keep telling. Also the churniest field in the model — excluding it is what makes the save digest (§5) stable.
- **`PaneLayout.split`'s `id: UUID`.** Nothing outside the tree references it across a launch (it only addresses a divider during a drag). Minted fresh at restore.
- **Run tabs.** A restored run tab would resurrect a dev server with no `AppStore.RunState` behind it — an untracked process orphaned on a port, exactly the failure `AppStore.swift:886-894` and `Core/WindowRegistry.swift:187` exist to prevent. Skipped at capture via `tab.surface?.isRunCommandSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:821`). `Defaults[.runCommands]` already survives, and ⌘R is one keystroke.
- **`selectedTargetID`.** Already owned by `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:109`), restored via `pendingRestoreSelection` (`AppStore.swift:839`, `:2495`), and covered by `SelectionTests`. Putting it in the snapshot too would give one value two homes — the exact failure mode `NavPayload`'s doc (`TerminalSessions.swift:135-137`) and `ProjectStore.ghAuthCache` (`ProjectStore.swift:38-40`) are written against. The snapshot owns **panels and layouts**; Defaults owns **which workroom**. They're orthogonal.
- **Scrollback.** libghostty exposes no session dump. Say so in the doc comment rather than letting a reader assume it was forgotten.

**No new id format ships.** `TerminalTarget.ID` strings are already the persisted encoding of `sidebarSelection` and `workroomTabOrder`. `SidebarID` round-trips through the existing pure pair `AppStore.targetIDString(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:4253`) and `AppStore.sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)` (`:4172`) — both `nonisolated static`, both already unit-tested, and the second already resolves stale ids to nil. That is the whole answer to "how does `SidebarID` become encodable": **it doesn't.**

### Degradation rules

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| File missing / unreadable | No restore, no error. Fresh-install path. |
| Envelope undecodable | Discard. Move once to `session.corrupt.json` (replacing any prior) so a bug report has something to attach, then start clean. |
| `schemaVersion > current` (downgrade) | Ignore, restore nothing. Overwritten on next save — accepted one-time loss for a rare developer scenario. |
| `schemaVersion < current` | Run migrations; no migration for that version ⇒ discard. |
| An element in a `@Lossy` array fails | **Drop that element, keep the rest.** |
| Unknown `TabSession.kind` | Decodes structurally, rejected at materialise ⇒ one tab dropped. |
| Layout leaf resolves to nothing | Node collapses to its sibling (`removingLeaf` semantics); result with <2 leaves ⇒ no split, tabs kept. |
| Unknown orientation string | Reject that target's whole split; keep its tabs. |
| Target no longer resolves | Whole `TargetSession` dropped (via `AppStore.target(for:)`). |

`@Lossy` is the single most valuable primitive here — ~20 lines decoding through an `UnkeyedDecodingContainer` element by element, skipping throws. It is what turns "a newer build wrote a fifth tab kind" from *your whole session is gone* into *one tab is missing*.

**This is exactly why tabs are keyed, not index-addressed.** Index addressing plus a lossy array is a silent corruption bug: drop tab 2 of 5 and every later split leaf points at the wrong tab. Keys are drop-safe and self-validating.

**Forward-compat rules, written into the file header:** new fields are always optional with a safe default; removed fields decode as optional and are ignored; unknown fields are **not** round-tripped (an older build saving over a newer one's file drops them). That's the cheap 95%; say it out loud rather than implying more.

## 3. Keeping `PaneLayout` and the runtime model clean

`Models/PaneLayout.swift` is **untouched**. `TerminalSessions.TerminalTab` is **untouched** — no id-taking init, no `Codable`.

Two pure conversions live in `SessionSnapshot.swift`:

```swift
extension LayoutNode {
  /// Runtime tree → snapshot tree. `address` maps a runtime leaf to its persisted key; a leaf that
  /// maps to nil is dropped and its parent collapses to the sibling.
  static func capture<L: Hashable>(_ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?) -> LayoutNode?

  /// Snapshot tree → runtime tree. `resolve` maps a persisted key to a live leaf; unresolvable
  /// leaves collapse. Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive — the "a lone leaf is not a
  /// split" invariant (`PaneLayout.swift:18`) enforced at the boundary, not left to the caller.
  func materialize<L: Hashable>(_ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?) -> PaneLayout<L>?
}
```

`materialize` mints a fresh `UUID()` per split node and pushes `ratio` through the existing `PaneRatio.sanitize` (`PaneLayout.swift:48`). Both functions are `nonisolated`, ~20 lines each, and directly unit-testable — the `AppStore.reconcileInspectorState` (`AppStore.swift:4209`) and `WindowRegistry.cyclePlan` (`WindowRegistry.swift:167`) idiom.

**Tab identity across a launch: it doesn't survive, on purpose.** `let id = UUID()` (`TerminalSessions.swift:15`) carries a live invariant — a tab id is minted once, in-process, and is unique across *windows*; `WindowRegistry.ownerOf(tabID:)` (`WindowRegistry.swift:132`), the notification spine, `SwitcherRecency`, `NavigationHistory`, and `runStates` all lean on it. Restoring persisted UUIDs would put a duplicate-id hazard one bug away (two windows restoring one snapshot) for zero benefit: nothing outside the snapshot refers to a pre-launch tab id. So restore **mints fresh ids and rewires order/split/focus through a `[persistedKey: TerminalTab.ID]` map**. `TerminalTab` needs no change at all.

## 4. Where capture and restore live

Asymmetric, for a concrete reason: Swift `private` is file-scoped, and `tabsByTarget` / `orderByTarget` / `splitByTarget` / `focusedTabByTarget` are `@Published private` (`TerminalSessions.swift:251-258`).

- **Capture** reads only through existing public queries — `activeTargetIDs` (`:401`), `displayedTabIDs(for:)` (`:368`), `tabs(for:)` (`:382`), `split(for:)` (`:412`), `focusedTab(for:)` (`:429`) — plus one new accessor for `counts` (`:264`). So it goes in `SessionSnapshot.swift` as a `@MainActor` free function.
  - Capturing `displayedTabIDs` (display order) rather than the loose `orderByTarget` is safe and avoids widening the class's surface: display normalisation is a fixed point (re-normalising an already-normalised order is identity), so it round-trips visually. Worth a one-line comment.
- **Restore** mutates the private state and needs `setFocused(_:for:notify:)` (`:974`), so it goes **inside `TerminalSessions.swift`** under a new `// MARK: Session restore (issue #46)`, beside the mutation primitives it mirrors. ~80 lines on a 1337-line file.

```swift
/// Re-materialise a persisted session for ONE target. Tabs get FRESH ids (see §3); order, split and
/// focus are rewired through the persisted keys. Focus is set with `notify: false` — a restore is not
/// a navigation, and `AppStore` has not resolved its selection yet, so firing `onFocusChange` here
/// would seed back/forward with a place the user never went.
@discardableResult
func restore(_ session: TargetSession, for target: TerminalTarget) -> Int
```

Terminal tabs are built through the existing `makeTerminalTab(for:cwd:command:title:)` (`:1277`) so every surface callback (`onActivity`, `onTitleChange`, `onCwdChange`, `onCommandFinished`, `onProgressReport`, `onFocused`, `onCmdClickFile`, `onOpenURL`) is wired identically to a live tab — no second wiring site to drift. `command:` is always nil (run tabs aren't restored). After building, `counts[target.id]` is set to `max(persisted, built)`.

**cwd validation** is a pure static so it's testable: persisted cwd if `FileManager.fileExists(atPath:isDirectory:)` says it's a live directory, else `target.path`. A dead cwd would otherwise make libghostty's spawn fail on a restored tab.

## 5. Save triggers, and the exact apply point

### The dirty hook — by construction, not by enumeration

Sink on `terminals.objectWillChange` (the `projectStoreObservation` pattern, `AppStore.swift:824`), plus explicit `didSet` marks on `workroomSplits` (`:265`) and `expandedTerminalTargets` (`:271`).

Hooking `objectWillChange` rather than adding `onSessionChanged?()` at the ~12 mutation sites in `TerminalSessions` is deliberate: it **cannot be forgotten** when a thirteenth mutation lands. That's the same value the codebase already buys with exhaustive switches ("a fifth content kind must be a compile error in ONE place", `TerminalSessions.swift:126-128`).

**Trap to write down:** `objectWillChange` fires *before* the mutation. Capture must therefore always be scheduled, never inline.

Cost control, both required:
- **Debounce 1s** on the main queue (`DispatchWorkItem`, cancel-and-replace).
- **Digest guard.** `WindowSession` is `Hashable`; compare `hashValue` against the last written one and skip identical writes. Because `liveTitle`/`progressActive` are excluded from the schema, a `claude` session animating its title 10×/s produces one cheap snapshot build + hash per second and **zero** disk writes.
- **`savedAt` must be outside the digest** — hash `WindowSession`, not `SessionFile`, or the guard never fires.

Encoding + writing happens on the store's serial `DispatchQueue` (`qos: .utility`); only the snapshot build is on the main actor.

### Flush points

| Hook | Location | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| ⌘Q / Quit Apple-event | `AppDelegate.applicationWillTerminate`, `WorkroomApp.swift:619` (currently empty) | synchronous |
| SIGTERM (`XCUIApplication.terminate()`, `make app-run`, `pkill`, logout) | inside the `MainActor.assumeIsolated` block at `WorkroomApp.swift:470`, **before** `gracefullyStopAllWindows` | synchronous |
| App backgrounded | `NSApplication.willResignActiveNotification`, registered in `applicationDidFinishLaunching` | debounced |

Both terminate hooks route through a new `WindowRegistry.flushSessions()`, so "which store writes" is answered in one place, next to `lastActiveStore` (`WindowRegistry.swift:41`), matching `gracefullyStopAllWindows` (`:199`).

**Crash tolerance:** worst case is ≤1s of layout change lost, or whatever happened since the last resign-active. The design must *not* depend on `applicationWillTerminate` for correctness — SIGKILL and libghostty EXC_BAD_ACCESS bypass it. The debounce is the primary mechanism; the flushes are belt-and-braces. (This also makes the XCUITest honest: it proves the debounce works, not just the terminate hook.)

### The apply point — the `ensureInitialTerminal` race

The race is real: `WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:95-100`'s `.task(id: target.id)` → `AppStore.ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:2280`) adds a tab when `tabCount == 0`. If restore lands after that, the user gets a stray "Terminal 1" beside their restored tabs.

Restore runs at the **end of `AppStore.apply(_:)`**, after `updateRootBranchWatches()` (`AppStore.swift:2538`). That is before any pane can mount, because a pane only mounts once `selectedTargetID` is non-nil and SwiftUI has rendered — which cannot happen inside `apply`'s synchronous body. And when it does mount, `tabCount != 0`, so `ensureInitialTerminal` is a no-op by its own existing guard. **No new coordination is needed** — that guard is already exactly right.

Placing it at the end (rather than between `validatedSelection` at `:2511` and `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` at `:2515`) keeps it self-contained: restore does its own leaf validation via `AppStore.target(for:)` (`:1110`), so it never interacts with `formerSelection` bookkeeping.

One-shot gating reuses the existing arbitration verbatim:

```swift
// AppStore.bootstrap(restore:) — AppStore.swift:2306, beside the existing pendingRestoreSelection clear
let shouldRestore = restore && projectStore.consumeInitialRestore()
pendingSessionRestore = shouldRestore          // ← added, before the fixture early-return
```

`apply` runs twice per bootstrap (`load("none")` then `load("fast")`, `:2321-2322`), so `restorePersistedSessionIfPending()` clears the flag on first call. A ⌘N window gets `shouldRestore == false` and restores nothing — matching `ProjectStore.consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`) exactly.

Fixture mode returns early from `bootstrap` (`:2310-2314`), so the same call goes into `loadFixture()` right after `projects = fixtures` (`:2371`). The fixture's own `terminals.ensureTab(for:)` calls guard on `orderByTarget[target.id] == nil` (`TerminalSessions.swift:459`), so restored targets are skipped automatically. (`UITestFixture.terminalTabs`'s unconditional `addTab` loop at `:2419` would stack on top — irrelevant, since no test sets both flags, but worth a comment.)

Writes are arbitrated by the existing `persistsSidebarPrefs` (`AppStore.swift:145`): only the last-active window persists. Same predicate, same reasoning, no second concept.

After restore: call `refreshSelectionHasTabs()` so the inspector reflects the restored tabs.

## 6. Terminal restore semantics and multi-window

### Eager model restore, lazy spawn — which is the current behaviour, unchanged

**Recommendation: restore every tab model eagerly; spawn nothing extra.**

Because `GhosttySurfaceView.init` is a bare NSView (§0.1) and only the visible workroom's visible panes mount, restoring 8 workrooms × 6 tabs costs 48 `NSView`s and **one to four shells** — precisely what you pay today when you click into a workroom. Adding a lazy-spawn layer would be building machinery the render tree already provides, plus a new state to get wrong.

What the user actually gets back per terminal: its **strip position, split position, size ratio, focus, title, and working directory**. Not scrollback — libghostty has no dump API. The cwd is the high-value half of "restore my terminal" anyway, and it's the part nobody else gives you.

### Multi-window: one session, owned by the last-active window

The smallest honest behaviour, and the only one available:

- **Capture:** the last-active window (`persistsSidebarPrefs`) writes its own session as `windows[0]`.
- **Restore:** the one window allowed by `consumeInitialRestore()` restores `windows.first`.

This is not a lie — it's *identical* to how `sidebarSelection`, `collapsedProjects`, and `workroomTabOrder` already behave across windows, and it matches the shipped reality that exactly one window opens at launch.

`windows` is an **array from day one** so growing to real per-window sessions is a data-compatible change, not a schema break. `windowKey` is nil today with a comment stating precisely what's missing: no window has cross-launch identity, because `WindowSeed.launch` mints a fresh UUID per access (`WorkroomApp.swift:90`), `RootWindow` takes `seed ?? .launch` (`:59`), and `attachWindow` sets `isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`) to deliberately suppress multi-window restore (`:968-970`). The growth path is concrete: persist a stable `WindowSeed.id`, re-enable window restoration, key `WindowSession.windowKey` on it. Writing all N windows' sessions *today* would capture data with no consumer and no way to get it back — that would be the dishonest version.

## 8. Test plan

### Unit (`WorkroomAppTests/`, `@testable import Workroom`)

No new test touches a shared `Defaults` key — the file store takes an injected temp URL, and restore never sets `selectedTargetID` (which would write `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` via its `didSet` at `AppStore.swift:161-165`). That keeps the whole suite clear of the `SharedPrefDefaultsTests` single-writer constraint.

**`SessionSnapshotCodecTests`** — the `GitHubReleaseDecodeTests` JSON-literal idiom:
- golden v1 JSON decodes to the expected snapshot (all four tab kinds, a nested split);
- **an unknown `kind` drops that tab and keeps its siblings** (the headline `@Lossy` guarantee);
- a truncated / malformed array element drops one element only;
- missing optional fields take their defaults;
- `schemaVersion: 999` → nil; `schemaVersion` absent → nil; garbage bytes → nil;
- `LayoutNode.materialize` with an unresolvable leaf collapses to the sibling; with <2 survivors returns nil; unknown orientation returns nil;
- round-trip byte stability (encode(decode(golden)) == golden) so a key rename can't slip through silently.

**`SessionCaptureTests`** — pure capture over a `TerminalSessions` built with the `makeView` factory seam (`TerminalSessionsTests.makeSessions()`, `TerminalSessionsTests.swift:12-16`): split tree keys line up with tab keys; focused key correct; preview flags and per-tab overrides preserved; **a run tab is excluded and its split leaf collapses**; `terminalCounter` captured.

**`SessionRestoreTests`** — apply a snapshot to a fresh `TerminalSessions`: tab count / order / split shape / focus; fresh unique ids; a nonexistent cwd falls back to `target.path`; `restore` fires no `onFocusChange`; ⌘T after restore continues the numbering.

**`SessionStoreTests`** — temp URL: write→read round trip; atomic replace leaves no partial file; unreadable → nil, no throw; a corrupt file is quarantined exactly once; `writeSynchronously` completes before returning.

---

# Issue #46 — Persist sessions (panels + layouts across restarts)

## 0. Corrections to the briefing

Most of the given context checks out. Five things need adjusting, and two of them change the design:

1. **`GhosttySurfaceView` construction is cheap — this is the load-bearing fact for eager-vs-lazy.** `init(workingDirectory:command:spawnsSurface:)` (`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156`) only builds an `NSView` + tracking area + scrollbar. The PTY and Metal surface are created in `createSurface()` (`:197`), reached from `viewDidMoveToWindow` or the explicit `ensureSurfaceCreated` (`:281`). And only visible panes mount: `WorkroomTerminalsView.contentLayout(active:)` (`.../Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:138`) renders the split *or* the single focused leaf, and `RootView.workroomSplitBody` (`.../Views/RootView.swift:645`) mounts only the visible workroom group. The codebase already relies on this — `AppStore.swift:2420-2423` says seeding N fixture targets "costs N tab models and one terminal". So **lazy spawn already exists by construction**; no new machinery is needed.

2. The reason a restored terminal is a fresh shell is **libghostty has no session dump**, not `canSpawnSurface` / torn-down views (`:195`). We never restore a torn-down view.

3. `apply(_:)` is declared at `AppStore.swift:2468`; `:2495` is the line *inside* it that consumes `pendingRestoreSelection` (captured from `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` at `AppStore.swift:839`), not `Defaults` directly.

4. `.task(id: target.id)` in `WorkroomTerminalsView.swift` is at **95–100**, not 96–101.

5. **There is a second, better terminate hook the brief missed**: the SIGTERM `DispatchSourceSignal` at `WorkroomApp.swift:464-478`. That is what `XCUIApplication.terminate()`, `make app-run`'s kill, and `pkill` actually hit — `applicationWillTerminate` (`:619`) only covers ⌘Q. Both need a flush.

One addition on multi-window: `WindowSeed.launch` is a **computed** `static var` minting a fresh UUID on every access (`WorkroomApp.swift:90`), and `RootWindow` takes `seed ?? .launch` (`:59`). Combined with `isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`), there is **no cross-launch window identity anywhere in the app today**.

---

## 1. Storage: a versioned JSON file in Application Support. Firm.

Not `Defaults`. The arguments, weighted:

**Decisive — blast radius.** This app's known crash mode is libghostty surface teardown; `WorkroomApp.swift:606-617` is an entire comment about not freeing surfaces on quit because it crashes. A session blob in UserDefaults shares one plist with `themeFamily`, `runCommands`, `workroomLabels`, `releaseChannel`, `switcher*Modifier`, `lastSeenVersion`. A corrupted or partially-flushed domain takes **all of them**. A separate file loses only the session. That asymmetry alone settles it.

**Decisive — schema evolution.** The house pattern for versioning a `Defaults` key is to version the *key string* (`inspector.layout.v2`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:175`) plus discard-on-shape-mismatch (`reconcileInspectorState`, `AppStore.swift:4209`). That's correct for a 4-bool preference. For a user's 40-tab layout, "silently throw it away on every schema bump" is the wrong default and a bad habit to build in. A file gets a real `schemaVersion` int, real migrations, and **element-granular** degradation.

**Debuggability.** "Delete `~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<bundle id>/session.json` and relaunch" is a support instruction a user can follow, and a file a bug report can attach. `defaults read com.developwithstyle.workroom` dumps every preference the app has.

**Size/shape.** 8 workrooms × 6 tabs with paths ≈ 20–40 KB. Not fatal in UserDefaults, but it's the wrong shape for a store designed for scalar preferences, and it rides `cfprefsd`'s whole-domain sync.

**Atomicity.** `Data.write(to:options:.atomic)` is a rename(2): the file on disk is always a complete old or complete new document. UserDefaults gives no per-key equivalent and `synchronize()` is deprecated.

**Test hygiene (underrated).** `SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift:10-19` documents that parallel test workers share one UserDefaults domain, so a whole class exists purely to serialise writes to three keys. An injectable file URL sidesteps that entirely — the new unit tests touch **zero** shared Defaults keys.

**The one real cost, and its price.** A file does *not* get the per-bundle-id domain separation that makes `Workroom`, `Workroom Dev`, and `Workroom Nightly` coexist (macapp/CLAUDE.md "Gotchas"). `GhosttyApp.themeConfigURL` (`Core/GhosttyApp.swift:217-223`) already writes `Application Support/Workroom/ghostty.conf` from all three identities. Without buying that back, a Debug run's fixture temp-dir workrooms would be restored into the release build. **So the path is scoped by bundle id:**

```
~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier>/session.json
```

Second cost: a new IO surface (permissions, disk full). Mitigation is a hard rule — **every read and write is best-effort; the app must behave identically with the file absent, empty, or unreadable.** Failures log via `Logger(subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "session")` (the `GhosttyApp.swift:39` / `LibGit2.swift:28` pattern) and are never surfaced.

---

## 2. The schema

New file `WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift`. **Every type here is a hand-written mirror.** No runtime type gains `Codable`.

```swift
struct SessionFile: Codable, Sendable {
  static let currentSchemaVersion = 1
  var schemaVersion: Int
  var savedAt: Date
  var appVersion: String?              // diagnostics only, never branched on
  @Lossy var windows: [WindowSession]  // exactly one today — the growth seam (§6)
}

struct WindowSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// Reserved for per-window restore. Always nil today: no window has a cross-launch identity
  /// (`WindowSeed.launch` mints a fresh UUID per access, `isRestorable = false`). See §6.
  var windowKey: String?
  @Lossy var targets: [TargetSession]
  /// `AppStore.workroomSplits` — leaves are `TerminalTarget.ID` strings.
  @Lossy var workroomSplits: [LayoutNode<String>]
  /// `AppStore.expandedTerminalTargets`.
  var expandedTargets: [String]?
}

struct TargetSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// `TerminalTarget.ID`: "wr|<project>|<name>" or "root|<project>".
  var targetID: String
  @Lossy var tabs: [TabSession]      // strip order; `key` is the address space
  var split: LayoutNode<String>?     // leaves are TabSession.key
  var focusedKey: String?
  var terminalCounter: Int?          // TerminalSessions.counts — keeps "Terminal 7" going
}

struct TabSession: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  /// Unique *within this TargetSession*. Sourced from the runtime `TerminalTab.ID.uuidString`
  /// at capture time purely because it's already unique — it is NOT a cross-launch identity
  /// (restore mints fresh runtime ids; see §3).
  var key: String
  var kind: String                   // "terminal" | "diff" | "file" | "changeset"
  var terminal: TerminalPayload?
  var diff: DiffPayload?
  var file: FilePayload?
  var changeset: ChangesetPayload?
}

struct TerminalPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var defaultTitle: String   // "Terminal 3" — NOT the live OSC title (see below)
  var cwd: String?           // last reported cwd; validated at restore
}
struct DiffPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var path: String
  var change: String                 // ChangedFile.Change.rawValue — already a String raw enum
  var source: DiffSourcePayload
  var isPreview: Bool
  var viewMode: String?              // TerminalTab.diffViewModeOverride
}
struct DiffSourcePayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var kind: String                   // "gitWorktree"|"jjWorkingCopy"|"jjParent"|"commit"
  var commit: String?
}
struct FilePayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var path: String; var isPreview: Bool; var markdownPreview: Bool?
}
struct ChangesetPayload: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var commitID: String; var title: String; var isPreview: Bool; var selectedPath: String?
}

/// The Codable mirror of `PaneLayout`, generic over its leaf address. Hand-written with an explicit
/// `kind` discriminator so the on-disk format is a contract THIS file owns — not whatever Swift's
/// synthesized Codable emits for an indirect enum with associated values.
indirect enum LayoutNode<Leaf: Codable & Hashable & Sendable>: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
  case leaf(Leaf)
  case split(orientation: String, ratio: Double, first: LayoutNode, second: LayoutNode)
}
```

**Deliberate omissions, each with a reason:**

- **`liveTitle` / `progressActive`.** A restored shell is a fresh process; a persisted live title is a lie the strip would keep telling. Also the churniest field in the model — excluding it is what makes the save digest (§5) stable.
- **`PaneLayout.split`'s `id: UUID`.** Nothing outside the tree references it across a launch (it only addresses a divider during a drag). Minted fresh at restore.
- **Run tabs.** A restored run tab would resurrect a dev server with no `AppStore.RunState` behind it — an untracked process orphaned on a port, exactly the failure `AppStore.swift:886-894` and `Core/WindowRegistry.swift:187` exist to prevent. Skipped at capture via `tab.surface?.isRunCommandSurface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:821`). `Defaults[.runCommands]` already survives, and ⌘R is one keystroke.
- **`selectedTargetID`.** Already owned by `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:109`), restored via `pendingRestoreSelection` (`AppStore.swift:839`, `:2495`), and covered by `SelectionTests`. Putting it in the snapshot too would give one value two homes — the exact failure mode `NavPayload`'s doc (`TerminalSessions.swift:135-137`) and `ProjectStore.ghAuthCache` (`ProjectStore.swift:38-40`) are written against. The snapshot owns **panels and layouts**; Defaults owns **which workroom**. They're orthogonal.
- **Scrollback.** libghostty exposes no session dump. Say so in the doc comment rather than letting a reader assume it was forgotten.

**No new id format ships.** `TerminalTarget.ID` strings are already the persisted encoding of `sidebarSelection` and `workroomTabOrder`. `SidebarID` round-trips through the existing pure pair `AppStore.targetIDString(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:4253`) and `AppStore.sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)` (`:4172`) — both `nonisolated static`, both already unit-tested, and the second already resolves stale ids to nil. That is the whole answer to "how does `SidebarID` become encodable": **it doesn't.**

### Degradation rules

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| File missing / unreadable | No restore, no error. Fresh-install path. |
| Envelope undecodable | Discard. Move once to `session.corrupt.json` (replacing any prior) so a bug report has something to attach, then start clean. |
| `schemaVersion > current` (downgrade) | Ignore, restore nothing. Overwritten on next save — accepted one-time loss for a rare developer scenario. |
| `schemaVersion < current` | Run migrations; no migration for that version ⇒ discard. |
| An element in a `@Lossy` array fails | **Drop that element, keep the rest.** |
| Unknown `TabSession.kind` | Decodes structurally, rejected at materialise ⇒ one tab dropped. |
| Layout leaf resolves to nothing | Node collapses to its sibling (`removingLeaf` semantics); result with <2 leaves ⇒ no split, tabs kept. |
| Unknown orientation string | Reject that target's whole split; keep its tabs. |
| Target no longer resolves | Whole `TargetSession` dropped (via `AppStore.target(for:)`). |

`@Lossy` is the single most valuable primitive here — ~20 lines decoding through an `UnkeyedDecodingContainer` element by element, skipping throws. It is what turns "a newer build wrote a fifth tab kind" from *your whole session is gone* into *one tab is missing*.

**This is exactly why tabs are keyed, not index-addressed.** Index addressing plus a lossy array is a silent corruption bug: drop tab 2 of 5 and every later split leaf points at the wrong tab. Keys are drop-safe and self-validating.

**Forward-compat rules, written into the file header:** new fields are always optional with a safe default; removed fields decode as optional and are ignored; unknown fields are **not** round-tripped (an older build saving over a newer one's file drops them). That's the cheap 95%; say it out loud rather than implying more.

---

## 3. Keeping `PaneLayout` and the runtime model clean

`Models/PaneLayout.swift` is **untouched**. `TerminalSessions.TerminalTab` is **untouched** — no id-taking init, no `Codable`.

Two pure conversions live in `SessionSnapshot.swift`:

```swift
extension LayoutNode {
  /// Runtime tree → snapshot tree. `address` maps a runtime leaf to its persisted key; a leaf that
  /// maps to nil is dropped and its parent collapses to the sibling.
  static func capture<L: Hashable>(_ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?) -> LayoutNode?

  /// Snapshot tree → runtime tree. `resolve` maps a persisted key to a live leaf; unresolvable
  /// leaves collapse. Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive — the "a lone leaf is not a
  /// split" invariant (`PaneLayout.swift:18`) enforced at the boundary, not left to the caller.
  func materialize<L: Hashable>(_ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?) -> PaneLayout<L>?
}
```

`materialize` mints a fresh `UUID()` per split node and pushes `ratio` through the existing `PaneRatio.sanitize` (`PaneLayout.swift:48`). Both functions are `nonisolated`, ~20 lines each, and directly unit-testable — the `AppStore.reconcileInspectorState` (`AppStore.swift:4209`) and `WindowRegistry.cyclePlan` (`WindowRegistry.swift:167`) idiom.

**Tab identity across a launch: it doesn't survive, on purpose.** `let id = UUID()` (`TerminalSessions.swift:15`) carries a live invariant — a tab id is minted once, in-process, and is unique across *windows*; `WindowRegistry.ownerOf(tabID:)` (`WindowRegistry.swift:132`), the notification spine, `SwitcherRecency`, `NavigationHistory`, and `runStates` all lean on it. Restoring persisted UUIDs would put a duplicate-id hazard one bug away (two windows restoring one snapshot) for zero benefit: nothing outside the snapshot refers to a pre-launch tab id. So restore **mints fresh ids and rewires order/split/focus through a `[persistedKey: TerminalTab.ID]` map**. `TerminalTab` needs no change at all.

---

## 4. Where capture and restore live

Asymmetric, for a concrete reason: Swift `private` is file-scoped, and `tabsByTarget` / `orderByTarget` / `splitByTarget` / `focusedTabByTarget` are `@Published private` (`TerminalSessions.swift:251-258`).

- **Capture** reads only through existing public queries — `activeTargetIDs` (`:401`), `displayedTabIDs(for:)` (`:368`), `tabs(for:)` (`:382`), `split(for:)` (`:412`), `focusedTab(for:)` (`:429`) — plus one new accessor for `counts` (`:264`). So it goes in `SessionSnapshot.swift` as a `@MainActor` free function.
  - Capturing `displayedTabIDs` (display order) rather than the loose `orderByTarget` is safe and avoids widening the class's surface: display normalisation is a fixed point (re-normalising an already-normalised order is identity), so it round-trips visually. Worth a one-line comment.
- **Restore** mutates the private state and needs `setFocused(_:for:notify:)` (`:974`), so it goes **inside `TerminalSessions.swift`** under a new `// MARK: Session restore (issue #46)`, beside the mutation primitives it mirrors. ~80 lines on a 1337-line file.

```swift
/// Re-materialise a persisted session for ONE target. Tabs get FRESH ids (see §3); order, split and
/// focus are rewired through the persisted keys. Focus is set with `notify: false` — a restore is not
/// a navigation, and `AppStore` has not resolved its selection yet, so firing `onFocusChange` here
/// would seed back/forward with a place the user never went.
@discardableResult
func restore(_ session: TargetSession, for target: TerminalTarget) -> Int
```

Terminal tabs are built through the existing `makeTerminalTab(for:cwd:command:title:)` (`:1277`) so every surface callback (`onActivity`, `onTitleChange`, `onCwdChange`, `onCommandFinished`, `onProgressReport`, `onFocused`, `onCmdClickFile`, `onOpenURL`) is wired identically to a live tab — no second wiring site to drift. `command:` is always nil (run tabs aren't restored). After building, `counts[target.id]` is set to `max(persisted, built)`.

**cwd validation** is a pure static so it's testable: persisted cwd if `FileManager.fileExists(atPath:isDirectory:)` says it's a live directory, else `target.path`. A dead cwd would otherwise make libghostty's spawn fail on a restored tab.

## 5. Save triggers, and the exact apply point

### The dirty hook — by construction, not by enumeration

Sink on `terminals.objectWillChange` (the `projectStoreObservation` pattern, `AppStore.swift:824`), plus explicit `didSet` marks on `workroomSplits` (`:265`) and `expandedTerminalTargets` (`:271`).

Hooking `objectWillChange` rather than adding `onSessionChanged?()` at the ~12 mutation sites in `TerminalSessions` is deliberate: it **cannot be forgotten** when a thirteenth mutation lands. That's the same value the codebase already buys with exhaustive switches ("a fifth content kind must be a compile error in ONE place", `TerminalSessions.swift:126-128`).

**Trap to write down:** `objectWillChange` fires *before* the mutation. Capture must therefore always be scheduled, never inline.

Cost control, both required:
- **Debounce 1s** on the main queue (`DispatchWorkItem`, cancel-and-replace).
- **Digest guard.** `WindowSession` is `Hashable`; compare `hashValue` against the last written one and skip identical writes. Because `liveTitle`/`progressActive` are excluded from the schema, a `claude` session animating its title 10×/s produces one cheap snapshot build + hash per second and **zero** disk writes.
- **`savedAt` must be outside the digest** — hash `WindowSession`, not `SessionFile`, or the guard never fires.

Encoding + writing happens on the store's serial `DispatchQueue` (`qos: .utility`); only the snapshot build is on the main actor.

### Flush points

| Hook | Location | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| ⌘Q / Quit Apple-event | `AppDelegate.applicationWillTerminate`, `WorkroomApp.swift:619` (currently empty) | synchronous |
| SIGTERM (`XCUIApplication.terminate()`, `make app-run`, `pkill`, logout) | inside the `MainActor.assumeIsolated` block at `WorkroomApp.swift:470`, **before** `gracefullyStopAllWindows` | synchronous |
| App backgrounded | `NSApplication.willResignActiveNotification`, registered in `applicationDidFinishLaunching` | debounced |

Both terminate hooks route through a new `WindowRegistry.flushSessions()`, so "which store writes" is answered in one place, next to `lastActiveStore` (`WindowRegistry.swift:41`), matching `gracefullyStopAllWindows` (`:199`).

**Crash tolerance:** worst case is ≤1s of layout change lost, or whatever happened since the last resign-active. The design must *not* depend on `applicationWillTerminate` for correctness — SIGKILL and libghostty EXC_BAD_ACCESS bypass it. The debounce is the primary mechanism; the flushes are belt-and-braces. (This also makes the XCUITest honest: it proves the debounce works, not just the terminate hook.)

### The apply point — the `ensureInitialTerminal` race

The race is real: `WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:95-100`'s `.task(id: target.id)` → `AppStore.ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:2280`) adds a tab when `tabCount == 0`. If restore lands after that, the user gets a stray "Terminal 1" beside their restored tabs.

Restore runs at the **end of `AppStore.apply(_:)`**, after `updateRootBranchWatches()` (`AppStore.swift:2538`). That is before any pane can mount, because a pane only mounts once `selectedTargetID` is non-nil and SwiftUI has rendered — which cannot happen inside `apply`'s synchronous body. And when it does mount, `tabCount != 0`, so `ensureInitialTerminal` is a no-op by its own existing guard. **No new coordination is needed** — that guard is already exactly right.

Placing it at the end (rather than between `validatedSelection` at `:2511` and `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` at `:2515`) keeps it self-contained: restore does its own leaf validation via `AppStore.target(for:)` (`:1110`), so it never interacts with `formerSelection` bookkeeping.

One-shot gating reuses the existing arbitration verbatim:

```swift
// AppStore.bootstrap(restore:) — AppStore.swift:2306, beside the existing pendingRestoreSelection clear
let shouldRestore = restore && projectStore.consumeInitialRestore()
pendingSessionRestore = shouldRestore          // ← added, before the fixture early-return
```

`apply` runs twice per bootstrap (`load("none")` then `load("fast")`, `:2321-2322`), so `restorePersistedSessionIfPending()` clears the flag on first call. A ⌘N window gets `shouldRestore == false` and restores nothing — matching `ProjectStore.consumeInitialRestore()` (`ProjectStore.swift:84`) exactly.

Fixture mode returns early from `bootstrap` (`:2310-2314`), so the same call goes into `loadFixture()` right after `projects = fixtures` (`:2371`). The fixture's own `terminals.ensureTab(for:)` calls guard on `orderByTarget[target.id] == nil` (`TerminalSessions.swift:459`), so restored targets are skipped automatically. (`UITestFixture.terminalTabs`'s unconditional `addTab` loop at `:2419` would stack on top — irrelevant, since no test sets both flags, but worth a comment.)

Writes are arbitrated by the existing `persistsSidebarPrefs` (`AppStore.swift:145`): only the last-active window persists. Same predicate, same reasoning, no second concept.

After restore: call `refreshSelectionHasTabs()` so the inspector reflects the restored tabs.

## 6. Terminal restore semantics and multi-window

### Eager model restore, lazy spawn — which is the current behaviour, unchanged

**Recommendation: restore every tab model eagerly; spawn nothing extra.**

Because `GhosttySurfaceView.init` is a bare NSView (§0.1) and only the visible workroom's visible panes mount, restoring 8 workrooms × 6 tabs costs 48 `NSView`s and **one to four shells** — precisely what you pay today when you click into a workroom. Adding a lazy-spawn layer would be building machinery the render tree already provides, plus a new state to get wrong.

What the user actually gets back per terminal: its **strip position, split position, size ratio, focus, title, and working directory**. Not scrollback — libghostty has no dump API. The cwd is the high-value half of "restore my terminal" anyway, and it's the part nobody else gives you.

### Multi-window: one session, owned by the last-active window

The smallest honest behaviour, and the only one available:

- **Capture:** the last-active window (`persistsSidebarPrefs`) writes its own session as `windows[0]`.
- **Restore:** the one window allowed by `consumeInitialRestore()` restores `windows.first`.

This is not a lie — it's *identical* to how `sidebarSelection`, `collapsedProjects`, and `workroomTabOrder` already behave across windows, and it matches the shipped reality that exactly one window opens at launch.

`windows` is an **array from day one** so growing to real per-window sessions is a data-compatible change, not a schema break. `windowKey` is nil today with a comment stating precisely what's missing: no window has cross-launch identity, because `WindowSeed.launch` mints a fresh UUID per access (`WorkroomApp.swift:90`), `RootWindow` takes `seed ?? .launch` (`:59`), and `attachWindow` sets `isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`) to deliberately suppress multi-window restore (`:968-970`). The growth path is concrete: persist a stable `WindowSeed.id`, re-enable window restoration, key `WindowSession.windowKey` on it. Writing all N windows' sessions *today* would capture data with no consumer and no way to get it back — that would be the dishonest version.

## 8. Test plan

### Unit (`WorkroomAppTests/`, `@testable import Workroom`)

No new test touches a shared `Defaults` key — the file store takes an injected temp URL, and restore never sets `selectedTargetID` (which would write `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` via its `didSet` at `AppStore.swift:161-165`). That keeps the whole suite clear of the `SharedPrefDefaultsTests` single-writer constraint.

**`SessionSnapshotCodecTests`** — the `GitHubReleaseDecodeTests` JSON-literal idiom:
- golden v1 JSON decodes to the expected snapshot (all four tab kinds, a nested split);
- **an unknown `kind` drops that tab and keeps its siblings** (the headline `@Lossy` guarantee);
- a truncated / malformed array element drops one element only;
- missing optional fields take their defaults;
- `schemaVersion: 999` → nil; `schemaVersion` absent → nil; garbage bytes → nil;
- `LayoutNode.materialize` with an unresolvable leaf collapses to the sibling; with <2 survivors returns nil; unknown orientation returns nil;
- round-trip byte stability (encode(decode(golden)) == golden) so a key rename can't slip through silently.

**`SessionCaptureTests`** — pure capture over a `TerminalSessions` built with the `makeView` factory seam (`TerminalSessionsTests.makeSessions()`, `TerminalSessionsTests.swift:12-16`): split tree keys line up with tab keys; focused key correct; preview flags and per-tab overrides preserved; **a run tab is excluded and its split leaf collapses**; `terminalCounter` captured.

**`SessionRestoreTests`** — apply a snapshot to a fresh `TerminalSessions`: tab count / order / split shape / focus; fresh unique ids; a nonexistent cwd falls back to `target.path`; `restore` fires no `onFocusChange`; ⌘T after restore continues the numbering.

**`SessionStoreTests`** — temp URL: write→read round trip; atomic replace leaves no partial file; unreadable → nil, no throw; a corrupt file is quarantined exactly once; `writeSynchronously` completes before returning.

**`AppStoreSessionRestoreTests`** — `apply` twice restores once; a second `AppStore` sharing one `ProjectStore` restores nothing (the `MultiWindowTests.testIsolatedStoresDoNotShareProjects` idiom); a `TargetSession` for a deleted workroom is dropped; **after restore, `ensureInitialTerminal(for:)` adds no tab** (the direct regression test for the `WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:95` race).

## 9. Risks worth naming up front

- **The Dev/Release shared-directory trap.** The single most likely way to ship this broken. Bundle-id scoping (§1) is mandatory, not tidiness.
- **`objectWillChange` fires pre-mutation.** Always schedule; never capture inline.
- **`savedAt` inside the digest** silently disables the write guard. Hash `WindowSession`.
- **Restoring run tabs** would orphan dev servers on ports. Excluded by design; assert it in `SessionCaptureTests`.
- **Index-addressed tabs + lossy arrays** silently mis-wire splits. Keyed addressing exists to prevent this — don't "simplify" it back to indices later.
- **Stale content targets** (a `.commit(id)` rebased away, a deleted file) already degrade correctly: `DiffViewer.swift:143` renders "Diff unavailable", `PlainFileViewer.swift:129` renders "File unavailable", and `AppStore.refreshOpenDiffChangeKinds` (`AppStore.swift:3865`) self-heals a stale `change` off the status sweep. Nothing new needed — worth a comment so a future reader doesn't add a redundant validation pass.
- **Free side effect to sanity-check:** with more targets active at launch, `Defaults[.workroomTabOrder]` starts doing real work through `orderedActiveTargets` (`AppStore.swift:4271`). Expected and desirable — but eyeball the workroom tab bar after a restore during step 3 review.

# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the orange-badged `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The three app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  all of them) share the yellow blocked mark; Dev and Nightly overlay their channel labels.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework). The embedding C API
  is not yet stable, so the pin is EXACT — don't float it. **`project.yml` is the single source of
  truth for which package version and which ghostty engine we ship** — read the comment there rather
  than trusting a version quoted anywhere else, and note the trap it documents: the package versions
  itself independently of ghostty, so package `1.3.1` is not ghostty `v1.3.1`. Bumping it is not a
  one-line change (see "Bump the libghostty pin" in `TODOS.md`). The terminal surface
  (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the
  bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo + shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.
- **⌥Tab / ⌃Tab (the quick switchers, issue #132) are monitor-only and deliberately NOT in
  `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut`.** That list is static, but whether the app owns Tab depends on
  runtime state: a workroom with one pane has nothing to switch to, so ⌃Tab must reach the TUI. The
  monitor branch consumes the event only when a switch actually happened, exactly as ⌥⌘digit and
  ⌥⌘arrows already do — same reasoning as the unreserved ⌃⌘arrows. `AppShortcutReservationTests` pins
  Tab as never-reserved so a later "defence in depth" edit can't take `<C-Tab>` from every TUI. Both
  trigger modifiers are `Defaults` keys (`switcher*Modifier`) because a global-hotkey grabber
  (AltTab, HyperSwitch, Contexts all bind ⌥Tab) intercepts upstream of `NSApp.sendEvent`, where no
  local monitor can see the key and no API can detect the conflict.
  The Go menu's **Last-Used Workroom / Last-Used Pane** items carry the same key equivalents purely so
  macOS renders and teaches them (and so the feature is mouse-reachable) — the monitor still owns the
  keystroke, since it runs ahead of menu dispatch and consumes the event whenever it switched. Their
  enablement is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic: a disabled item drops its key equivalent, which is
  what stops the menu eating a Tab the monitor deliberately passed through. Their action resolves the
  store from the **key window** (`QuickSwitcher.stepFromKeyWindow`), not from the `Commands` body's
  focused store, which outlives an aux window becoming key.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, labelled
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

options.label: JSON file in App Support (Recommended)
options.description: ~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<bundle-id>/session.json, versioned + atomic write. Bundle-id scoped so Dev/Nightly/Release don't cross-restore. Per-element lossy decode (one bad tab drops, rest survive), real migrations, deletable for support, and unit tests inject a temp URL — sidestepping the shared-UserDefaults-domain single-writer rule SharedPrefDefaultsTests documents. Costs ~80 lines of store + IO error handling.

options.label: Defaults key (session.snapshot.v1)
options.description: One Codable blob beside every other persisted pref in DefaultsKeys.swift. Least new code, free bundle-id separation, no IO to fail. But a 20-40KB layout blob rides the same plist as themeFamily/runCommands, versioning means discarding the whole session on any schema bump, and every session test joins the shared-domain single-writer constraint.

options.label: One window, panels only (Recommended)
options.description: Keeps today's deliberate design: exactly one window opens at launch (isRestorable = false, AppStore.swift:971), and it rehydrates its panels. The last-active window writes the snapshot — same arbitration as sidebarSelection/collapsedProjects already use. Snapshot schema keeps a windows[] array so real multi-window restore is a data-compatible follow-up, not a schema break.

options.label: Reopen every window that was open at quit
options.description: Bigger feature: needs a stable cross-launch window identity (WindowSeed.launch mints a fresh UUID per access), reversing isRestorable = false, and per-window snapshot keying. More surface for the multi-window bugs #70 was about.
