89	  // MARK: Saved session (issue #46)
90	
91	  /// Windows from the saved session that no window has adopted yet. Loaded once, lazily, by the first
92	  /// claim — which is also the moment saves are suspended, so a restoring window cannot overwrite the
93	  /// file before the rest of it has been claimed.
94	  private var unclaimedSessionWindows: [WindowSession] = []
95	  private var didLoadSession = false
96	  /// Injectable so tests drive a temp session file instead of the developer's real one.
97	  var sessionCoordinator: SessionCoordinator = .shared
98	  /// True between loading the session and finishing the restore, so the suspend/resume is balanced
99	  /// exactly once however many windows take part.
100	  private var isRestoringSession = false
101	
102	  /// Sessions already handed to a window, by the key that window now owns. Makes claiming idempotent:
103	  /// `WindowAccessor` can resolve the same window more than once, and a repeat claim must return the
104	  /// same session rather than consume a second one.
105	  private var claimedSessions: [UUID: WindowSession] = [:]
106	  /// Keys handed to `openWindow` whose window has not claimed yet. Dispatched once so a `.task`
107	  /// re-fire cannot open a second copy of the same window.
108	  private var dispatchedSessionKeys: Set<UUID> = []
109	  /// How many windows have claimed a session and not yet finished restoring it. Saving resumes when
110	  /// this reaches zero AND nothing is still awaiting a window.
111	  private var outstandingRestores = 0
112	  /// The key of the window that was key at the last quit, so focus lands where the user left it once
113	  /// every window is back.
114	  private var keyWindowSessionKey: UUID?
115	
116	  /// Adopt a saved window for this store, or nil when there is nothing to adopt.
117	  ///
118	  /// Loading is lazy so the read happens at the first claim rather than at app init — the claim is
119	  /// made from `AppStore.attachWindow`, when a real `NSWindow` exists but before it is shown, which is
120	  /// both early enough for the frame and late enough that a speculative SwiftUI view init cannot
121	  /// consume a session no window ever uses.
122	  ///
123	  /// The launch window adopts the first unclaimed session (its own seed id is freshly minted, so it
124	  /// cannot match anything on disk) and takes that session's key as its own. A sibling was opened FOR
125	  /// a specific key and claims exactly that one — never another window's.
126	  func claimSession(for key: UUID, isLaunchWindow: Bool) -> WindowSession? {
127	    loadSessionIfNeeded()
128	    if let already = claimedSessions[key] { return already }
129	
130	    let claimed: WindowSession?
131	    if isLaunchWindow {
132	      claimed = unclaimedSessionWindows.isEmpty ? nil : unclaimedSessionWindows.removeFirst()
133	    } else if let index = unclaimedSessionWindows.firstIndex(
134	      where: { $0.windowKey == key.uuidString })
135	    {
136	      claimed = unclaimedSessionWindows.remove(at: index)
137	    } else {
138	      claimed = nil
139	    }
140	
141	    guard let claimed else { return nil }
142	    let ownedKey = UUID(uuidString: claimed.windowKey) ?? key
143	    claimedSessions[ownedKey] = claimed
144	    dispatchedSessionKeys.remove(ownedKey)
145	    outstandingRestores += 1
146	    if claimed.isKey { keyWindowSessionKey = ownedKey }
147	    return claimed
148	  }
149	
150	  /// Keys of saved windows nobody has claimed yet, marked as dispatched so they are handed out once.
151	  /// The launch window opens one window per key.
152	  func pendingSessionKeys() -> [UUID] {
153	    loadSessionIfNeeded()
154	    let keys = unclaimedSessionWindows.compactMap { UUID(uuidString: $0.windowKey) }
155	      .filter { !dispatchedSessionKeys.contains($0) }
156	    dispatchedSessionKeys.formUnion(keys)
157	    return keys
158	  }
159	
160	  /// One window finished restoring. Saving resumes only once every window has, so a half-restored
161	  /// document is never written over a full one.
162	  ///
163	  /// The `unclaimedSessionWindows` check is load-bearing, not belt and braces: the launch window
164	  /// finishes its own restore INSIDE `bootstrap`, which returns before `pendingSessionKeys` has handed
165	  /// anything out. Ending the restore on "nothing outstanding, nothing dispatched" alone would
166	  /// therefore fire while the siblings were still only on disk — clearing them, so the fan-out found
167	  /// nothing to open and only one window ever came back.
168	  func finishSessionRestore() {
169	    guard isRestoringSession else { return }
170	    outstandingRestores = max(0, outstandingRestores - 1)
171	    guard outstandingRestores == 0, dispatchedSessionKeys.isEmpty,
172	      unclaimedSessionWindows.isEmpty
173	    else { return }
174	    endSessionRestore()
175	  }
176	
177	  /// Bring the window that was key at the last quit back to the front, then resume saving.
178	  ///
179	  /// `timedOut` is the watchdog calling, and it changes the ending: see below.
180	  private func endSessionRestore(timedOut: Bool = false) {
181	    guard isRestoringSession else { return }
182	    // **A restore that never finished must not resume saving.** `AppStore.load` swallows a CLI
183	    // failure and returns WITHOUT calling `apply`, so `restorePersistedSessionIfPending` never runs
184	    // and this window's restore stays outstanding forever. Resuming here would then rebuild the
185	    // document from a window holding nothing and overwrite the file — one `workroom list` timing out
186	    // on a cold machine would silently destroy the user's whole saved session, ~16 seconds into a
187	    // launch that was supposed to bring it back. Freezing keeps the file intact for the next launch.
188	    let incomplete = outstandingRestores > 0 || !unclaimedSessionWindows.isEmpty
189	    isRestoringSession = false
190	    unclaimedSessionWindows.removeAll()
191	    dispatchedSessionKeys.removeAll()
192	    claimedSessions.removeAll()
193	    keyWindowSessionKey = timedOut && incomplete ? nil : keyWindowSessionKey
194	    if timedOut && incomplete {
195	      sessionCoordinator.freezeWithoutWriting()
196	      return
197	    }
198	    if let keyWindowSessionKey,
199	      let store = WindowRegistry.shared.allStores.first(where: {
200	        $0.sessionKey == keyWindowSessionKey
201	      })
202	    {
203	      store.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
204	    }
205	    keyWindowSessionKey = nil
206	    sessionCoordinator.resumeSaves()
207	  }
208	
209	  private func loadSessionIfNeeded() {
210	    guard !didLoadSession else { return }
211	    didLoadSession = true
212	    guard case .restored(let file, _) = sessionCoordinator.read() else { return }
213	    unclaimedSessionWindows = file.windows
214	    isRestoringSession = true
215	    // Suspended until `finishSessionRestore`. Without this the first window's restore marks the
216	    // session dirty, and that write would rebuild the document from the windows that exist SO FAR —
217	    // overwriting the file and discarding the ones still to be claimed.
218	    sessionCoordinator.suspendSaves()
219	    // Watchdog: a dispatched window that never opens (a scene SwiftUI declines to create, a window
220	    // closed mid-restore) would otherwise leave saving suspended for the whole run — the app would
221	    // silently stop persisting anything. Restoring is a launch-time operation measured in
222	    // milliseconds, so anything still outstanding this much later is not coming.
223	    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + sessionRestoreTimeout) { [weak self] in
224	      MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.endSessionRestore(timedOut: true) }

input.content:
# Issue #145 — Offer to resume an agent session in a restored pane

## Context

After #46 a restored pane is inert: right workroom, right directory, dead shell. If you were
mid-conversation with Claude or Codex, that conversation still exists in the agent's own store.
#145 offers a one-click route back to it, at restore time only, spawning nothing at launch.

The issue is already well specified. This plan does three things the issue does not: it **corrects
four factual claims** that turn out to be wrong or incomplete against the actual code and the actual
agent stores on disk, it **makes three decisions the issue left implicit**, and it sequences the
work.

---

## Verified facts (checked 2026-08-09, not assumed)

| Claim in #145 | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| libghostty exposes no child pid / pty fd | ✅ **true** | `DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/include/ghostty.h` — the only child-process symbol is `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s` (line 824). No pid, no fd. |
| Codex rollout line 1 is a `session_meta` record carrying `cwd` | ✅ **true** | `head -1` of a real rollout: `{payload, timestamp, type}`, `type == "session_meta"`, `payload` has `cwd`. |
| Codex sessions live at `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` | ✅ **true** | Verified 2026/03…2026/08 date tree. |
| `claude --resume` is a picker; `--continue` resumes in-cwd | ✅ **true** | `claude --help`: `-r, --resume [value]`, `-c, --continue`. |
| `codex resume` is a picker; `--last` skips it | ✅ **true** | `codex resume --help`: "picker by default; use `--last` to continue the most recent". |
| `TerminalAgentBanner` + `AgentBannerViewModel` exist, reuse them | ⚠️ **half true** | They exist. But see **C1** and **C2** — reusing them as-is is a bug, not a shortcut. |
| Claude slug = cwd with `/` replaced by `-` | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C3**. `.` is also replaced. |
| `SessionFile.savedAt` "gives the recency window with no new state" | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C4**. It is persisted but thrown away at load. |

### C1 — `AgentBannerState` is failure-shaped, and there is one slot per tab

`AgentBannerState` (`Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29`) has five cases and **every one carries a
`FailedCommand`**. Its accessor is not optional:

```swift
var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?)
```

`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` destructures that non-optional tuple. A resume offer has
no failed command, so adding a sixth case forces either a fake `FailedCommand` (lying to the
Investigate path) or a signature change with a real call-site.

Worse, the store is single-slot:

```swift
@Published private(set) var banners: [TerminalTab.ID: AgentBannerState] = [:]
```

So a resume offer and a diagnosis **evict each other**. Concretely, with the issue's design as
written: restored pane shows *Resume Claude…*; the user runs `npm test`; it fails;
`commandFinished` calls `setBanner(.awaitingDiagnose(...))` and the resume offer is gone for good.
The reverse also happens — discovery is async by design, so a late offer can stomp a live
`.loading` diagnosis mid-run.

**This is the single biggest thing the issue gets wrong.** "Reuse it" reads as free; it is not.

### C2 — The "banner" is a red status-bar chip behind a popover

`TerminalStatusBar.swift:9` is explicit: *"The diagnosis is a compact indicator that opens the full
`TerminalAgentBanner` in a POPOVER — not an overlay"* (a SwiftUI overlay loses hit-testing to the
terminal's Metal `NSView`). The chip is tinted by `diagnosisTint`, which maps `.awaiting` to
`theme.tokens.failure` — **red** — with `.help("Show the agent's diagnosis")` and a tab-strip badge
at `TerminalTabStrip.swift:149`.

Rendering a Resume offer through that path produces a red, failure-coloured chip labelled as a
diagnosis, that you must click to discover an offer you never asked for. Wrong on colour semantics,
wrong on tooltip, wrong on discoverability for the one affordance whose entire job is to be noticed
in the first ten seconds after launch.

### C3 — The Claude slug replaces `.` as well as `/`

Verified against 58 real project directories:

| Directory on disk | Real path |
|---|---|
| `-Users-joelmoss--buzz` | `/Users/joelmoss/.buzz` (confirmed to exist) |
| `-Users-joelmoss--superconductor-worktrees-platform-sc-…` | `/Users/joelmoss/.superconductor/worktrees/…` |
| `-Users-joelmoss-dev-clients-…-platform--claude-worktrees-…` | `…/platform/.claude/worktrees/…` |

A single leading `.` becomes a second `-`. Implementing the issue's stated rule verbatim means any
workroom path containing a dot — `~/.local/...`, a workroom branch named `v2.0`, a `.worktrees`
directory — silently produces a wrong slug and **never offers the button**, with no error and no
way to tell it apart from "no history here".

`_` is unverified: no underscore path exists in this store. **Do not guess it.** T1 below is a
two-minute spike that settles it empirically.

This also strengthens the issue's own collision argument, and the plan keeps its conclusion: the
scheme is Claude's, we mirror it, we do not invent our own.

### C4 — `savedAt` is persisted but discarded at load

`ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded` (`ProjectStore.swift:209`) keeps only the windows:

```swift
guard case .restored(let file, _) = sessionCoordinator.read() else { return }
unclaimedSessionWindows = file.windows
```

`file.savedAt` is dropped on the floor. The issue's "no new state" claim is true of the *file
format* (nothing new is written) but false of the runtime: `savedAt` needs a stored property on
`ProjectStore` and a read path out to whatever does discovery. Small, but it is a real edit in a
file the issue's Files Reference does not list.

### C5 — Restored panes are not marked, and the mark must be per-tab

`TerminalSessions.restore` (`:601`) builds tabs through the same `makeTerminalTab` that `addTab`
(⌘T) uses. Nothing afterwards distinguishes them. The issue's eligibility rule ("only panes created
by `restore` during this launch") therefore needs a new field.

It must be **per tab**, not a launch-scoped flag: acceptance criterion 4 and testing-plan row 7 both
require that a ⌘T pane opened in a restored target does *not* qualify. `TerminalTab` is a struct
with `let id = UUID()`, so `var wasRestored: Bool = false` is a one-line, value-typed addition that
copies correctly through every existing mutation path.

---

## The three decisions the issue left open

### D1 — Where the offer lives

**Decision: a separate `resumeOffers: [TerminalTab.ID: [AgentBackend]]` on `TerminalAgentManager`,
rendered as its own status-bar segment.** Not a sixth `AgentBannerState` case.

#145 offers a one-click route back to it, at restore time only, spawning nothing at launch.

four factual claims** that turn out to be wrong or incomplete against the actual code and the actual
agent stores on disk, it **makes three decisions the issue left implicit**, and it sequences the
work.

| `TerminalAgentBanner` + `AgentBannerViewModel` exist, reuse them | ⚠️ **half true** | They exist. But see **C1** and **C2** — reusing them as-is is a bug, not a shortcut. |
| Claude slug = cwd with `/` replaced by `-` | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C3**. `.` is also replaced. |
| `SessionFile.savedAt` "gives the recency window with no new state" | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C4**. It is persisted but thrown away at load. |

`AgentBannerState` (`Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29`) has five cases and **every one carries a
`FailedCommand`**. Its accessor is not optional:

```swift
var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?)
```

`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` destructures that non-optional tuple. A resume offer has
no failed command, so adding a sixth case forces either a fake `FailedCommand` (lying to the
Investigate path) or a signature change with a real call-site.

Worse, the store is single-slot:

```swift
@Published private(set) var banners: [TerminalTab.ID: AgentBannerState] = [:]
```

So a resume offer and a diagnosis **evict each other**. Concretely, with the issue's design as
written: restored pane shows *Resume Claude…*; the user runs `npm test`; it fails;
`commandFinished` calls `setBanner(.awaitingDiagnose(...))` and the resume offer is gone for good.
The reverse also happens — discovery is async by design, so a late offer can stomp a live
`.loading` diagnosis mid-run.

**This is the single biggest thing the issue gets wrong.** "Reuse it" reads as free; it is not.

terminal's Metal `NSView`). The chip is tinted by `diagnosisTint`, which maps `.awaiting` to
`theme.tokens.failure` — **red** — with `.help("Show the agent's diagnosis")` and a tab-strip badge
at `TerminalTabStrip.swift:149`.

Rendering a Resume offer through that path produces a red, failure-coloured chip labelled as a
diagnosis, that you must click to discover an offer you never asked for. Wrong on colour semantics,
wrong on tooltip, wrong on discoverability for the one affordance whose entire job is to be noticed
in the first ten seconds after launch.

Verified against 58 real project directories:

| Directory on disk | Real path |
|---|---|

| `-Users-joelmoss--superconductor-worktrees-platform-sc-…` | `/Users/joelmoss/.superconductor/worktrees/…` |

must not starve the cooperative pool — batch all panes' discovery into **one** background unit that
publishes once, rather than N concurrent tasks racing the launch path.

A slow or huge session directory delays the button, never the pane. Result dropped only if the tab
id is gone; selection changing is irrelevant (a background pane keeps its offer).

---

## Build sequence

Every step ends with `make app-format` + `make app-lint`; new files need `make app-generate`.

- **T1 (spike, 2 min)** — settle the `_` question in the Claude slug. `mkdir /tmp/wr_slug_probe &&
  cd it && claude -p 'hi' --allowed-tools none --permission-mode plan`, then read the directory name
  under `~/.claude/projects/`. Encode the answer in `ClaudeSessionStore.slug` with the evidence in a
  comment. **Do this first** — every other Claude-side test depends on the transform being right.
- **T2** — `Core/AgentSessionDiscovery.swift` (new). Pure slug + normalizer + recency predicate +
  Codex `session_meta` parse. No IO in the pure layer; a thin `discover(cwd:savedAt:)` on top.
- **T3** — `AgentInvocationBuilder.resume(_:)` + the argv tests.
- **T4** — `TerminalTab.wasRestored` (C5) and the one assignment in `TerminalSessions.restore`.
- **T5** — `ProjectStore` retains `savedAt` (C4) and exposes it; `AppStore+Session` kicks discovery
  for restored terminal tabs at the end of `restorePersistedSessionIfPending`.
- **T6** — `TerminalAgentManager.resumeOffers` (D1) + `tabClosed` clearing it.
- **T7** — `TerminalStatusBar` resume segment: accent tint, per-agent buttons, `.help(…)` on each
  (house rule: every control gets a tooltip), a11y ids `terminal.statusBar.resume.claude` /
  `.resume.codex`. Click → `addRunTab` (D2b).
- **T8** — `UITestFixture.agentSessionRoot` via the existing `text(_:)` seam, default-off exactly
  like `sessionFilePath`. With no path supplied, discovery is a **no-op in fixture mode** — the 34
  existing UI tests must never read the developer's real `~/.claude`.
- **T9** — tests (below).
- **T10** — docs: `macapp/README.md` line for the new file; strike nothing (no comment is falsified
  by this change).

### Files

**New:** `Core/AgentSessionDiscovery.swift`, `WorkroomAppTests/AgentSessionDiscoveryTests.swift`,
`WorkroomAppTests/AgentResumeInvocationTests.swift`.

**Modified:** `Core/AgentRunner.swift`, `Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift`,
`Core/TerminalSessions.swift`, `Core/ProjectStore.swift`, `Core/AppStore+Session.swift`,
`Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift`, `macapp/README.md`.

The issue's Files Reference misses `ProjectStore.swift` (C4), `TerminalSessions.swift` (C5) and
`UITestFixture.swift`, and names `Views/TerminalAgentBanner.swift`, which D1 leaves untouched.

---

## Verification

### Unit (`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/`)

- **`AgentSessionDiscoveryTests`**
  - slug: plain path; path with `-`; path with `.` (the C3 regression — `/Users/x/.buzz` →
    `-Users-x--buzz`); path with `_` (pinned to T1's answer); the documented `/a-b/c` vs `/a/b/c`
    collision, asserted as *accepted*, not fixed.
  - normalizer: symlink resolved, trailing slash dropped, case-insensitive match.
  - recency: inside, outside, and both 24 h boundaries; a future-dated mtime qualifies.
  - Codex `session_meta`: valid cwd parsed; malformed JSON, empty file, non-JSON first line, and a
    first line over 64 KB all ignored without throwing.
  - a missing / unreadable session root yields no offers and no error (AC 7).
- **`AgentResumeInvocationTests`** — `.claude` → `["--resume"]`, `.codex` → `["resume"]`; neither
  argv contains `--continue` or `--last`; both agents qualifying yields two offers, not one guess.
- **`TerminalSessionsTests`** — `restore` marks `wasRestored`; `addTab` does not (AC 4, C5).
- **`TerminalAgentManagerTests`** — **the C1 regression:** a resume offer and a
  `.awaitingDiagnose` banner coexist on one tab; neither evicts the other in either order.
  `tabClosed` clears both.
- **`SessionRestoreTests`** — discovery does not run during `restore` itself (same lazy-IO rule the
  #144 sidecar test pins).

### XCUITest (`WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests.swift`)

Seeded via `-WorkroomUITestAgentSessionRoot <abs path>`, mirroring `-WorkroomUITestSessionFile`.

1. Restored pane + seeded Claude root → *Resume Claude…* visible; process count before/after launch
   is unchanged (AC 5).
2. Seeded Codex root → *Resume Codex…*; both seeded → two independent actions (AC 2, 3).
3. No seeded root → no button, no error (AC 4, 7).

Scoped run (`make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so raw `xcodebuild`):

```
cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj \
  -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData \
  -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' \
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests test
```

Full gate: `make app-test` + `make app-lint` (AC 8). Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via
`xcresulttool`; Xcode 26 hides the summary. All `make app-*` need the sandbox disabled.

### Manual

Have a Claude conversation in a workroom, quit with ⌘Q, relaunch, confirm the button appears and
the picker opens. Then: a workroom whose path contains a dot (the C3 case). Then ⌘T in a restored
target and confirm it offers nothing.

---

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Test | Handling | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slug transform | `.` in path → wrong slug, silent no-button | ✅ C3 regression | Mirror Claude's real rule | — (silent before fix) |
| Banner slot | Resume offer and diagnosis evict each other | ✅ C1 regression | Separate dictionary (D1) | Offer vanishes on first failed command |
| `savedAt` | Not retained → no recency input at all | ✅ | Stored on `ProjectStore` (C4) | Button never appears |
| Recency | Idle agent before quit → false negative | ✅ boundaries | 24 h window (D3) | Button missing on the headline case |
| Eligibility | ⌘T pane offers resume | ✅ AC 4 | Per-tab `wasRestored` (C5) | Offer on a pane with no history |
| Discovery IO | Blocking read starves the launch path | ✅ (lazy-IO test) | One batched background unit | Slow launch |
| Late result | Pane closed before discovery returns | ✅ | Drop if tab id gone | — |
| Missing binary | `claude` not installed | ✅ AC 7 | Shell's own `command not found`; `AgentErrorKind.cliNotFound` deliberately **not** reused | Normal shell error |
| Fixture leak | UI tests read the real `~/.claude` | ✅ | Default-off `agentSessionRoot` (T8) | — |

**Critical gaps (no test AND no handling AND silent): 0.**

---

## NOT in scope

- **Auto-resume at launch.** Contradicts #46's run-tab decision, and agents cost money.
- **Knowing which session belonged to which pane.** The picker handles it. Correlating #144's
  captured scrollback against candidate session files is a possible later refinement.
- **Agent detection by process inspection.** Impossible on this libghostty pin — verified, no pid,
  no pty fd.
- **A third agent backend.** `AgentBackend` is a two-case enum; adding one is additive later.
- **Persisting anything about agents.** No session id, no backend, no new `WindowSession` field.

## What already exists

| Need | Existing code | Reused? |
|---|---|---|
| Picker-form argv construction | `AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline` | ✅ same enum, new case |
| Executable name resolution | `AgentBackend.executable` + `/usr/bin/env` on the augmented PATH | ✅ |
| Opening an interactive agent from a click | `TerminalStatusBar` Investigate → `sessions.addRunTab` | ✅ D2b is this precedent |
| Per-tab agent state keyed on `TerminalTab.ID` | `TerminalAgentManager.banners` | ⚠️ **second dictionary**, not this one (C1) |
| Pane-lifecycle cleanup | `TerminalAgentManager.tabClosed` | ✅ extend |
| Default-off fixture path seam | `UITestFixture.sessionFilePath` | ✅ mirrored |
| Status-bar segment composition | `TerminalStatusBar` (5 segments today) | ✅ |

## Open decision for the user

**D2 is a product call, not an engineering one.** (b) is the safer build; (a) is the feature the
issue describes. Everything else in this plan is settled.

content.content:
So adding `.resume` to `AgentBannerState` is wrong, and a single enum value could not represent diagnosis plus resume simultaneously.

The plan overstates this as “the biggest thing” and assumes the issue necessarily requires a sixth case. It is a routine state-model mismatch, not an architectural crisis.

Concrete fix: keep resume state independent from `AgentBannerState`, but do not automatically put a second unrelated concern on `TerminalAgentManager`; see D1 below.

### C2 — Existing banner presentation is failure-specific

**Severity: medium — real.**

Evidence:

- The status-bar control is explicitly a diagnosis popover ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:9](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:9)).
- Its tooltip and accessibility label say “diagnosis” ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:256](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:256)).
- Awaiting/ready/failure states are deliberately failure-red ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:251](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:251), [TerminalStatusBar.swift:286](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:286)).
- The tab-strip badge likewise means a live diagnosis ([TerminalTabStrip.swift:147](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:147)).

Concrete fix: use a separate, direct resume affordance. Do not reuse `AgentBannerViewModel`, diagnosis tinting, tooltip, badge, or popover.

### C3 — Claude slug handling

**Severity: high — not established by repository code, and the proposed implementation remains unsafe.**

Nothing in the named code implements or documents Claude’s private storage slug. The plan’s claim comes from inspecting one machine’s private store, not from repository evidence, and it explicitly leaves `_` unresolved.

Worse, its proposed `resolvingSymlinksInPath()` before slugging changes the path string that Claude itself may have used. A session launched from `/work/link` may be stored under the textual symlink path, while the plan looks under the resolved target. Lowercasing is also wrong on case-sensitive APFS or external volumes.

Concrete fix:

- Treat the slug only as a candidate-directory optimization, not proof of identity.
- Validate candidate session metadata against the exact saved cwd where the format supports it.
- Do not lowercase paths globally.
- Define explicit symlink semantics and test both textual and resolved paths.
- Do not ship a guessed reverse-engineered transform with “accepted” collisions as the sole identity check.

### C4 — `savedAt` is discarded

**Severity: low — real, but the proposed ownership is poor.**

Evidence:

- `SessionFile` contains `savedAt` ([SessionSnapshot.swift:480](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift:480)).
- `ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded()` retains only `file.windows` ([ProjectStore.swift:209](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:209)).

Concrete fix: carry `savedAt` inside a one-shot restore context returned with claimed windows. Do not add a long-lived mutable `ProjectStore.savedAt` property that survives after restore and can accidentally be reused by later windows or reloads.

### C5 — Restored tabs are not marked

**Severity: low — factually real, proposed fix unnecessary.**

Evidence:

- `restore` creates fresh ordinary `TerminalTab` values through `makeTerminalTab` ([TerminalSessions.swift:612](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:612)).
- `TerminalTab` has no restoration provenance ([TerminalSessions.swift:14](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:14)).
- `restore` currently returns only an `Int`, losing the identities it just created ([TerminalSessions.swift:601](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:601), [TerminalSessions.swift:652](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:652)).

A persistent `wasRestored` boolean is needless state. The restore call already knows exactly which terminal tabs it created.

Concrete fix: return `[RestoredTerminal]` containing `tabID`, target ID, and effective cwd. Start discovery from that result. Newly created ⌘T tabs can never enter the discovery input, so no permanent flag is needed.

## 2. D2: `addRunTab` is wrong

**Severity: critical.**

The plan’s statement that direct `addRunTab` is “tracked by `AppStore.RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner`” is false.

`addRunTab` only creates and inserts a fixed-command surface. Its own documentation says the caller owns run state and exit wiring ([TerminalSessions.swift:912](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:912), [TerminalSessions.swift:940](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:940)).

Actual run tracking happens only in `AppStore.startRunCommand`:

- It creates supervisor/pid-file machinery.
- It writes `runStates`.
- It wires `onChildExited`.
- It installs graceful close handling.

See [AppStore.swift:1923](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1923), [AppStore.swift:1932](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1932), [AppStore.swift:1950](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1950), and [AppStore.swift:1958](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1958).

Direct `addRunTab` therefore causes all of these failures:

- **Critical — untracked process at quit.** Quit-time detection iterates `runStates`, not surfaces ([AppStore.swift:2248](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2248), [AppStore.swift:2257](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2257)). The agent will be skipped by graceful teardown.
- **High — issue #7 protections are bypassed.** A raw surface close causes a PTY hangup; the code explicitly warns this can orphan descendants ([AppStore.swift:1964](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1964)).
- **High — `WindowRegistry.runOwner` does nothing.** It checks another window’s `runStates` ([WindowRegistry.swift:208](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WindowRegistry.swift:208)). A direct agent run is invisible, so two restored windows can launch duplicates.
- **High — trying to add it to `RunState` is also wrong.** There is one run state per target ([AppStore.swift:1310](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1310)). An agent session would collide with the project’s configured dev-server run, inherit Run/Stop/Restart UI, and produce toasts whose command is read from project run configuration ([AppStore.swift:1471](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1471)).
- **High — it deliberately will not restore.** Any surface with a command is excluded from session capture ([TerminalSessions.swift:211](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:211)). The user resumes an agent, quits again, and the resumed pane disappears from the next restore.
- **Medium — wrong UX semantics.** Fixed commands use `wait_after_command` ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:255](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:255)); after exit, the next key closes the tab ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989)).
- **Medium — it does not appear “beside” the restored pane.** `addRunTab` appends a solo tab and focuses it ([TerminalSessions.swift:943](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:943)). It creates no split.
- **High — it violates the feature itself.** The requested action is in the restored pane. A new, non-restorable Run tab leaves that pane inert.

The existing Investigate handlers directly calling `addRunTab` ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:267](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:267), [TerminalTabStrip.swift:437](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:437)) are evidence of an existing lifecycle hole, not a precedent to duplicate.

Concrete fix: execute the static picker command in the restored login shell, but only while the pane is pristine. Track user input/paste since restore and remove the offer after the first input event. On a click, atomically consume the offer and send the fixed command plus Return. The comment at `sendText` forbids auto-running an **AI-suggested fix**, not a static command explicitly authorized by a button click ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970)).

If product insists on a new pane, build a separate interactive-agent lifecycle. Do not mislabel it as issue #7 Run state.

## 3. D1: second dictionary

**Severity: medium.**

Independent resume and diagnosis state is correct. A second `[tabID: ...]` dictionary on `TerminalAgentManager` is not the cleanest shape:

- The manager’s documented responsibility is failure classification and diagnosis ([TerminalAgentManager.swift:55](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:55)).
- Resume discovery has different lifecycle, IO, cancellation, and cost semantics.
- Two dictionaries plus `wasRestored` create three representations that must agree.
- `[AgentBackend]` permits duplicates and gives ordering accidental semantic weight.

Concrete fix:

- Have `TerminalSessions.restore` return restored-terminal descriptors.
- Put discovery state in a small `AgentResumeCoordinator`/`ResumeOfferStore`.
- Key it by tab ID with a value such as `{ offers: Set<AgentBackend>, generation, discoveryTask }`.
- Atomically consume an offer before launching.
- Let `tabClosed` notify that coordinator alongside the diagnosis manager.

If avoiding another object is important, use one composite per-tab state rather than parallel dictionaries:

```swift
struct TabAgentState {
  var diagnosis: AgentBannerState?
  var resumeOffers: Set<AgentBackend>
}
```

But that still leaves discovery awkwardly owned by a diagnosis manager.

## 4. D3: 24 hours

**Severity: high.**

This converts “likely associated with the restored session” into “someone used an agent somewhere in this directory yesterday.”

The underlying timestamp is already weak: `savedAt` is global to the entire session document, not per pane, per cwd, or per agent. Widening it by 288× does not repair that missing identity; it multiplies false positives.

Other defects:

- A future-mtime window is not harmless. Corrupt or manipulated timestamps can keep offers alive.
- Three Codex day directories can contain thousands of rollout files.
- A 24-hour Claude match will commonly trigger for routine daily use, even if the restored pane never contained Claude.
- The picker being interactive does not make a misleading button free. It leaks session existence, starts an executable, invites billed work, and trains users to click an unreliable signal.
- Lowercasing paths because the “default APFS volume” is insensitive is invalid for case-sensitive and external volumes.
- Symlink resolution can intentionally merge two textual workrooms into one identity.

Concrete fix: keep the issue’s conservative five-minute window initially, preferably one-sided with a small clock-skew allowance. Better still, correlate with restored scrollback or persist non-sensitive agent provenance prospectively. Do not pretend a 24-hour directory-level heuristic identifies a pane.

## 5. Entirely missed

### Unbounded discovery IO

**Severity: critical.**

“One background unit” is not a bound. Synchronous directory enumeration inside a detached task is not cooperatively cancellable. With thousands of rollouts, it can run long after every relevant pane closes.

Concrete fix: index each Codex file once per launch, deduplicate cwds, use bounded reads through `FileHandle`, impose maximum files/bytes/wall time, check cancellation between entries, and publish partial/no result on deadline.

### Restore watchdog interaction

**Severity: high.**

`restorePersistedSessionIfPending` calls `finishSessionRestore` in a `defer` ([AppStore+Session.swift:159](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore+Session.swift:159)). The watchdog fires after 15 seconds and freezes session writes if any window remains incomplete ([ProjectStore.swift:179](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:179), [ProjectStore.swift:223](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:223)).

If discovery is awaited before the defer, a large store can freeze persistence. If it is fire-and-forget, each window starts its own “single batch” while sibling windows are still restoring. The plan has no global completion point or ownership.

Concrete fix: finish structural restore first. Then schedule discovery asynchronously from returned descriptors. Use a process-wide discovery index/cache shared by windows.

### Two windows restoring the same workroom

**Severity: high.**

Fresh tab IDs are deliberately global across windows ([TerminalSessions.swift:588](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:588)), but cwd matching will give both windows identical offers. Direct `addRunTab` bypasses `runOwner`, allowing duplicate agents and duplicate billed sessions.

Concrete fix: consume atomically per tab, suppress double-clicks, and introduce explicit interactive-agent ownership if cross-window duplication is disallowed. Add a two-window restore test.

### Symlink and path-boundary security

**Severity: high.**

The plan follows symlinks and case-folds without defining trust boundaries. Candidate session files themselves may be symlinks. A malicious project-local action could arrange links causing Workroom to inspect unrelated files under the user account.

Concrete fix: require regular files, reject symlinked candidate files/directories unless explicitly supported, enforce containment under the configured agent root, avoid global lowercasing, and test case-sensitive volumes and symlinked workrooms.

### Scrollback replay ordering

**Severity: medium.**

Issue #144 intentionally defers sidecar IO until a pane mounts ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156)); replay then occurs synchronously during surface creation ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:290](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:290)). The plan adds eager, unrelated store scanning for every restored pane, including panes whose scrollback may never be loaded.

Concrete fix: do not claim this preserves scrollback “beside” anything. Test that discovery cannot delay surface creation/replay and that clicking resume consumes the offer without altering restored history.

### Repeated paid execution

**Severity: high.**

The offer is never removed on click in the design. A double-click or repeated clicks can spawn multiple CLIs. The T1 “spike” itself runs `claude -p 'hi'`, which can incur cost and mutate the developer’s real Claude history.

Concrete fix: delete T1. Use checked-in fixtures or a documented compatibility table. Consume/disable the offer before execution and require a new explicit action to retry after a failed picker launch.

### Invocation abstraction is dishonest

**Severity: medium.**

The plan claims argv is “built as data,” but `addRunTab` accepts a single command string ([TerminalSessions.swift:940](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:940)), which is assigned to Ghostty’s command field ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:258](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:258)). The proposed `AgentInvocation` must therefore be serialized back into a command line somewhere the plan does not specify or test.

Concrete fix: for the two static picker commands, use audited constants. If arbitrary argv is ever needed, add a single tested shell-command encoder or a spawn API that accepts argv.

### Error handling is inadequate

**Severity: medium.**

“No history,” unreadable root, permission denied, malformed files, scan deadline, unsupported schema, CLI missing, and CLI spawn failure all collapse to silence or a shell error. The plan’s “critical gaps: 0” claim is false.

Concrete fix: keep expected absence silent, log bounded discovery failures without paths/session contents, and show a transient user-facing error when an explicit click cannot start the CLI.

### Test plan misses the action

**Severity: critical.**

The UI tests only assert button visibility and that launch does not spawn a process. They never click the button.

Required additions:

- Exactly one click starts exactly one picker command.
- Double-click/repeated click cannot start duplicates.
- Offer disappears atomically on action and tab closure.
- Existing typed input suppresses the offer or prevents execution.
- Two-window same-workroom restore.
- Existing configured Run command remains unaffected.
- Quit/window-close teardown with an active resumed agent.
- Resume pane remains persistable on the next launch.
- Symlinked cwd, case-sensitive paths, and slug collisions.
- Thousands of rollout files, deadline, cancellation, and bounded memory.
- Restore watchdog plus slow discovery.
- Scrollback replay ordering.
- Missing executable and failed spawn.
- No live agent process in tests; all execution must use an injected fake.

Cut these outright:

- **D2/addRunTab.** It is the wrong lifecycle and violates the feature.
- **The 24-hour window and symmetric future matching.**
- **T1’s real `claude -p` probe.** Tests must not spend money or mutate private agent state.
- **`TerminalTab.wasRestored`.** Return restored IDs instead.
- **Unconditional path lowercasing.**
- **The claim that slug collisions are “accepted” without metadata validation.**
- **The single unbounded detached batch.**
- **The grep gate for `--continue`/`--last`.** A repository-wide text ban is brittle and unrelated to runtime correctness; test the invocation builder/action instead.
- **The “critical gaps: 0” assertion.** It is demonstrably false.

The plan needs redesign around executing a one-shot, user-authorized static command in a pristine restored shell, with bounded discovery and explicit lifecycle ownership.

**Severity: low — factually real, proposed fix unnecessary.**

- **Critical — untracked process at quit.** Quit-time detection iterates `runStates`, not surfaces ([AppStore.swift:2248](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2248), [AppStore.swift:2257](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2257)). - **High — issue #7 protections are bypassed.** A raw surface close causes a PTY hangup; the code explicitly warns this can orphan descendants ([AppStore.swift:1964](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1964)).
- **High — `WindowRegistry.runOwner` does nothing.** It checks another window’s `runStates` ([WindowRegistry.swift:208](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WindowRegistry.swift:208)). A direct agent run is invisible, so two restored windows can launch duplicates.
- **High — trying to add it to `RunState` is also wrong.** There is one run state per target ([AppStore.swift:1310](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1310)). # Issue #145 — Offer to resume an agent session in a restored pane

**Status:** eng-reviewed, one open decision (D3). Revision 2 — revision 1's recommended execution
vehicle was wrong and has been cut; see the Review Log at the end.

## Context

After #46 a restored pane is inert: right workroom, right directory, dead shell. If you were
mid-conversation with Claude or Codex, that conversation still exists in the agent's own store.
#145 offers a one-click route back to it, at restore time only, spawning nothing at launch.

The issue is well specified. This plan does what the issue does not: it **corrects claims that are
wrong against the actual code and the actual agent stores**, **settles the decisions the issue left
implicit**, and sequences the work.

---

## Verified facts (checked against code and disk, 2026-08-09)

| Claim in #145 | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| libghostty exposes no child pid / pty fd | ✅ true | `DerivedData/…/include/ghostty.h:824` — the only child symbol is `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s`. No pid, no fd. |
| Codex rollout line 1 is `session_meta` with `cwd` | ✅ true | Real rollout: `{payload, timestamp, type}`, `type == "session_meta"`, `payload.cwd` present. |
| Codex layout `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` | ✅ true | Verified 2026/03…2026/08. |
| `claude --resume` picker; `--continue` in-cwd | ✅ true | `claude --help`: `-r, --resume [value]`, `-c, --continue`. |
| `codex resume` picker; `--last` skips it | ✅ true | `codex resume --help`. |
| Reuse `TerminalAgentBanner` / `AgentBannerViewModel` | ⚠️ misleading | C1, C2. |
| Claude slug = cwd with `/` → `-` | ❌ wrong, **and the whole approach is unnecessary** | C3. |
| `savedAt` gives recency "with no new state" | ❌ wrong | C4. |
| Restored panes are identifiable | ❌ they are not | C5. |

### C1 — `AgentBannerState` is failure-shaped, and there is one slot per tab

Every case of `AgentBannerState` (`Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29`) carries a `FailedCommand`,
and its accessor is non-optional:

```swift
var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?)
```

`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` destructures that tuple. A sixth `.resumeOffer` case
forces either a fabricated `FailedCommand` or a signature change with a real call site.

The store is also single-slot — `banners: [TerminalTab.ID: AgentBannerState]` — so the two states
would evict each other. Restored pane offers *Resume Claude…*; the user runs `npm test`; it fails;
`commandFinished` calls `setBanner(.awaitingDiagnose(...))`; the offer is gone for good. The reverse
happens too: discovery is async, so a late offer can stomp a live `.loading` diagnosis.

Severity: medium. It is a routine state-model mismatch, not a crisis — but "reuse it" reads as free
and is not.

### C2 — The "banner" is a red status-bar chip behind a popover

`TerminalStatusBar.swift:9` is explicit: the diagnosis is a compact indicator opening the banner in
a **popover**, because a SwiftUI overlay loses hit-testing to the terminal's Metal `NSView`.
`diagnosisTint` maps `.awaiting` to `theme.tokens.failure` — **red** — with
`.help("Show the agent's diagnosis")` and a tab-strip badge (`TerminalTabStrip.swift:149`).

A Resume offer rendered there is a red, failure-coloured chip labelled as a diagnosis, hidden behind
a click. Wrong on colour, tooltip and discoverability for the one affordance whose job is to be
noticed in the ten seconds after launch.

### C3 — Do not reverse-engineer Claude's slug. Read the `cwd` the file already records.

The issue's rule (`/` → `-`) is wrong: `.` is replaced too. Verified against 58 real project
directories — `/Users/joelmoss/.buzz` is stored as `-Users-joelmoss--buzz`. `_` is unverified,
because no underscore path exists in this store.

But the whole guessing exercise is unnecessary. **Claude's session `.jsonl` records carry `cwd`
directly**, on `user` / `assistant` / `attachment` records (not on line 1, which is a
`{leafUuid, sessionId, type}` summary). Verified against a real transcript:

```
$ head -20 <session>.jsonl | jq -r 'select(has("cwd")) | .cwd'
/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom
```

So Claude gets the **same exact-match treatment Codex already gets** from `session_meta.cwd`, and
every downstream problem dissolves:

- No `_` guess, so **T1's `claude -p` probe is cut** — it would have spent money and written to the
  developer's own conversation history.
- The documented `/a-b/c` vs `/a/b/c` collision stops being "accepted"; it is *resolved*.
- No global `lowercased()`, which is wrong on case-sensitive or external volumes.
- No `resolvingSymlinksInPath()` before slugging. Resolving is actively harmful: a session started
  through a symlink may be recorded under the textual path, so resolving first looks in the wrong
  place.

The slug survives **only as a candidate-directory hint** — cheap narrowing, never identity. When the
hint misses (an unknown character class), fall back to enumerating `~/.claude/projects/` (58 dirs
here; a trivial scan) and validating by recorded `cwd`.

Path comparison: compare the recorded `cwd` to the pane cwd **textually first**; accept a
`resolvingSymlinksInPath()` match as a secondary candidate. Never case-fold unconditionally.

### C4 — `savedAt` is persisted but discarded at load

`ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded` (`ProjectStore.swift:209`) keeps only the windows:

```swift
guard case .restored(let file, _) = sessionCoordinator.read() else { return }
unclaimedSessionWindows = file.windows
```

`file.savedAt` is dropped. The issue's "no new state" is true of the *file format* and false of the
runtime.

**Carry it in the one-shot restore context, not as a long-lived `ProjectStore` property.** A stored
`savedAt` outlives the restore and can be picked up by a later window or a reload, silently
re-arming discovery long after launch.

### C5 — Return the restored tabs; do not add a persistent flag

`TerminalSessions.restore` (`:601`) builds tabs through the same `makeTerminalTab` that ⌘T uses, and
returns only an `Int` — throwing away the identities it just minted.

Revision 1 proposed `TerminalTab.wasRestored`. That is redundant state. `restore` already knows
exactly which terminal tabs it created; returning them means a ⌘T tab can never enter the discovery
input in the first place, which satisfies AC 4 by construction rather than by a flag that three
representations must agree on.

```swift
struct RestoredTerminal { let tabID: TerminalTab.ID; let targetID: TerminalTarget.ID; let cwd: String }
@discardableResult
func restore(_:for:scrollback:) -> RestoreResult   // { count: Int, terminals: [RestoredTerminal] }
```

`AppStore+Session.swift:177`'s `guard terminals.restore(...) > 0` becomes `.count > 0`.

---

## Decisions

### D1 — Where the offer lives — **a separate coordinator, not a second dictionary on the manager**

`TerminalAgentManager`'s documented job is failure classification and diagnosis
(`TerminalAgentManager.swift:55`). Resume discovery has a different lifecycle, different IO,
different cancellation and a real money cost. Bolting a second `[tabID: …]` dictionary onto it puts
two unrelated concerns in one object and creates parallel maps that must agree.

**New `Core/AgentResumeCoordinator.swift`**, `@MainActor`, `ObservableObject`:

```swift
struct ResumeOffer { var backends: Set<AgentBackend> }   // a Set: no duplicates, no accidental order
@Published private(set) var offers: [TerminalTab.ID: ResumeOffer]
func discover(_ restored: [RestoredTerminal], savedAt: Date)
func consume(tab: TerminalTab.ID, backend: AgentBackend) -> AgentInvocation?   // ATOMIC
func tabClosed(_ tab: TerminalTab.ID)
```

`consume` removes the offer **before** returning the invocation, so a double-click or a re-render
cannot start two billed CLI sessions. `Set<AgentBackend>` rather than `[AgentBackend]` because
duplicates are meaningless and array order would acquire accidental semantics.

Rendered as its own `TerminalStatusBar` segment: accent tint (not `theme.tokens.failure`), its own
tooltip, a direct button rather than a popover — a resume offer has no body to show, it is one click.
`TerminalAgentBanner` and `AgentBannerViewModel` are **not touched**.

Rejected: a sixth `AgentBannerState` case (C1). Rejected: a second dictionary on
`TerminalAgentManager` (mixes concerns; still leaves `wasRestored` as a third representation).

### D2 — How the command runs — **type into the pristine restored shell.** `addRunTab` is CUT.

Revision 1 recommended `sessions.addRunTab(...)`, on the grounds that the Investigate button already
does it and that it is "tracked by `AppStore.RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner`".

**That was false, and the review caught it.** `addRunTab`'s own docstring
(`TerminalSessions.swift:912`) says: *"The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab."* Run tracking lives in
`AppStore.startRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:1923-1964`). A direct `addRunTab` therefore:

| Consequence | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Fatal — the resumed pane does not survive the next restore.** Any surface carrying a command is excluded from session capture. | `TerminalSessions.swift:211`: run tabs `return nil` from `TabSession.init?`, identified by `isRunCommandSurface`. |
| Quit-time graceful teardown skips it — it iterates `runStates`, not surfaces. | `AppStore.hasLiveRunCommand` / `liveRunView` (`AppStore.swift:2248-2260`). |
| `WindowRegistry.runOwner` cannot see it, so two restored windows can each launch one. | `WindowRegistry.swift:208` reads `runStates`. |
| Registering it *in* `runStates` is also wrong: one run state per target, so it would collide with the project's configured dev-server run and inherit Run/Stop/Restart UI. | `AppStore.swift:1310`. |
| Wrong UX: fixed commands use `wait_after_command`, so after the agent exits the next keypress closes the tab. | `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:255`, `:989`. |
| It does not appear "beside" the restored pane — `addRunTab` appends a **solo** tab and focuses it. No split. | `TerminalSessions.swift:943`. |

The first row alone is disqualifying: a feature built on session restore must not produce a pane
that session restore refuses to persist.

**Decision: send the static command into the restored pane's own login shell, plus Return, and only
while that pane is pristine.**

- **Pristine guard.** Discovery is async; by the time the offer lands the user may have typed half a
  command. Appending `claude --resume\r` to a dirty line runs the wrong thing. Track whether the
  surface has received any key or paste since restore; the first input event **drops the offer**.
  This is strictly better than the alternative (`Ctrl-U` kill-line), which is shell-dependent and
  destroys what the user typed.
- **The #49 policy is not violated.** `GhosttySurfaceView.sendText`'s comment
  (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970`) forbids auto-executing an **AI-suggested** command — a string a
  model produced. This is a compile-time constant behind an explicit button labelled Resume. Add a
  second, separately named entry point (`sendCommandLine(_:)`) rather than loosening `sendText`, so
  the existing guarantee stays legible and greppable.
- **Spike (T2):** confirm `ghostty_surface_text` passes `\r` through as Enter rather than filtering
  control bytes. If it filters, use the key-event path instead. Two minutes; costs nothing.

### D3 — The recency window — **OPEN, see the decision brief**

This is the only unsettled item, and it is a product call. See "Open decision" below.

What is settled: the window is symmetric in *tolerance* (a future-dated mtime from clock skew still
qualifies) but bounded, and Codex date-directory scanning only reads day directories that intersect
the window.

---

## Design

```
  launch ─▶ ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded   ──▶ restore context carries savedAt   (C4)
                │                                   (one-shot, not a stored property)
                ▼
        AppStore.restorePersistedSessionIfPending
                │
                ├──▶ TerminalSessions.restore ──▶ RestoreResult.terminals            (C5)
                │
                ├──▶ finishSessionRestore()  ← the `defer`. STRUCTURAL RESTORE ENDS HERE.
                │                              Discovery is NEVER awaited before this
                │                              (it would race the 15s watchdog freeze).
                ▼
        AgentResumeCoordinator.discover(terminals, savedAt:)   — fire and forget
                │
                ▼
        AgentSessionIndex (PROCESS-WIDE, built once per launch, shared by all windows)
                │
                ├── Claude:  slug(cwd) narrows to a candidate dir (HINT ONLY)
                │            → read each *.jsonl (depth 1) until the first record with `cwd`
                │            → EXACT match against the pane cwd                       (C3)
                │
                └── Codex:   day dirs intersecting the window
                             → first line → session_meta.payload.cwd → EXACT match
                │
                │   BOUNDS (hard, all of them): ≤N files, ≤M bytes/file, ≤T seconds
                │   wall clock, cancellation checked between entries, partial result
                │   published on deadline.
                ▼
        main actor, IF the tab id still exists:
                coordinator.offers[tabID] = ResumeOffer(backends: [.claude, .codex])
                │
                ▼
        TerminalStatusBar: accent "Resume Claude…" / "Resume Codex…"
                │  click
                ▼
        coordinator.consume(tab:backend:) → invocation   (offer removed FIRST — atomic)
                │
                ▼
        pristine? ──no──▶ nothing (offer was already dropped on first input)
                │ yes
                ▼
        surface.sendCommandLine("claude --resume")        ← static constant + Return
```

### Argv

Two audited constants, in `AgentInvocationBuilder` beside `claudeInline`:

```swift
static func resume(_ backend: AgentBackend) -> AgentInvocation
// .claude → AgentInvocation(executable: "claude", arguments: ["--resume"])
// .codex  → AgentInvocation(executable: "codex",  arguments: ["resume"])
```

Nothing read from disk reaches the command line — the only variable is `AgentBackend.executable`, a
`rawValue` on a two-case enum. Because the shell takes a **string**, the plan does not pretend argv
stays structured all the way down: one tested `commandLine` accessor does the join, and for these
two commands the result is assertable character-for-character.

Review objected to the repo-wide `--continue` / `--last` grep gate as brittle. It stays: it is the
user's own acceptance criterion 6, and it is cheap. The invocation-builder unit test is the real
guarantee; the grep is a tripwire.

### Threading and bounds

Per the #144 lessons (`macapp-cli-shellout-cooperative-pool`,
`macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd`), blocking file work must not starve the cooperative pool.
Discovery runs on a dedicated background queue, not a swarm of detached tasks.

`AgentSessionIndex` is **process-wide and built once per launch**. Two windows restoring the same
workroom must not each scan thousands of Codex rollouts. It also means the two windows produce the
same offers — see the two-window test below.

---

## Build sequence

Each step ends with `make app-format` + `make app-lint`; new files need `make app-generate`.

- **T1** — `Core/AgentSessionIndex.swift` (new): pure slug hint, exact-`cwd` extraction for both
  formats, recency predicate, and the bounded scanner. Pure layer has no IO; a thin `build(…)` sits
  on top.
- **T2 (spike, 2 min)** — confirm `ghostty_surface_text` forwards `\r` as Enter. No API cost.
- **T3** — `AgentInvocationBuilder.resume(_:)` + `commandLine` + argv tests.
- **T4** — `TerminalSessions.restore` returns `RestoreResult` (C5); update the one call site and
  tests.
- **T5** — restore context carries `savedAt` (C4) out of `ProjectStore`.
- **T6** — `Core/AgentResumeCoordinator.swift` (D1): offers, atomic `consume`, `tabClosed`,
  cancellation.
- **T7** — `GhosttySurfaceView.sendCommandLine(_:)` + the pristine-input tracking that drops the
  offer on first key/paste (D2).
- **T8** — `TerminalStatusBar` resume segment: accent tint, per-agent buttons, `.help(…)` on each
  (house rule: every control gets a tooltip), a11y ids `terminal.statusBar.resume.claude` /
  `.resume.codex`.
- **T9** — `UITestFixture.agentSessionRoot` via the existing `text(_:)` seam, default-off exactly
  like `sessionFilePath`. With no path supplied, discovery is a **no-op in fixture mode** — the 34
  existing UI tests must never read the developer's real `~/.claude`.
- **T10** — tests (below).
- **T11** — docs: `macapp/README.md` line for the two new files.

### Files

**New:** `Core/AgentSessionIndex.swift`, `Core/AgentResumeCoordinator.swift`, plus
`WorkroomAppTests/AgentSessionIndexTests.swift`,
`WorkroomAppTests/AgentResumeCoordinatorTests.swift`,
`WorkroomAppTests/AgentResumeInvocationTests.swift`,
`WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests.swift`.

**Modified:** `Core/AgentRunner.swift`, `Core/TerminalSessions.swift`, `Core/ProjectStore.swift`,
`Core/AppStore+Session.swift`, `Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`, `Core/UITestFixture.swift`,
`Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift`, `macapp/README.md`.

The issue's Files Reference misses `ProjectStore.swift`, `TerminalSessions.swift`,
`GhosttySurfaceView.swift` and `UITestFixture.swift`, and names `TerminalAgentManager.swift` and
`Views/TerminalAgentBanner.swift`, which D1 leaves untouched.

---

## Verification

### Unit

- **`AgentSessionIndexTests`**
  - Claude `cwd` extracted from a `user` record when line 1 is the `{leafUuid, sessionId, type}`
    summary; extraction stops at the first record carrying `cwd`.
  - The C3 regression: `/Users/x/.buzz` — the slug hint alone would miss it; exact `cwd` matching
    finds it. And the `/a-b/c` vs `/a/b/c` collision resolves to the right one.
  - Symlinked cwd matches textually; the resolved path is a secondary candidate. A case-sensitive
    path is **not** folded.
  - Codex `session_meta`: valid cwd parsed; malformed JSON, empty file, non-JSON first line and a
    first line over the byte cap are ignored without throwing.
  - Recency: inside, outside, both boundaries; a future-dated mtime qualifies.
  - **Bounds:** a seeded store of 5,000 rollout files respects the file cap, the byte cap and the
    wall-clock deadline, publishes a partial result, and honours cancellation.
  - Missing / unreadable / permission-denied root yields no offers and no throw (AC 7).
- **`AgentResumeInvocationTests`** — `.claude` → `["--resume"]`, `.codex` → `["resume"]`; neither
  contains `--continue` or `--last`; the command-line join is asserted exactly; both agents
  qualifying yields two offers, not one guess.
- **`AgentResumeCoordinatorTests`**
  - **The C1 regression:** an offer and a `.awaitingDiagnose` banner coexist on one tab; neither
    evicts the other, in either order.
  - **`consume` is atomic** — two calls in a row return one invocation and one nil.
  - `tabClosed` clears the offer and cancels in-flight discovery.
  - A result arriving after the tab is gone is dropped.
- **`TerminalSessionsTests`** — `restore` returns its terminals; `addTab` contributes none (AC 4).
- **`SessionRestoreTests`** — discovery does not run inside `restore`, and `finishSessionRestore`
  is not gated on it (the watchdog regression).

### XCUITest (`AgentResumeUITests`)

Seeded via `-WorkroomUITestAgentSessionRoot <abs path>`, mirroring `-WorkroomUITestSessionFile`.
**No test spawns a real agent** — execution goes through an injected fake that records the command.

1. Restored pane + seeded Claude root → *Resume Claude…*; process count unchanged across launch
   (AC 5).
2. Seeded Codex root → *Resume Codex…*; both seeded → two independent actions (AC 2, 3).
3. **Clicking it sends exactly one command line, once.** Double-click sends nothing further and the
   button is gone.
4. Typing into the pane before clicking removes the offer (the pristine guard).
5. No seeded root → no button, no error (AC 4, 7).
6. Two windows restoring the same workroom: both offer, and clicking in one does not disturb the
   other's pane.
7. A resumed pane still persists into the *next* restore — the regression that killed the run-tab
   design.
8. An existing configured Run command for the same target is unaffected.

Scoped run (`make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so raw `xcodebuild`):

```
cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj \
  -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData \
  -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' \
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests test
```

Full gate: `make app-test` + `make app-lint` (AC 8). Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via
`xcresulttool` — Xcode 26 hides the summary. All `make app-*` need the sandbox disabled.

---

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Test | Handling | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude matching | Slug guess wrong (`.`, `_`) → silent no-button | ✅ C3 | Exact `cwd` from file contents; slug is a hint | — (silent before fix) |
| Offer state | Offer and diagnosis evict each other | ✅ C1 | Separate coordinator (D1) | Offer vanishes on first failed command |
| Execution | Resumed pane never persists again | ✅ UI test 7 | `sendCommandLine`, not `addRunTab` (D2) | Pane gone next launch |
| Execution | Command typed onto a half-typed line | ✅ UI test 4 | Pristine guard drops the offer on first input | Wrong command runs |
| Billing | Double-click spawns two paid sessions | ✅ UI test 3 | `consume` is atomic (D1) | Duplicate agents |
| Discovery IO | Thousands of rollouts block / outlive the panes | ✅ bounds test | File + byte + wall-clock caps, cancellation | Slow or absent button |
| Watchdog | Discovery awaited before `finishSessionRestore` → 15 s freeze | ✅ | Fire-and-forget after the `defer` | **Session writes frozen for the run** |
| Two windows | Each window rescans thousands of files | ✅ UI test 6 | Process-wide `AgentSessionIndex` | Slow launch |
| `savedAt` | Long-lived property re-arms discovery later | ✅ | One-shot restore context (C4) | Offers on non-restored panes |
| Eligibility | ⌘T pane offers resume | ✅ AC 4 | Restore returns its own tabs (C5) | Offer with no history |
| Missing binary | `claude` not installed | ✅ | Shell's own `command not found`; `AgentErrorKind.cliNotFound` deliberately **not** reused | Normal shell error |
| Fixture leak | UI tests read the real `~/.claude` | ✅ | Default-off `agentSessionRoot` (T9) | — |

**Known residual gaps** (revision 1 claimed zero; that was false):

- A discovery scan that hits its deadline logs and publishes partially, with **no user-visible
  signal**. Deliberate: the failure mode is a missing button, and a toast for "we did not finish
  looking" is noise. Logged, bounded, no paths or session content in the log.
- A click that fails to start the CLI surfaces only the shell's own `command not found`. Acceptable
  per the issue's own decision, but it *is* a gap, not a handled path.

---

## NOT in scope

- **Auto-resume at launch.** Contradicts #46's run-tab decision, and agents cost money.
- **Knowing which session belonged to which pane.** The picker handles it. Correlating #144's
  captured scrollback against candidate session files is a later refinement.
- **Agent detection by process inspection.** Impossible on this pin — verified, no pid, no pty fd.
- **Fixing the pre-existing Investigate lifecycle hole.** Separate; see below.
- **A third agent backend.** `AgentBackend` is a two-case enum; additive later.
- **Persisting anything about agents.** No session id, no backend, no new `WindowSession` field.

## Adjacent bug found during review (NOT this issue)

`TerminalStatusBar.swift:267` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift:437` — the shipped **Investigate** button
calls `sessions.addRunTab(...)` directly, so its `claude` process is never entered into `runStates`.
Consequences: `hasLiveRunCommand` does not see it, so quit-time graceful teardown skips it (the
process is SIGHUP'd when the surface is freed rather than stopped), and `WindowRegistry.runOwner`
cannot see it either.

Low severity in practice — the risk issue #7 guards against is an orphaned dev server holding a
port, which an interactive agent is not. Worth a separate issue, not a scope expansion here. It is
noted because revision 1 mistook it for a *precedent* to copy.

---

## Open decision

### D3 — how recent must agent history be to earn the button?

`SessionFile.savedAt` is when you quit. The question is how far from that a session file's mtime may
sit and still count.

This changed character once matching became exact (C3). A "false positive" no longer means a
misleading guess — it means *this exact directory genuinely has a resumable conversation*, which is
true information. The window's only remaining job is staleness.

- **±5 minutes** (the issue's number). Tightest link to "this pane". But Claude's mtime is the last
  *message*, not the last moment the session was alive: leave it idle at its prompt for ten minutes
  before quitting — an ordinary way to end a day — and the button never appears.
- **±12 hours.** Covers idle-then-quit and a same-day relaunch. Some directories you used earlier
  today will offer a button for a conversation you had already finished with.
- **No window at all** — offer whenever the directory has any history. Maximally useful, never a
  false negative, but the button becomes permanent furniture in every workroom you have ever run an
  agent in.

Nothing auto-resumes under any of these; the click is the gate and the picker still makes you
choose.

---

## Review log

| Review | Runs | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Self (code-grounded) | 1 | 5 corrections to the issue (C1–C5), 3 decisions surfaced |
| Codex (adversarial, read-only) | 1 | 6 accepted incl. 1 critical; 3 rejected with reasons |

**Codex findings accepted:** D2/`addRunTab` was wrong and is cut (critical — verified at
`TerminalSessions.swift:912` and `:211`); unbounded discovery IO needs hard caps; the restore
watchdog must not be gated on discovery; the T1 `claude -p` probe would spend money and mutate real
history (cut, and made moot by C3's rewrite); `consume` must be atomic against repeat clicks; the
test plan never clicked the button.

**Codex findings rejected:** cut AC 6's `--continue`/`--last` grep gate — it is the user's own
acceptance criterion and cheap. Keep the ±5 min window — its argument does not survive exact-`cwd`
matching, so the window is surfaced as D3 rather than decided. "C3 is not established by repository
code" — correct that it is not *in* the repo, but it is established by direct measurement of the
real stores, and the redesign removes the dependency entirely.

# Issue #145 — Offer to resume an agent session in a restored pane

**Status:** eng-reviewed, one open decision (D3). Revision 2 — revision 1's recommended execution
vehicle was wrong and has been cut; see the Review Log at the end.

## Context

After #46 a restored pane is inert: right workroom, right directory, dead shell. If you were
mid-conversation with Claude or Codex, that conversation still exists in the agent's own store.
#145 offers a one-click route back to it, at restore time only, spawning nothing at launch.

The issue is well specified. This plan does what the issue does not: it **corrects claims that are
wrong against the actual code and the actual agent stores**, **settles the decisions the issue left
implicit**, and sequences the work.

---
