Measured live (2026-08-09, GhosttyKit 1.2.3, issue #145 XCUITest). Writing `"claude --resume\r"`
through `ghostty_surface_text` types the command and **does not run it** — the screen dump showed it
sitting on the prompt:

```
❯ claude --resume
```

`ghostty_surface_text` is the **text input** path (it also backs `NSTextInputClient.insertText`), so
a control byte in that payload is not a keystroke. Return has to arrive as a key event:

```swift
var keyEvent = ghostty_input_key_s()
keyEvent.action = GHOSTTY_ACTION_PRESS
keyEvent.keycode = 0x24  // kVK_Return
keyEvent.mods = GHOSTTY_MODS_NONE
keyEvent.consumed_mods = GHOSTTY_MODS_NONE
keyEvent.composing = false
keyEvent.text = nil
keyEvent.unshifted_codepoint = 0x0D
_ = ghostty_surface_key(surface, keyEvent)
```

**The trap inside the fix:** `ghostty_input_key_s.keycode` is the **native macOS virtual keycode**
(libghostty does the mapping — see `buildKeyEvent`, which passes `event.keyCode` straight through).
It is NOT a `GHOSTTY_KEY_*` constant, even though `ghostty.h` defines `GHOSTTY_KEY_ENTER`. Only the
press is sent; `keyDown` never forwards a release either.

This was **unreachable by reading the repo**: nothing else puts a control byte through the text path,
because run-tab Stop signals its supervisor via a pid file rather than the terminal. It took an
end-to-end test, which is the argument for [[macapp-terminal-content-assertable-in-xcuitest]].

Lives in `GhosttySurfaceView.sendCommandLine` / `sendReturn`. Re-measure after any GhosttyKit bump.
Related: [[libghostty-drops-ctrl-tab]], [[libghostty-already-has-capture-apis]].

Merge: offer to resume an agent session in a restored pane (#145)

After #46 a restored pane is inert: right workroom, right directory, dead
shell. A restored pane whose working directory has recent agent history now
offers "Resume Claude…" / "Resume Codex…"; clicking types the agent's own
picker command into that pane and runs it. Nothing spawns at launch.

Matching is exact, never guessed: both agents record their working directory
inside the session file, so a candidate is confirmed by reading it rather than
by reconstructing Claude's directory-name slug. That removed the `.`-in-path
bug, the `/a-b/c` collision, and the case-folding and symlink hazards at once.

Three designs were evaluated and cut. `--continue` / `--last` reopen the newest
conversation for the current directory, and two agent panes in one workroom
share a directory, so both would land in the same one. A run tab is excluded
from session capture, so a resumed agent there would vanish on the next
restore. And the #49 banner is failure-shaped with one slot per tab, so an
offer and a diagnosis would evict each other.

Review found seven issues, all fixed on the branch. The one worth naming: ⌘V
does not reach `insertText` — libghostty owns the keybind and completes the
clipboard read straight into the surface — so the pristine-input guard was
bypassable and Resume's synthetic Return could execute previously pasted text.

2195 unit tests, 7/7 XCUITests, swift-format --strict clean.

Closes #145

# Issue #46 — Persist sessions (panels, layouts, windows)

## Context

Today the macOS app forgets your working layout when it quits. `TerminalSessions` is in-memory by
design (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:241-242`: "Cross-relaunch disk persistence is intentionally out
of scope"), `AppStore.workroomSplits` is "session-only" (`Core/AppStore.swift:262`), and
`window.isRestorable = false` (`Core/AppStore.swift:971`) means launch always opens exactly one blank
window. Only the sidebar selection survives (`Defaults[.sidebarSelection]`, issue #14/#70).

So a user who has arranged four workrooms across two windows — a diff pane split beside a terminal
here, a changeset pane there — rebuilds all of it by hand on every relaunch.

**Outcome:** on launch the app reopens every window that was open at quit, each with its workroom
selection, its open tabs (terminals, diffs, files, changesets) in strip order, its split trees and
ratios, its focused pane, and its frame. Terminals return as **fresh shells in their last reported
working directory** — libghostty exposes no session dump, so scrollback and running processes are
irrecoverable and this plan does not pretend otherwise.

**Confirmed product decisions:** versioned JSON file in Application Support (not a `Defaults` key);
restore **every** window that was open at quit; always on, no settings toggle.

**Ships as two PRs** (complexity gate, eng review D3). PR1 = panels in one window. PR2 = every
window. Same total scope; PR2's window-lifecycle and quit-path surface lands on a panel restore
already proven live.

---

## What is persisted

Per window: frame, `selectedTargetID`, `workroomSplits`, `expandedTerminalTargets`, whether it was
key. Per target (`TerminalTarget.ID`): the tab list in strip order, the split tree, the focused tab,
the "Terminal N" counter. Per tab: its content descriptor plus `diffViewModeOverride` /
`markdownPreviewOverride`.

**Terminal `cwd` is persisted, and it is the LAST REPORTED cwd**, not the tab's original one — that
is the whole value of restoring a terminal. (The plan previously contradicted itself here; resolved
by eng review, Codex finding 4.) What is *not* persisted is `liveTitle` / `progressActive` /
`activityPulses` — display state about a process that no longer exists. Excluding those is also what
keeps the write digest stable.

Deliberately dropped, each needing a code comment saying why:

- **Scrollback / PTY / child processes** — libghostty has no session-dump API.
- **Run tabs** — restoring one resurrects a dev server with no `AppStore.RunState` behind it, an
  untracked process orphaned on a port (the failure `WindowRegistry.runOwner(for:excluding:)` and
  issue #7 exist to prevent). `Defaults[.runCommands]` already survives and `RunConfig.autoRun` is a
  deliberate opt-in. Excluded at capture; the restore path never passes a `command:`, so even a
  leaked entry returns as a plain shell.
- **Navigation history** — entries key on tab ids, which are re-minted on restore. Deferred with a
  TODOS.md entry (below).

---

## Storage

New `Core/SessionStore.swift` — injectable file URL, `read()` / `write(_:)` /
`writeSynchronously(_:)` / `clear()`, atomic write (`Data.write(to:options:.atomic)`).

Path is **scoped by bundle id**, which is mandatory and the likeliest way to ship this broken:

```
~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/<Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier>/session.json
```

`Core/GhosttyApp.swift:217-239` already writes into `Application Support/Workroom/` from all three
identities (`Workroom`, `Workroom Dev`, `Workroom Nightly`); without the bundle-id subdirectory a Dev
run's fixture temp-dir workrooms would be restored into the release build. UserDefaults gets that
separation free — a file must buy it back.

**Create the directory explicitly.** `Data.write(.atomic)` does not create intermediate directories
(Codex finding 6). Use `FileManager.createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories: true)` on the
parent before every write, mirroring `GhosttyApp`'s config write.

Hard rule: every read and write is **best-effort**. The app behaves identically with the file absent,
empty, or unreadable. Failures log through
`Logger(subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "session")` (`GhosttyApp.swift:39`
pattern) and are never surfaced.

---

## Schema — new `Core/SessionSnapshot.swift`

Every type is a hand-written mirror. **No runtime type gains `Codable`** — `PaneLayout`,
`TerminalTab`, `SidebarID` and the descriptors are untouched.

```
SessionFile      { schemaVersion, savedAt, appVersion?, windows: [WindowSession] }
WindowSession    { windowKey, frame?, isKey, selectedTargetID?, targets: [TargetSession],
                   workroomSplits: [LayoutNode<String>], expandedTargets: [String]? }
TargetSession    { targetID, tabs: [TabSession], split: LayoutNode<String>?,
                   focusedKey?, terminalCounter? }
TabSession       { key, kind, terminal?, diff?, file?, changeset? }
LayoutNode<Leaf> { .leaf(Leaf) | .split(orientation: String, ratio: Double, first, second) }
```

Payloads: `TerminalPayload { defaultTitle, cwd? }`; `DiffPayload { path, change, source{kind,
commit?}, isPreview, viewMode? }`; `FilePayload { path, isPreview, markdownPreview? }`;
`ChangesetPayload { commitID, title, isPreview, selectedPath? }`. `change` and `viewMode` persist as
existing raw strings (`ChangedFile.Change` at `Core/WorkroomStatus.swift:97`, `DiffViewMode` at
`Core/DiffViewMode.swift:12`).

**Where the bridge lives (eng review 3B).** `TabSession` stays a separate on-disk DTO — the file
format must not be hostage to internal field names (the stored-data-contract warning on `RunConfig`,
`DefaultsKeys.swift:6-8`). But its two exhaustive switches go in the **existing MARK block beside the
`NavPayload` bridge** (`TerminalSessions.swift:124-182`), whose comment already promises the property
this preserves: *"a fifth content kind is a compile error in ONE place instead of failing silently in
several."* Two projections in two files would quietly break that.

Other notes:

- **Tabs are keyed, not index-addressed.** With lossy decoding, dropping tab 2 of 5 would silently
  re-point every later split leaf. Keys are drop-safe. Do not "simplify" this back to indices.
- **`@Lossy`** (~20 lines over an `UnkeyedDecodingContainer`, skipping elements that throw) on
  `windows`, `targets`, `tabs`, `workroomSplits`.
- `PaneLayout`'s per-split `UUID` is **not** persisted — it only addresses a divider mid-drag. Minted
  fresh on materialise.
- **`SidebarID` never becomes `Codable`.** It round-trips through the existing pure pair
  `AppStore.targetIDString(for:)` (`AppStore.swift:4253`) and `sidebarID(forTargetID:in:)`
  (`:4171`) — both `nonisolated static`, both unit-tested, and the second already resolves stale ids
  to nil. Same encoding `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` and `workroomTabOrder` already use.
- **Caps (eng review 8A):** 8 windows, **20 targets per window, 20 tabs per target**. The plan's
  original 50 × 40 permitted 16,000 view allocations on the launch path, which is not a bound.
  `log()` what was dropped when a file exceeds them — silent truncation reads as full coverage.

Two pure conversions live beside the schema:

```swift
LayoutNode.capture(_ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?) -> LayoutNode?
LayoutNode.materialize(_ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?) -> PaneLayout<L>?
```

Unresolvable leaves collapse to their sibling (`removingLeaf` semantics, `PaneLayout.swift:120`);
fewer than two survivors returns nil, enforcing "a lone leaf is not a split" (`PaneLayout.swift:18`)
at the boundary. `materialize` pushes `ratio` through `PaneRatio.sanitize` (`PaneLayout.swift:48`).

### Versioning rule — WRITE THIS IN THE FILE HEADER (eng review 5A)

**Additive changes never bump `schemaVersion`.** Adding a tab kind, or adding an optional field, is
additive. Only a breaking reshape bumps. This is what makes `@Lossy` load-bearing rather than
decorative: a Nightly build writes a fifth kind, you roll back to stable, and stable drops that one
tab while restoring everything else. Bump the version for an additive kind and the whole file is
discarded before the lossy path ever runs — deleting every user's session for no reason.

This is the same split the codebase already drew between versioning a key (`inspector.layout.v2`,
`DefaultsKeys.swift:175`) and reconciling a shape (`reconcileInspectorState`, `AppStore.swift:4209`).

**A newer schema is read-only (Codex finding 5).** If `schemaVersion` exceeds the current version,
restore nothing **and disable writes to that file for the session**. Otherwise an older build
silently destroys a newer build's session on its next save — a real risk with three side-by-side
build identities.

### Degradation

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| File missing / unreadable | No restore, no error — the fresh-install path. |
| Envelope undecodable | Move once to `session.corrupt.json` (so a bug report has something to attach), start clean. |
| `schemaVersion` newer | Restore nothing **and do not write** for this session. |
| `schemaVersion` older | Migrate, or discard if no migration exists. |
| Element in a `@Lossy` array throws | Drop that element, keep the rest. |
| Unknown `TabSession.kind` | One tab dropped at materialise; siblings restore. |
| **Valid file, zero surviving windows** | Treat as **no usable session** — fall back to `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` (Codex finding 12). Otherwise lossy recovery launches emptier than deleting the file would. |
| Target/leaf no longer resolves | Dropped; split collapses. Same self-heal as `validatedSelection` (`AppStore.swift:2571`) and `pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves` (`AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift:297`). |
| Deleted file / rebased-away commit | **Restore anyway, do not stat.** `DiffViewer` and `PlainFileViewer` already own "unavailable" states, and `refreshOpenDiffChangeKinds` (`AppStore.swift:3865`) self-heals a stale `change` off the status sweep. Pre-flighting would put N filesystem/VCS hits on the launch path for an answer that expires immediately. |
| Dead terminal `cwd` | Falls back to `target.path` (a pure static, unit-tested) — otherwise the spawn fails. |

### Structural validation (Codex finding 9)

Caps bound array *length*; they do nothing against a hostile or corrupt shape. Before materialising,
reject or repair:

- **Duplicate `windowKey` / `targetID` / tab `key`** — dictionary construction would silently
  redirect split leaves and focus to the wrong pane. Keep the first, drop the rest.
- **Split-tree depth** — cap recursion; a deeply nested tree is a stack hazard in `materialize`.
- **Total file size** — refuse above a sane ceiling before decoding.
- **String length** — clamp paths / titles / commit ids.

---

## Identity

**Tab ids are re-minted, not revived.** `TerminalTab.id` is `let id = UUID()`
(`TerminalSessions.swift:15`) and is unique *across windows*: `WindowRegistry.ownerOf(tabID:)`
(`WindowRegistry.swift:127`) routes OS-notification clicks by it. Restoring persisted UUIDs would put
a duplicate-id hazard one bug away for zero benefit. `TabSession.key` is a join key valid only within
one snapshot; restore builds a `[key: TerminalTab.ID]` map and rewires order, split and focus through
it. `TerminalTab` needs no change.

**Windows get a cross-launch identity, which they lack today.** `WindowSeed.launch`
(`WorkroomApp.swift:90`) is a computed `static var` minting a fresh UUID per access, and `RootWindow`
takes `seed ?? .launch` (`:59`). Add `AppStore.sessionKey: UUID` — the claimed session's key when a
window adopts one, else `seed.id`. That is what `WindowSession.windowKey` stores, stable thereafter.

---

## Multi-window restore

`window.isRestorable = false` (`AppStore.swift:971`) **stays**, and its comment gets the *correct*
rationale (eng review, Step 0). The built-in is real: SwiftUI's value-based `WindowGroup` restores
scene values — `WindowSeed` is `Codable` precisely for that — and it was suppressed in `642d2c01` for
one stated reason, *"Enforce single-window-on-launch"*, the product decision this issue reverses. We
still decline it, because **it is gated on a system preference that ships off**: "Close windows when
quitting an application" is checked by default (`defaults read -g NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` is unset
on a default install). Leaning on it means the feature silently does nothing for most users. Keeping
`isRestorable = false` also stops OS-restored and app-restored windows doubling up.

### Claiming (eng review 10B)

`ProjectStore` — the app-wide singleton that already owns the one-shot `consumeInitialRestore()`
(`ProjectStore.swift:84`) — gains the loaded `SessionFile` and:

```swift
func claimSession(for key: UUID, isLaunchWindow: Bool) -> WindowSession?  // idempotent by key
func pendingSessionKeys() -> [UUID]                                       // unclaimed, marked dispatched
```

**Claim in `attachWindow`, not `RootWindow.init`.** A SwiftUI view initialiser can run speculatively
or repeatedly, so a discarded init could consume a session no real window ever uses — a
nondeterministic panel-loss bug. `attachWindow` (`AppStore.swift:939`) runs from `WindowAccessor` in
`viewDidMoveToWindow`, when a real `NSWindow` exists and still **before display**, which is what the
frame needs. Claiming is also **idempotent by key** (belt and braces: a repeat call returns the same
session, never a second one).

Launch-window identity must be **explicit**, not `allStores.isEmpty` — at claim time neither window
has registered, so that check is a race. It gates `isRestoreWindow`, which gates the What's-New
auto-check (`WorkroomApp.swift:109`); get it wrong and every restored window pops the dialog.

`consumeInitialRestore()` survives as the **fallback**: with no usable session, one window still
restores `Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` exactly as today.

### Opening the siblings

After the launch window bootstraps, it opens one window per unclaimed key via
`@Environment(\.openWindow)`: `openWindow(value: WindowSeed(id: key, restore: true))`. Each sibling
claims its own session by key. Keys are marked dispatched when handed out, so a `.task` re-fire
cannot double-open. Finally the store whose session had `isKey == true` calls
`hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)`.

### Suspend saves until restore completes (Codex finding 1 — the worst bug either review found)

Restoring the launch window mutates `TerminalSessions` and `AppStore`, which marks the session dirty.
If that write lands before the siblings have registered, the coordinator snapshots only the live
stores and **overwrites the file with one window** — deleting windows 2 and 3 on the very launch that
was supposed to restore them.

Saves are therefore **suspended from the moment the file is loaded until every dispatched key has
either claimed a window or timed out**. This gate ships in **PR1**, not PR2 (Codex finding 11): the
app already supports multiple windows today, so an intermediate release must not be able to overwrite
a session it cannot fully restore.

### Frames (eng review 4A)

The session file **owns** per-window frames. `Defaults[.mainWindowFrame]` is demoted to the
cold-start fallback (first launch, no usable session). The per-window observers stop writing it once
a session exists — today they are ungated and three windows already fight over one key:

```swift
// AppStore.swift:990-999 — installed per window, no persistsSidebarPrefs gate
MainActor.assumeIsolated { Defaults[.mainWindowFrame] = NSStringFromRect(window.frame) }
```

Frame precedence in `attachWindow`: **claimed session frame → `pendingInitialWindowSize` → default**.
Mind the no-flash pre-display ordering that `642d2c01` fought for.

**Clamp restored frames to a visible screen** (Codex finding 7). `savedMainWindowFrame()` only checks
width/height > 200. A removed display or a resolution change reopens every window off-screen with no
way to reach it. Validate against `NSScreen.screens` and clamp; use one sanitizer for both paths.

### Selection (eng review 6A)

Same rule as frames: the session file's per-window `selectedTargetID` is authoritative on restore;
`Defaults[.sidebarSelection]` keeps its existing writer and is consulted only when there is no usable
session — preserving issue #14 behaviour for users upgrading into their first session-file launch.

```swift
// AppStore.swift:161-165 — the existing single-slot writer, unchanged
@Published var selectedTargetID: SidebarID? {
  didSet {
    if persistsSidebarPrefs {
      Defaults[.sidebarSelection] = Self.targetIDString(for: selectedTargetID)
    }
```

---

## Capture and write

**One writer.** A `SessionCoordinator` (or an extension on `WindowRegistry`, which already owns
cross-window concerns) rebuilds the whole `SessionFile` by asking every registered store for its
`WindowSession`. This *replaces* `persistsSidebarPrefs` arbitration for the session — that gate
exists because one `Defaults` key can't hold N windows; our file can. `persistsSidebarPrefs` keeps
governing the existing Defaults keys.

**Dirty sources.** Sink on `terminals.objectWillChange` (the `projectStoreObservation` pattern,
`AppStore.swift:824`) plus `didSet` on `workroomSplits` (`:265`), `expandedTerminalTargets` (`:271`)
and `selectedTargetID` (`:161`). Hooking the publisher rather than ~12 mutation sites means a
thirteenth mutation cannot be forgotten.

**Window lifecycle is also a dirty source (eng review 9A).** Window register / unregister / resize /
move / became-key reach *none* of the above. Without this, closing a window never schedules a save
and the closed window comes back; frames and `isKey` persist only by accident. Hook the points
`WindowRegistry` already has (`register` `:70`, `unregister` `:93`, the `didBecomeKeyNotification`
observer `:50`) plus the per-window frame observers. A window drag fires continuously, so these share
the same coalescing as the terminal sink.

**Coalescing — debounce WITH A MAX-DELAY CEILING (eng review 1A).** A plain cancel-and-replace
debounce **starves**: the publisher fires faster than 1 Hz whenever a terminal is doing anything —

```swift
// TerminalSessions.swift:262
@Published private(set) var activityPulses: [TerminalTab.ID: Int] = [:]
// TerminalSessions.swift:1100-1102
func pulsePaneActivity(_ tabID: TerminalTab.ID) { activityPulses[tabID, default: 0] += 1 }
// TerminalSessions.swift:1131 — title/cwd/progress republish
private func mutateTerminalState(...)
```

— so every publish pushes the deadline out and the write never lands while output streams. Record
when the session first went dirty and **force a write once N seconds have passed since that first
dirty mark**, regardless of ongoing chatter. `objectWillChange` fires *before* the mutation, so
capture is always scheduled, never inline.

**Change detection by equality, not hash (Codex finding 10).** Keep the previously written
`WindowSession` and compare with `==`. Swift's `hashValue` is seeded per process and a collision
would suppress a required write. `savedAt` must sit outside the comparison or it never matches.

Encoding and the write happen on a serial `.utility` queue; only the capture is main-actor.

Capture reads only through existing public queries — `activeTargetIDs` (`:401`),
`displayedTabIDs(for:)` (`:368`), `tabs(for:)` (`:382`), `split(for:)` (`:412`), `focusedTab(for:)`
(`:429`) — plus one new accessor for `counts` (`:264`), so it lives beside the schema rather than
inside `TerminalSessions`. Capturing *displayed* order is safe: display normalisation is a fixed
point, so it round-trips.

### Flush and freeze (eng review 2A, Codex finding 8)

| Hook | Location |
|---|---|
| ⌘Q, past the confirm dialog | `stopRunCommandsThenTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:576-587`), beside `registry.isTerminating = true` |
| SIGTERM (`terminate()`, `make app-run`, `pkill`, logout) | inside `MainActor.assumeIsolated` at `WorkroomApp.swift:470`, before `gracefullyStopAllWindows` |
| App backgrounded | `NSApplication.willResignActiveNotification` (debounced) |
| Fixture quit | the `UITestFixture.isActive` early return at `:549` needs the flush too, or XCUITest is nondeterministic |

**The freeze must sit past the cancel guard.** `applicationShouldTerminate` can return without
terminating:

```swift
// WorkroomApp.swift:565
guard shouldQuit else { return .terminateCancel }
// WorkroomApp.swift:580 — reached only past that guard
registry.isTerminating = true
```

Freezing above it would mean one cancelled ⌘Q silently kills session saving for the rest of the app's
life. Putting the flush and freeze beside `isTerminating` also keeps them before any window closes,
which is the property the freeze exists to protect.

**A flush must synchronously capture on the main actor and complete its atomic write before
termination continues** — routing through `flushSessions()` does not guarantee either on its own.

**Crash tolerance:** bounded by the max-delay ceiling. The design must not depend on
`applicationWillTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:619`, empty) for correctness — SIGKILL and the
documented libghostty `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` bypass it.

---

## Restore

**Terminal panes: eager models, lazy spawn — already the behaviour.** `GhosttySurfaceView.init`
(`:156`) builds an `NSView`; the PTY and Metal surface come from `createSurface()` (`:197`), reached
only from `viewDidMoveToWindow` / `ensureSurfaceCreated`. Only visible panes mount
(`WorkroomTerminalsView.contentLayout(active:)` at `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:138`,
`RootView.workroomSplitBody` at `Views/RootView.swift:645`). `AppStore.swift:2420-2423` already notes
that seeding N fixture targets *"costs N tab models and one terminal"*. **No lazy-spawn layer is
needed.** Eager is also *required*: the sidebar's terminal subtree and its restored expansion render
from those tabs.

**Where restore runs.** At the **end of `AppStore.apply(_:)`** (`AppStore.swift:2468`), after
`updateRootBranchWatches()` (`:2538`). This beats the `ensureInitialTerminal` race by construction,
not timing: a pane mounts only once `selectedTargetID` is non-nil *and* SwiftUI has rendered, which
cannot happen inside `apply`'s synchronous main-actor body. When it does mount, `tabCount != 0`, so
`ensureInitialTerminal`'s existing guard (`:2280-2297`) is a no-op. `apply` runs twice per bootstrap
(`load("none")` then `load("fast")`, `:2321-2322`), so restore clears its own pending flag on the
first call.

**The one new mutating primitive** goes inside `TerminalSessions.swift` (the four dictionaries are
`@Published private`, and it needs `setFocused(_:for:notify:)` at `:974`), under a new
`// MARK: Session restore (issue #46)`:

```swift
@discardableResult
func restore(_ session: TargetSession, for target: TerminalTarget) -> Int
```

Terminal tabs are built through the existing `makeTerminalTab(for:cwd:command:title:)` (`:1277`) —
which already takes a `title:`, so restoring "Terminal 3" adds no new construction path and every
surface callback is wired identically to a live tab. `command:` is always nil. Focus is set with
`notify: false` (the escape `reap` uses at `:1056`): a restore is not a navigation. Ends with
`reconcileOcclusion` and sets `counts[target.id] = max(persisted, built)`. No-op when the target
already has tabs.

### Launch flow

```
  session.json ──read──▶ SessionFile ──▶ ProjectStore  [SAVES SUSPENDED]
                            │
        launch window ──────┤ attachWindow: claimSession(key, isLaunch: true)
                            │      ├─▶ frame: session ▶ pendingInitialWindowSize ▶ default
                            │      │            (clamped to a visible NSScreen)
                            │      └─▶ store.pendingSessionRestore
                            │
                    bootstrap ─▶ load ─▶ apply(_:)
                            │              ├─ selection: session ▶ Defaults ▶ nil
                            │              └─ END: restoreSession()  ◀── before any pane mounts,
                            │                                            so ensureInitialTerminal
                            │                                            sees tabCount != 0
                            │
        pendingSessionKeys ─▶ openWindow(WindowSeed(id: key, restore: true)) × N
                            │      └─▶ each sibling: attachWindow ─▶ claimSession(key) ─▶ …
                            │
        all keys claimed ───┴──▶ [SAVES RESUME] ──▶ isKey window makeKeyAndOrderFront
```

### Save flow

```
  terminal publishes ─┐
  workroomSplits      ├─▶ markDirty ─▶ debounce(1s) ──────────┐
  expandedTargets     │        │                              ├─▶ capture (main actor)
  selectedTargetID    │        └─▶ max-delay ceiling ─────────┘        │
  window register/    │            (fires even under constant chatter)  ▼
   unregister/resize/ │                                          == previous?
   move/becameKey ────┘                                          ├─ yes ─▶ drop
                                                                 └─ no  ─▶ encode + atomic write

   `attachWindow` (idempotent by key), explicit launch-window identity, sibling `openWindow`
   fan-out, `isKey` refocus.

   `TerminalSessions.swift:242`, `AppStore.swift:262`, `AppStore.swift:268-270`,

## Failure modes

| New codepath | Realistic production failure | Test? | Error handling? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Save debounce | Starves under continuous output; nothing written | ✅ 1A regression | Max-delay ceiling | — (silent before fix) |
| Quit freeze | Cancelled ⌘Q freezes writes forever | ✅ 2A regression | Freeze past cancel guard | — (silent before fix) |
| Restore + save race | Launch window overwrites siblings' sessions | ✅ Codex-1 regression | Saves suspended during restore | Windows silently gone |
| Window lifecycle | Closed window resurrects; frames stale | ✅ 9A | Window events mark dirty | Wrong windows return |
| Decode | Duplicate tab key re-points a split leaf | ✅ | Uniqueness validation | Pane shows wrong content |
| Frame restore | Window reopens off-screen after display change | ✅ | Clamp to `NSScreen` | Unreachable window |
| Directory | Parent dir missing → every write fails | ✅ | `createDirectory` + log | Nothing persists, silently |
| Rollback | Older build overwrites a newer schema | ✅ | Newer version ⇒ read-only | Newer session destroyed |
| Restore content | Diff/changeset target vanished | ✅ | Existing "unavailable" states | Clear empty state |
| Terminal spawn | Persisted `cwd` deleted | ✅ | Fall back to `target.path` | Shell opens at workroom root |

**Critical gaps (no test AND no handling AND silent): 0** — every row above has both.

  new login shell. Nothing to build until the engine offers it.
- **Run-tab restore** — would orphan dev servers on ports; `RunConfig.autoRun` is the deliberate
  opt-in.
- **Cross-launch navigation history** — blocked on the tab-id remap; deferred to TODOS.md.

> This project has gstack vendored in `.claude/skills/gstack/`. Vendoring is deprecated.
> Migrate to team mode?

Options:
- A) Yes, migrate to team mode now
- B) No, I'll handle it myself

If A:
1. Run `git rm -r .claude/skills/gstack/`
2. Run `echo '.claude/skills/gstack/' >> .gitignore`
3. Run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-team-init required` (or `optional`)
4. Run `git add .claude/ .gitignore CLAUDE.md && git commit -m "chore: migrate gstack from vendored to team mode"`
5. Tell the user: "Done. Each developer now runs: `cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup --team`"

If B: say "OK, you're on your own to keep the vendored copy up to date."

eval "$(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-slug 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || true

```

If marker exists, skip.

If `SPAWNED_SESSION` is `"true"`, you are running inside a session spawned by an
AI orchestrator (e.g., OpenClaw). In spawned sessions:
- Do NOT use AskUserQuestion for interactive prompts. Auto-choose the recommended option.
- Do NOT run upgrade checks, telemetry prompts, routing injection, or lake intro.
- Focus on completing the task and reporting results via prose output.
- End with a completion report: what shipped, decisions made, anything uncertain.

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-li

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

# TODOs

> Grouped by priority, then by area. Within a group, cheaper/higher-leverage first. Each entry states
> what it is, why, how to start, what it depends on, and its priority. Completed work is summarised in
> **Recently done** at the bottom — including the traps found while doing it, which are the parts worth
> reading before touching the same code. Full write-ups for finished items live in git history.

## P1 — before GA

### Terminal *content* accessibility (macapp) — CMT-3

**What:** VoiceOver support for the terminal's *rendered text* on `GhosttySurfaceView` — accessible
value (screen text), selected text, and change notifications — so the terminal content is navigable
with assistive tech.

**Done so far:** the **UI-tree** a11y has landed (commit `f3859f9`) — `PaneTreeView` exposes each
leaf as `terminal.pane` with a label ("Terminal <title>, pane N of M"), a focused/selected trait, and
an adjustable split divider (`pane.grip`). That claim is unqualified: the one caveat raised against it
(the tab strips' glyph buttons reporting `isHittable == false`) was investigated and closed as an
XCUITest artefact — see **Recently done**. What's still missing is the *content* layer: the
libghostty surface is Metal-rendered, so its text is pixels — invisible to the accessibility system.
Today the surface view sets `role=.textArea` + a label only; it exposes **no value and no selection**,
so VoiceOver reads nothing inside the terminal. Accepted regression for the beta (CMT-3). This is also
the **enabler for content-level UI tests**: once terminal text is in the a11y tree, XCUITest can
assert on rendered output (backspace deleted, TUI drew, scrollback) on top of the now-landed fixture
seam — see `macapp/QA-libghostty.md` (Bucket 2).

**When:** feasible on the currently pinned engine today (the read APIs exist), but ghostty upstream
has merged a11y plumbing worth riding — **ghostty #12902** ("core: send selection_changed
notification", merged 2026-06-04), which on macOS posts `.ghosttySelectionDidChange` → debounced →
`NSAccessibility.selectedTextChanged`. On the pinned engine we'd have to post that notification
ourselves from our own selection events; after the pin bump it comes from the engine as
`GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED`.

This is unblocked by the **pin bump** (see "Bump the libghostty pin", P2), NOT by owning the
xcframework — an earlier version of this entry sequenced it behind CMT-2, which was wrong. A
before-GA item either way; doing it before the bump costs one self-posted notification.

**How to start (minimal-viable, keep light per D1 — crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`):**
- `accessibilityValue()` → visible screen text via `ghostty_surface_read_text(surface, <viewport
  ghostty_selection_s>, …)` (reuse the `extractString(from:)` helper).
- `accessibilitySelectedText()` → `ghostty_surface_read_selection` (the same read that powers
  copy-on-select).
- Post `NSAccessibility.post(element:notification:)` `.selectedTextChanged` on selection change
  (we already detect mouseUp / copy-on-select) and a throttled `.valueChanged` on output so
  VoiceOver follows along; keep the role/label and report focus.
- Skip the full `NSAccessibility` text protocol (line/char-range/bounds geometry) — overkill for a
  terminal, and Muxy keeps it minimal too.

**Caveat:** terminal a11y is inherently partial (dynamic output, scrollback, full-screen TUIs);
target "announce output + selection, navigable text", not a perfect document model.

**Depends on:** the read APIs already present in the pinned engine (`ghostty_surface_read_selection`,
`ghostty_surface_read_text`, `extractString`) in `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`.
Cheaper after the pin bump (engine-sent `selection_changed`), but not blocked by it.

**Priority:** P2 (accessibility regression — address before GA, not blocking the beta).

## P2 — perf, correctness, and the next VCS phase

Next up = only P1 item.

**Terminal *content* accessibility (macapp) — CMT-3** (`TODOS.md:10`)

VoiceOver reads nothing inside a terminal. Surface is Metal-rendered, so text is pixels. Today the view sets `role=.textArea` + label, no value, no selection. Accepted beta regression, listed as before-GA.

Three bullets:
1. `accessibilityValue()` = visible screen text via `readText(tag: VIEWPORT)`
2. `accessibilitySelectedText()` = `ghostty_surface_read_selection`
3. Post `.selectedTextChanged` on selection change + throttled `.valueChanged` on output

**#145 already did most of bullet 1** — `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1050` has exactly that `accessibilityValue()`, but gated behind `UITestFixture.isActive` because it was built to make terminal output assertable in XCUITest. Shipping CMT-3 = drop the fixture gate, add selection + notifications. Cheaper than the entry assumes; the entry predates that commit.

Other helpers already present: `readSelection` (`:778`), `extractString` (`:783`), `readText` (`:828`).

Not blocked. Entry notes it's cheaper after the libghostty pin bump (engine sends `SELECTION_CHANGED`), but the pin bump is explicitly post-GA, so doing it now costs one self-posted notification.

Everything below P1 is P2/P3 follow-up. Want me to plan CMT-3?

61	### Bump the libghostty pin (macapp) — post-GA, first change after the GA tag
62	
63	**What:** move `macapp/project.yml` from the currently pinned `libghostty-spm` package to **1.3.2**
64	(ghostty commit `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`). Those two numbers are this task's
65	TARGET, not a claim about what ships — for what is pinned today, read `project.yml`'s comment, which
66	is the single source of truth. Re-check the target against the packager's newest release before
67	starting; it moves.
68	
69	**Why:** it is the only way to reach `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid` + `ghostty_surface_tty_name`
70	(the "libghostty exposes no PTY child PID" limitation CMT-1 records at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:95`)
71	and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (CMT-3's a11y hook), plus ~1300 upstream commits. **It ships
72	no user-visible change by itself** — both wins need separate work to wire — which is exactly why it
73	waits for GA rather than riding under it.
74	
75	**The version trap that produced two wrong roadmap entries — read this first.** `libghostty-spm`
76	versions its **package** independently of ghostty. The release bodies state the ghostty ref
77	explicitly, and package `1.2.3` is built from ghostty **`v1.3.1`**. Reading a package version as a
78	ghostty version is what made an earlier CMT-2 claim we trailed ghostty by ~2 versions and file it as
79	P1. Package `1.3.1` ≠ ghostty `v1.3.1`. Always read `Ghostty.ref` + the release body, never the tag.
80	
81	**The real risk is the patch swap, not the API.** The packager applies its own patches to ghostty
82	before building, and `Script/apply-patches.sh` feature-probes the header to choose between them:
83	
84	```
85	  grep -q "ghostty_surface_foreground_pid" include/ghostty.h
86	      │
87	      ├── absent  (ghostty v1.3.1 — what we ship today)
88	      │     └── 0002-host-managed-io.patch          (17,588 B)
89	      │
90	      └── present (ghostty 35e1a016 — package 1.3.2)
91	            └── 0002-host-managed-io-modern.patch   (18,447 B)   ← never run here
92	                                                                    PTY/IO hosting: surface teardown,
93	                                                                    orphan shells, the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
94	                                                                    site WorkroomApp.swift:606 documents
95	```
96	
97	By contrast the mid-enum `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` insert — which renumbers 14 following
98	tags including `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` and `COMMAND_FINISHED` — is **not** a risk: header and static
99	archive ship together, `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` dispatches on symbolic labels, and
100	nothing persists a raw tag. Don't spend the retest budget there. (Don't write a test asserting a
101	tag's raw value either — test and app import the same header, so it can never fail.)
102	
103	**Blocking work, same commit:**
104	- **Regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/`** from the same ghostty ref — `terminfo/` and
105	  `shell-integration/` ONLY. See the separate entry below for why `themes/` must not be touched.
106	- **Resolve `TerminalSearch.navigationPlan`.** It both inverts direction against the engine's
107	  ordering and synthesizes wrap by emitting `total - 1` steps, keyed to the pinned engine's "stops
108	  dead at the ends" behaviour. If wrapping or match ordering moved upstream, ⌘G becomes *wrong*, not
109	  redundant.
110	
111	**Retest the IO layer, not the enum:** repeated surface create/destroy, split/close churn, workroom
112	switch/delete, the run-tab supervisor, and the `ps` orphan check. `0010-fix-scroll-remainder-zeroing.patch`
113	is also new, so include the scrollbar overlay. The XCUITest action-tag baseline (added ahead of this
114	work, deliberately against the old engine) is the pass/fail gate.
115	
116	**Also required:**
117	- **A universal Release build before landing.** CI only ever builds Debug/arm64 and `release.sh`
118	  takes `ARCHS_STANDARD`, so today the first universal link happens at release time:
119	  `VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs`, then
120	  `xcodebuild -configuration Release ARCHS="arm64 x86_64" ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO build`.
121	- **A bake gate.** `nightly.yml` builds daily from master, so this reaches nightly users ~24h after
122	  landing. Require N clean nightlies before it enters a `pre` tag.
123	- **A `QA-libghostty.md` §N "engine bump smoke"** (~12 items). Committing to the full 13-section
124	  manual walk on every bump guarantees it won't happen next time.
125	
126	**Rollback is not one line:** revert the commit(s), `rm -rf macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages`,
127	rebuild. CI's `spm-`/`xcbuild-` caches key on `project.yml` and their `restore-keys` fallback can
128	restore a mixed state. Do **not** remove any workaround (backspace DEL-as-text, ⌃Tab) until this has
129	baked — both fail safe, and the backspace test passes either way, so removal needs a raw-PTY probe.
130	
131	**Depends on:** GA shipping first. `Package.resolved` is now tracked, so the resolved revision is a
132	reviewable diff.
133	
134	**Priority:** P2 — real value, no user-visible gain on its own, and it swaps the layer that runs the
135	user's shell. First change after the GA tag, not before it.
136	
137	### Own the GhosttyKit xcframework (macapp) — CMT-2, GA-time supply-chain decision
138	
139	**What:** stop depending on the third-party `libghostty-spm` (Lakr233) package as the source of
140	truth. Build our own universal `GhosttyKit.xcframework` + version-matched resources from a ghostty
141	ref *we* pin, and point `project.yml` at it.
142	
143	**Status: demoted from P1, and re-argued.** Two of the three rationales this entry used to carry were
144	wrong, and are struck:
145	
146	- ~~"We trail ghostty by ~2 versions"~~ — a **package-vs-ghostty version confusion**; see the trap
147	  described in the pin-bump entry above. We have been on ghostty's newest *release* the whole time.
148	- ~~"Only owning the pin can reach OSC 99"~~ — **a fork cannot deliver OSC 99 either.** See the OSC 99
149	  entry under Notifications for the upstream state; the short version is that the open parser PR
150	  routes the command into an "unimplemented → discard" branch, and the pieces that would make it
151	  reach an embedder do not exist as PRs at all.
152	
153	**What survives, and it is the whole argument: supply chain.** The shipped binary is **not stock
154	ghostty**. `Patches/ghostty/` carries 11 patches (~200 KB, including a 113 KB prebuilt-framedata
155	patch and the ~18 KB host-managed-IO patch that rewrites PTY hosting), applied at build time by a
156	single maintainer. The artifact is checksummed by SPM but **not signed or notarized** — unlike
157	ghostty-org, which minisigns its own `ghostty-vt` artifacts. We link that into a notarized app, in
158	the component that runs the user's shell. Slice composition churns too: arm64e slices shipped
159	2026-07-21 and were reverted three days later, re-cutting an already-published tag.
160	
161	**And the lag concern is real — for a mechanism the old entry never identified.** The packager does
162	**not** track ghostty. `.github/workflows/build.yml` reads its ghostty commit from a hand-maintained
163	`Ghostty.ref` file (regex-validated as a 40-char sha), and the weekly cron never queries ghostty at
164	all — it bumps the package's own patch number and bails with `"main matches package tag …, skipping
165	scheduled release"` when the package repo hasn't moved. Release-tag auto-detection existed up to
166	package 1.2.9 and was **removed**. Five package releases in 17 days all shipped one engine. So when
167	ghostty ships 1.4.0, nothing pulls it until one person edits a file.
168	
169	**How to start (cheaper than a full fork — reuse the packager's tooling):** clone
170	`ghostty-org/ghostty` at the chosen ref, run the packager's build script against it, and regenerate
171	`terminfo`/`shell-integration` from that same ref. Decide deliberately which of the 11 patches to
172	carry — `0002-host-managed-io*` is load-bearing for embedding; the iOS/Catalyst ones are not ours.
173	Vendor the xcframework + a 2-file C shim, or host it as a release artifact in a separate repo's CI.
174	Zig is needed only to *build*, not to *consume*. Signing is unchanged (a static archive in the main
175	executable, no new framework to sign).
176	
177	**Depends on:** nothing in-app. Best decided once GA has shipped and the pin bump has baked, since
178	owning the pin means owning the patch decisions above.
179	
180	**Priority:** P3 — a real supply-chain posture question with no feature blocked behind it. Revisit at
181	GA, or the first time the hand-maintained `Ghostty.ref` leaves us stranded on an engine we need to
182	move off.
183	
184	### Finish the action-dispatch UI coverage (macapp) — search counters
185	
186	**What:** add the `SEARCH_TOTAL` / `SEARCH_SELECTED` case to
187	`WorkroomAppUITests/GhosttyActionDispatchUITests.swift`. The other two visible tags (`SET_TITLE`,
188	`PROGRESS_REPORT`) are covered and green; this one was attempted, hit a wall, and was parked rather
189	than left as a failing test.
190	
191	**Why:** the scrollback find bar's "n/N" counter is the only surface for those two actions, so
192	without it they have no automated detector — the same gap the rest of that file exists to close, and
193	it matters most when the engine is bumped.
194	
195	**What is already known (do not re-derive):**
196	- The bar DOES open under XCUITest from **`Edit ▸ Find…`** (`app.menuBars.menuBarItems["Edit"]
197	  .menuItems["Find…"].click()`). The menu item is `exists=true enabled=true hittable=true` while a
198	  terminal is focused — measured. `app.typeKey("f", modifierFlags: .command)` does NOT work: the
199	  focused terminal consumes the keystroke, exactly as `RunStatusUITests` documents for the Run button.
200	- Assert bar-open on the **text field** (`app.textFields.firstMatch`), NOT on the match summary:
201	  `TerminalSearchModel.matchSummary` is `""` until a needle is set, and an empty SwiftUI `Text`
202	  produces no accessibility element at all, so waiting on it waits forever while the bar is up.
203	- **The wall:** the needle never reaches the field. Both `app.typeText` and element-scoped
204	  `field.typeText` leave the summary at its empty-needle state (`""` — distinguishable from a real
205	  no-match, which renders "No results"). So `model.needle` is not being set. The field is a SwiftUI
206	  `TextField` with `.focused($fieldFocused)` and a deferred `onAppear` focus grab
207	  (`TerminalSearchBar.swift`), and `TerminalContainerView.applyFocus` yields to it — that interaction
208	  is the place to look.
209	- `terminal.search.summary` (the a11y identifier on the summary `Text`) already exists for whoever
210	  picks this up.
211	
212	**How to start:** dump the accessibility tree with the find bar open
213	(`app.debugDescription` written to a file from inside the test) and confirm what the field element
214	actually is and whether it reports keyboard focus. If SwiftUI focus proves undrivable here, the
215	fallback is to drive `TerminalSearchModel.setNeedle` through a `UITestFixture` seam and assert the
216	counter, which still exercises the two engine actions end-to-end.
217	
218	**Depends on:** nothing. `TerminalSearchTests` already covers the pure state folding, so this is
219	purely about the engine→UI leg.
220	
221	**Priority:** P3 — two of the three visible tags are covered, and the search path has unit coverage
222	for everything except the engine round-trip.
223	
224	### Regenerate the bundled ghostty resources (macapp) — blocking for the pin bump
225	
226	**What:** regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/terminfo/` and `shell-integration/` from the exact
227	ghostty ref the pinned package builds from, and record that ref in `SOURCE.md`.
228	
229	**Why:** `SOURCE.md` records the provenance as "a recent Ghostty build" — no ref, no sha. The
230	shell-integration scripts and the engine's Zig-side injection are a **coupled contract**
231	(ZDOTDIR/ENV/XDG_DATA_DIRS, `GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES`, ssh integration). `GhosttyApp.resolveResources`
232	only checks the directory exists, so if that contract moved, OSC 7 and OSC 133 degrade **silently** —
233	taking ⌘-click path resolution, tab titles, and the busy indicator with them. There is no error, no
234	log, and no test: the terminal just quietly stops reporting things.
235	
236	**Trap:** `themes/` in that directory is **ours**, not upstream's — 116 curated files (`8fd7fa19`,
237	`602b5aa3`, and the 27→58 family expansion) whose filenames `ThemeService.families` parses.
238	Regenerating it breaks theming. Scope the regeneration to `terminfo/` and `shell-integration/`.
239	Unlike those two, `themes/` records its own provenance (`themes/SOURCE.md` pins the upstream commit,
240	`themes/CHECKSUMS` pins the bytes), so refreshing it is a real diff rather than a re-vendor.
241	
242	**Watch first:** `libghostty-spm` PR #43 proposes shipping compiled terminfo + shell-integration from
243	the package itself, pointing `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR` at the package bundle. If that merges, this
244	becomes "delete our copies" instead. Open as of 2026-08-05.
245	
246	**Depends on:** the pin bump — the resources must match the engine that ships with them.
247	
248	**Priority:** P2, but only as part of the bump. Regenerating against the *current* engine separately
249	is also valid and strictly reduces risk, since today's provenance is unknown.

### Bump the libghostty pin (macapp) — post-GA, first change after the GA tag

**What:** move `macapp/project.yml` from the currently pinned `libghostty-spm` package to **1.3.2**
(ghostty commit `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`). Those two numbers are this task's
TARGET, not a claim about what ships — for what is pinned today, read `project.yml`'s comment, which
is the single source of truth. Re-check the target against the packager's newest release before
starting; it moves.

**Why:** it is the only way to reach `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid` + `ghostty_surface_tty_name`
(the "libghostty exposes no PTY child PID" limitation CMT-1 records at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:95`)
and `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` (CMT-3's a11y hook), plus ~1300 upstream commits. **It ships
no user-visible change by itself** — both wins need separate work to wire — which is exactly why it
waits for GA rather than riding under it.

**The version trap that produced two wrong roadmap entries — read this first.** `libghostty-spm`
versions its **package** independently of ghostty. The release bodies state the ghostty ref
explicitly, and package `1.2.3` is built from ghostty **`v1.3.1`**. Reading a package version as a
ghostty version is what made an earlier CMT-2 claim we trailed ghostty by ~2 versions and file it as
P1. Package `1.3.1` ≠ ghostty `v1.3.1`. Always read `Ghostty.ref` + the release body, never the tag.

**The real risk is the patch swap, not the API.** The packager applies its own patches to ghostty
before building, and `Script/apply-patches.sh` feature-probes the header to choose between them:

```
  grep -q "ghostty_surface_foreground_pid" include/ghostty.h
      │
      ├── absent  (ghostty v1.3.1 — what we ship today)
      │     └── 0002-host-managed-io.patch          (17,588 B)
      │
      └── present (ghostty 35e1a016 — package 1.3.2)
            └── 0002-host-managed-io-modern.patch   (18,447 B)   ← never run here
                                                                    PTY/IO hosting: surface teardown,
                                                                    orphan shells, the EXC_BAD_ACCESS
                                                                    site WorkroomApp.swift:606 documents
```

By contrast the mid-enum `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` insert — which renumbers 14 following
tags including `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` and `COMMAND_FINISHED` — is **not** a risk: header and static
archive ship together, `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction` dispatches on symbolic labels, and
nothing persists a raw tag. Don't spend the retest budget there. (Don't write a test asserting a
tag's raw value either — test and app import the same header, so it can never fail.)

**Blocking work, same commit:**
- **Regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/`** from the same ghostty ref — `terminfo/` and
  `shell-integration/` ONLY. See the separate entry below for why `themes/` must not be touched.
- **Resolve `TerminalSearch.navigationPlan`.** It both inverts direction against the engine's
  ordering and synthesizes wrap by emitting `total - 1` steps, keyed to the pinned engine's "stops
  dead at the ends" behaviour. If wrapping or match ordering moved upstream, ⌘G becomes *wrong*, not
  redundant.

**Retest the IO layer, not the enum:** repeated surface create/destroy, split/close churn, workroom
switch/delete, the run-tab supervisor, and the `ps` orphan check. `0010-fix-scroll-remainder-zeroing.patch`
is also new, so include the scrollbar overlay. The XCUITest action-tag baseline (added ahead of this
work, deliberately against the old engine) is the pass/fail gate.

**Also required:**
- **A universal Release build before landing.** CI only ever builds Debug/arm64 and `release.sh`
  takes `ARCHS_STANDARD`, so today the first universal link happens at release time:
  `VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal make app-vcs`, then
  `xcodebuild -configuration Release ARCHS="arm64 x86_64" ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO build`.
- **A bake gate.** `nightly.yml` builds daily from master, so this reaches nightly users ~24h after
  landing. Require N clean nightlies before it enters a `pre` tag.
- **A `QA-libghostty.md` §N "engine bump smoke"** (~12 items). Committing to the full 13-section
  manual walk on every bump guarantees it won't happen next time.

**Rollback is not one line:** revert the commit(s), `rm -rf macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages`,
rebuild. CI's `spm-`/`xcbuild-` caches key on `project.yml` and their `restore-keys` fallback can
restore a mixed state. Do **not** remove any workaround (backspace DEL-as-text, ⌃Tab) until this has
baked — both fail safe, and the backspace test passes either way, so removal needs a raw-PTY probe.

**Depends on:** GA shipping first. `Package.resolved` is now tracked, so the resolved revision is a
reviewable diff.

**Priority:** P2 — real value, no user-visible gain on its own, and it swaps the layer that runs the
user's shell. First change after the GA tag, not before it.

### Own the GhosttyKit xcframework (macapp) — CMT-2, GA-time supply-chain decision

**What:** stop depending on the third-party `libghostty-spm` (Lakr233) package as the source of
truth. Build our own universal `GhosttyKit.xcframework` + version-matched resources from a ghostty
ref *we* pin, and point `project.yml` at it.

**Status: demoted from P1, and re-argued.** Two of the three rationales this entry used to carry were
wrong, and are struck:

- ~~"We trail ghostty by ~2 versions"~~ — a **package-vs-ghostty version confusion**; see the trap
  described in the pin-bump entry above. We have been on ghostty's newest *release* the whole time.
- ~~"Only owning the pin can reach OSC 99"~~ — **a fork cannot deliver OSC 99 either.** See the OSC 99
  entry under Notifications for the upstream state; the short version is that the open parser PR
  routes the command into an "unimplemented → discard" branch, and the pieces that would make it
  reach an embedder do not exist as PRs at all.

**What survives, and it is the whole argument: supply chain.** The shipped binary is **not stock
ghostty**. `Patches/ghostty/` carries 11 patches (~200 KB, including a 113 KB prebuilt-framedata
patch and the ~18 KB host-managed-IO patch that rewrites PTY hosting), applied at build time by a
single maintainer. The artifact is checksummed by SPM but **not signed or notarized** — unlike
ghostty-org, which minisigns its own `ghostty-vt` artifacts. We link that into a notarized app, in
the component that runs the user's shell. Slice composition churns too: arm64e slices shipped
2026-07-21 and were reverted three days later, re-cutting an already-published tag.

**And the lag concern is real — for a mechanism the old entry never identified.** The packager does
**not** track ghostty. `.github/workflows/build.yml` reads its ghostty commit from a hand-maintained
`Ghostty.ref` file (regex-validated as a 40-char sha), and the weekly cron never queries ghostty at
all — it bumps the package's own patch number and bails with `"main matches package tag …, skipping
scheduled release"` when the package repo hasn't moved. Release-tag auto-detection existed up to
package 1.2.9 and was **removed**. Five package releases in 17 days all shipped one engine. So when
ghostty ships 1.4.0, nothing pulls it until one person edits a file.

**How to start (cheaper than a full fork — reuse the packager's tooling):** clone
`ghostty-org/ghostty` at the chosen ref, run the packager's build script against it, and regenerate
`terminfo`/`shell-integration` from that same ref. Decide deliberately which of the 11 patches to
carry — `0002-host-managed-io*` is load-bearing for embedding; the iOS/Catalyst ones are not ours.
Vendor the xcframework + a 2-file C shim, or host it as a release artifact in a separate repo's CI.
Zig is needed only to *build*, not to *consume*. Signing is unchanged (a static archive in the main
executable, no new framework to sign).

**Depends on:** nothing in-app. Best decided once GA has shipped and the pin bump has baked, since
owning the pin means owning the patch decisions above.

**Priority:** P3 — a real supply-chain posture question with no feature blocked behind it. Revisit at
GA, or the first time the hand-maintained `Ghostty.ref` leaves us stranded on an engine we need to
move off.

### Finish the action-dispatch UI coverage (macapp) — search counters

**What:** add the `SEARCH_TOTAL` / `SEARCH_SELECTED` case to
`WorkroomAppUITests/GhosttyActionDispatchUITests.swift`. The other two visible tags (`SET_TITLE`,
`PROGRESS_REPORT`) are covered and green; this one was attempted, hit a wall, and was parked rather
than left as a failing test.

**Why:** the scrollback find bar's "n/N" counter is the only surface for those two actions, so
without it they have no automated detector — the same gap the rest of that file exists to close, and
it matters most when the engine is bumped.

**What is already known (do not re-derive):**
- The bar DOES open under XCUITest from **`Edit ▸ Find…`** (`app.menuBars.menuBarItems["Edit"]
  .menuItems["Find…"].click()`). The menu item is `exists=true enabled=true hittable=true` while a
  terminal is focused — measured. `app.typeKey("f", modifierFlags: .command)` does NOT work: the
  focused terminal consumes the keystroke, exactly as `RunStatusUITests` documents for the Run button.
- Assert bar-open on the **text field** (`app.textFields.firstMatch`), NOT on the match summary:
  `TerminalSearchModel.matchSummary` is `""` until a needle is set, and an empty SwiftUI `Text`
  produces no accessibility element at all, so waiting on it waits forever while the bar is up.
- **The wall:** the needle never reaches the field. Both `app.typeText` and element-scoped
  `field.typeText` leave the summary at its empty-needle state (`""` — distinguishable from a real
  no-match, which renders "No results"). So `model.needle` is not being set. The field is a SwiftUI
  `TextField` with `.focused($fieldFocused)` and a deferred `onAppear` focus grab
  (`TerminalSearchBar.swift`), and `TerminalContainerView.applyFocus` yields to it — that interaction
  is the place to look.
- `terminal.search.summary` (the a11y identifier on the summary `Text`) already exists for whoever
  picks this up.

**How to start:** dump the accessibility tree with the find bar open
(`app.debugDescription` written to a file from inside the test) and confirm what the field element
actually is and whether it reports keyboard focus. If SwiftUI focus proves undrivable here, the
fallback is to drive `TerminalSearchModel.setNeedle` through a `UITestFixture` seam and assert the
counter, which still exercises the two engine actions end-to-end.

**Depends on:** nothing. `TerminalSearchTests` already covers the pure state folding, so this is
purely about the engine→UI leg.

**Priority:** P3 — two of the three visible tags are covered, and the search path has unit coverage
for everything except the engine round-trip.

### Regenerate the bundled ghostty resources (macapp) — blocking for the pin bump

**What:** regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/terminfo/` and `shell-integration/` from the exact
ghostty ref the pinned package builds from, and record that ref in `SOURCE.md`.

**Why:** `SOURCE.md` records the provenance as "a recent Ghostty build" — no ref, no sha. The
shell-integration scripts and the engine's Zig-side injection are a **coupled contract**
(ZDOTDIR/ENV/XDG_DATA_DIRS, `GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES`, ssh integration). `GhosttyApp.resolveResources`
only checks the directory exists, so if that contract moved, OSC 7 and OSC 133 degrade **silently** —
taking ⌘-click path resolution, tab titles, and the busy indicator with them. There is no error, no
log, and no test: the terminal just quietly stops reporting things.

**Trap:** `themes/` in that directory is **ours**, not upstream's — 116 curated files (`8fd7fa19`,
`602b5aa3`, and the 27→58 family expansion) whose filenames `ThemeService.families` parses.
Regenerating it breaks theming. Scope the regeneration to `terminfo/` and `shell-integration/`.
Unlike those two, `themes/` records its own provenance (`themes/SOURCE.md` pins the upstream commit,
`themes/CHECKSUMS` pins the bytes), so refreshing it is a real diff rather than a re-vendor.

**Watch first:** `libghostty-spm` PR #43 proposes shipping compiled terminfo + shell-integration from
the package itself, pointing `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR` at the package bundle. If that merges, this
becomes "delete our copies" instead. Open as of 2026-08-05.

**Depends on:** the pin bump — the resources must match the engine that ships with them.

**Priority:** P2, but only as part of the bump. Regenerating against the *current* engine separately
is also valid and strictly reduces risk, since today's provenance is unknown.

697	**What:** Patch `libghostty-spm` to add a `ghostty_surface_alt_screen_active()` export, and use it in
698	`GhosttySurfaceView.captureScrollback` in place of today's inference.
699	
700	**Why:** Session scrollback capture must not persist a TUI's screen — restoring a frozen vim or
701	Claude Code frame as dead text looks interactive and is not. The pinned libghostty offers no way to
702	ask, so capture currently *infers* it: `SURFACE` returns history normally and false while the
703	alternate screen is up, so "this pane produced scrollback before and reads false now" means a TUI.
704	That covers the normal workflow (work in a pane, then open a TUI) but **misses a pane that launches
705	a TUI before producing any output** — indistinguishable from a short session, so its frame is
706	captured.
707	
708	`ghostty_surface_mouse_captured` was measured as a candidate and is useless: false for `less`, `man`,
709	`vim` and Claude Code alike.

712	it as `self.screens.active_key == .alternate` (line ~1331), and `Surface.zig` already reaches terminal
713	state the same way for the existing API:
714

717	    self.renderer_state.mutex.lock();
718	    defer self.renderer_state.mutex.unlock();
719	    return self.io.terminal.flags.mouse_event != .none;
720	}
721	```
722	
723	An `altScreenActive()` beside it is the same four lines under the same lock, plus a C export in
724	`embedded.zig`. `libghostty-spm` already carries eight patches, and `0002-host-managed-io.patch` is
725	the worked example of adding a new `ghostty_surface_*` export. Upstream exposes nothing for this
726	today (checked the whole C API), so a pin bump alone will not deliver it.
727

729	`GhosttySurfaceView.shouldSkipViewport(hasHistoryNow:everHadScrollback:)` is the one place to
730	replace, and its unit test documents the behaviour to preserve.
731	
732	**Priority:** P3 — the inference covers the common case, and the cost of the gap is one screenful of
733	inert text, not data loss. The real price is carrying a ninth patch through every libghostty upgrade,
734	which is why this is a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight.
735	
736	**Issue #145 made the gap easier to hit.** The unprotected case is "a pane launches a TUI before

### Expose the alternate screen from libghostty (macapp) — issue #144 follow-up

**What:** Patch `libghostty-spm` to add a `ghostty_surface_alt_screen_active()` export, and use it in
`GhosttySurfaceView.captureScrollback` in place of today's inference.

**Why:** Session scrollback capture must not persist a TUI's screen — restoring a frozen vim or
Claude Code frame as dead text looks interactive and is not. The pinned libghostty offers no way to
ask, so capture currently *infers* it: `SURFACE` returns history normally and false while the
alternate screen is up, so "this pane produced scrollback before and reads false now" means a TUI.
That covers the normal workflow (work in a pane, then open a TUI) but **misses a pane that launches
a TUI before producing any output** — indistinguishable from a short session, so its frame is
captured.

`ghostty_surface_mouse_captured` was measured as a candidate and is useless: false for `less`, `man`,
`vim` and Claude Code alike.

**How to start:** feasibility is already verified against ghostty v1.3.1 source. `Terminal.zig` tracks
it as `self.screens.active_key == .alternate` (line ~1331), and `Surface.zig` already reaches terminal
state the same way for the existing API:

```zig
pub fn mouseCaptured(self: *Surface) bool {
    self.renderer_state.mutex.lock();
    defer self.renderer_state.mutex.unlock();
    return self.io.terminal.flags.mouse_event != .none;
}
```

An `altScreenActive()` beside it is the same four lines under the same lock, plus a C export in
`embedded.zig`. `libghostty-spm` already carries eight patches, and `0002-host-managed-io.patch` is
the worked example of adding a new `ghostty_surface_*` export. Upstream exposes nothing for this
today (checked the whole C API), so a pin bump alone will not deliver it.

**Depends on:** #144 landing. The call site is already isolated —
`GhosttySurfaceView.shouldSkipViewport(hasHistoryNow:everHadScrollback:)` is the one place to
replace, and its unit test documents the behaviour to preserve.

**Priority:** P3 — the inference covers the common case, and the cost of the gap is one screenful of
inert text, not data loss. The real price is carrying a ninth patch through every libghostty upgrade,
which is why this is a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight.

**Issue #145 made the gap easier to hit.** The unprotected case is "a pane launches a TUI before
producing any output", and Resume is now a one-click way to do exactly that: click *Resume Claude…*
in a freshly restored pane and Claude takes the alternate screen with nothing above it, so
`everHadScrollback` is false and the inference cannot fire. Quit from there and the captured
scrollback is Claude's frame. Still one screenful of inert text rather than data loss, so the
priority stands — but the "you have to go out of your way to hit this" part of the P3 argument no
longer holds.

744	### Resume offer doesn't know the shell is at a prompt (macapp) — issue #145 follow-up
745	
746	**What:** `AgentResumeCoordinator` publishes an offer as soon as discovery finishes, and
747	`TerminalStatusBar` enables the button whenever a surface exists. Neither establishes that the
748	restored pane's shell has actually reached its first prompt.
749	
750	**Why:** Clicking Resume writes the picker command and a synthetic Return. If a `.zshrc` is still
751	running something interactive — a `read`, a version-manager activation, an ssh key passphrase
752	prompt — that text goes to *that* program instead of the shell, and the Return answers it. Raised by
753	Codex in the #145 pre-landing review and deliberately not fixed there: the two guards that ship
754	(first keystroke drops the offer, and a pane whose cwd moved refuses to resume) cover the cases that
755	happen in practice, and the real fix needs state we don't plumb yet.
756	
757	**How to start:** the signal exists but isn't surfaced. The bundled shell integration already emits
758	OSC 7 on each prompt, which is what feeds `GhosttySurfaceView.lastKnownCwd` — so "has this pane ever
759	reported a cwd" is a usable first-prompt proxy today, and gating `TerminalStatusBar.resumable` on
760	`state?.cwd != nil` is a two-line down payment. Doing it properly means tracking prompt-start /
761	command-start as explicit state on the surface (the same shell-integration events `#49`'s
762	`command_finished` capture already rides on) and clearing the offer while a command is running.
763	
764	**Priority:** P3 — a restored pane is a fresh login shell that is normally at its prompt long before
765	a filesystem scan returns, so the window is small. It is a correctness gap rather than a hazard: the
766	worst case is one wrong line typed into a program the user can see.
